places.name: 1921 Mount Dora
places.address: 1921 Mount Dora, 142 E 4th Ave, Mt Dora, FL 32757-5584
places.description: Modern Florida cooking in a historic 1921 house, and the meal feels personal rather than formal. The kitchen leans on local farms for Spanish octopus with hazelnut romesco, wood-oven roasted oysters and a Wagyu burger, and regulars warn you to go hungry and never skip the appetizers. It is the Mount Dora splurge guests call one of their best meals ever, finished with the 1921 cheesecake made with goat cheese.

places.name: Amar Orlando
places.address: 8001 S Orange Blossom Trl, Ste #1510, Orlando, FL 32809
places.description: Lebanese cooking in a calm, intimate room just outside the Florida Mall food court, a step up from its surroundings. Guests rave about the hummus, calling it the best they have had, and the chicken shawarma and mixed grill platter carry that same care. Portions run modest, so order a spread and let the Taste of Lebanon platter do the touring.

places.name: Amare
places.address: Amare, 1255 Epcot Resorts Blvd, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: A calm Mediterranean room at the Walt Disney World Swan Reserve that feels a world away from the parks. The Ishkabubble Bread platter lands with dips and falafel that stays flavorful and moist, the kind of start tables love enough to order twice. Swordfish, scallops with couscous and Mediterranean wine flights carry the coastal thread at a relaxed, unhurried pace.

places.name: American Social
places.address: 7335 W Sand Lake Rd Ste 101, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Restaurant Row's high-energy sports lounge has screens in every sightline and a room built for game day. The kitchen treats bar food seriously: the Social Smash Burger, goat cheese croquettes, spinach artichoke dip, warm pretzels and wagyu fried rice, with a PB&J old fashioned at the bar. It runs loud when the games are on and service can stretch on busy nights, which regulars seem to count as part of the energy.

places.name: Aphrodisiaco
places.address: 8267 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: On International Drive, this low-lit speakeasy builds romance into the lighting, the music, and the plate. Guests call the ambiance breathtaking and the room velvet and theatrical, with handcrafted cocktails built to match the mood of each dish. It reads as a date night built on atmosphere first.

places.name: Bacán
places.address: Bacán, 6100 Wave Hotel Dr, Orlando, FL 32827
places.description: Inside Lake Nona's Wave Hotel, the open kitchen cooks across the Americas for a special-night-out crowd. The wagyu picanha wows steak lovers, the Florida snapper arrives in Guyanese curry, and plates like chaufa and pork belly al pastor keep the menu intentional and surprising. It is special-occasion pricing, and guests who call it pricey usually add that it was worth it.

places.name: Banh Mi Boy
places.address: 1110 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Tucked into Mills Market, this Bib Gourmand stall is no-frills, with a crisp baguette loaded with pate, cold cuts and pickled vegetables. The roast pork belly sandwich wins converts, the pho French dip is built for dunking, and the spring and summer rolls get raves. Wash it down with Vietnamese iced coffee or fresh sugarcane juice.

places.name: Banh Mi Cali
places.address: Banh Mi Cali, 5210 W Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32808-7606
places.description: An old-school, no-frills counter on West Colonial where the baguettes come out soft and crisp with pate and pickled vegetables. The grilled pork banh mi with a strong, sweet Vietnamese iced coffee is the regulars' order, and plenty make it a once a week habit. Service is brisk and to the point, and the sandwich does the talking.

places.name: Beefy King
places.address: Beefy King, 424 N Bumby Ave, Orlando, FL 32803-6028
places.description: Orlando's old-school roast beef counter, steaming since 1968 and proudly no-frills about it. The roast beef comes sliced thin and tender, piled insanely beefy onto soft steamed rolls with Beefy Spuds and horsey sauce on the side. Guests call it a true slice of old-school Americana, the kind of sandwich shop they just do not make anymore, with service that stays fast and friendly.

places.name: Black Bean Deli
places.address: 1835 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: An airy, plant-filled Mills 50 cafe where Cuban family recipes anchor the menu and regulars say it reminds them of home. The Cuban sandwich and pan con lechon come pressed and generous, the guava and cheese pastelito is flaky perfection, and the cafe con leche is strong and sweet. Parking can be tight, but guests happily drive across town for it anyway.

places.name: Blue Man Group
places.address: Blue Man Theater at ICON Park, 8390 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Three blue performers, no words, and a room full of paint drums, PVC pipe instruments, and giant balloons over the crowd. The custom theater at ICON Park keeps it loud, colorful, and interactive, the kind of all-ages chaos where guests leave saying their faces hurt from laughing.

places.name: Bombay Street Kitchen
places.address: 6215 S Orange Blossom Trl, Orlando
places.description: Street food from Mumbai, Delhi, Chennai and Bangalore is the draw at this bright, buzzy Orange Blossom Trail room with a Michelin Bib Gourmand. Guests work through pani puri, crispy kurkuri bhindi bhel and a gunpowder ghee dosa with perfectly spiced potatoes, then finish with Bombay falooda or rasmalai. The cooking is bold and fresh enough that guests say it takes them back to India, and that one visit turns into a craving for the next.

places.name: Boxi Park Lake Nona
places.address: 6877 Tavistock Lakes Blvd, Orlando, FL 32827
places.description: Shipping containers stacked into an open-air food park in Lake Nona, with a stage, a dog park, and stalls to wander. Guests graze on Claw and Order lobster rolls, Canonita tacos, and housemade burgers while a live band plays, and the music runs loud enough to end conversations. It suits families and groups who want the night outside, with event nights sometimes carrying an entry fee.

places.name: Briarpatch
places.address: Briarpatch Restaurant, 252 N Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789-3814
places.description: Park Avenue's breakfast room is chill and charming, cozy and bustling in equal measure. The Very Berry French toast gets called the best French toast ever, the Raspberry Lemon Cream Pancakes and Short Rib Benedict anchor the menu, and everything tastes homemade, down to the carrot cake and the tuna melt. Expect a crowd and a wait at peak, because Winter Park has loved this place for a long time.

places.name: Buttermilk Bakery
places.address: Buttermilk Bakery, 1198 N Orange Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789-4908
places.description: A cozy Winter Park bakery where the case fills fresh every morning and choosing just a few treats is the hard part. The ham and Gruyere croissant, the kouign amann and the tomato and cheese tart lead a lineup guests call sweet but not too sweet, with specials rotating in every week. The popular items sell out fast, so regulars plan accordingly.

places.name: Camille
places.address: Camille, 4962 New Broad St, Orlando, FL 32814-6415
places.description: Chef Tung Phan named this Baldwin Park counter for his daughter, pairing Vietnamese flavors with French forms in an intimate room. Guests describe the journey as thoughtful and well executed, with pho reimagined through wagyu tartare, plus scallops, squab, and a Dungeness crab curry tartlet among the courses that linger. The room feels welcoming and theatrical at once, creative without being gimmicky in the words of diners who have taken the full tasting.

places.name: Capa
places.address: 10100 Dream Tree Blvd, Orlando, FL 32836
places.description: Seventeen floors above the Four Seasons, this steakhouse has a Spanish accent, a wood-burning grill, and fireworks views. A5 Miyazaki Wagyu, a Wagyu flight and Iberico pork share the menu with paella, fried cauliflower with capers and a fried egg, and pork cheeks with Marcona almonds. Guests call it romantic, elegant and celebratory, ranking the meal among the top few they have had anywhere near the parks.

places.name: Casa Mezcal
places.address: 8267 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: A festive, elegant room on International Drive built around mezcal and tequila poured with conviction. Live dancers move through the room, a hidden speakeasy called Aphrodisiaco waits behind the scenes, and guests call the whole thing an elevated experience. Prices run high, and diners say the drinks and appetizers outshine the entrees, so come for the spectacle and the pours.

places.name: Cañonita
places.address: 6877 Tavistock Lakes Blvd, Orlando, FL 32827
places.description: At Boxi Park in Lake Nona, this walk-up counter serves Mexico City style street food under the string lights. Street tacos, birria nachos and chips with salsa pair with margaritas from the park bar, open-air and casual. A full-service Cañonita sibling has also opened at Lake Nona West, but this record is the taqueria: order at the counter and fold it into a Boxi Park night.

places.name: Celine Orlando
places.address: 22 S Magnolia Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Downtown on Magnolia Avenue, it stacks a Prohibition-era speakeasy, a grand main room, and a rooftop guests call their favorite in Orlando. The feel is polished casual and high-energy, moving between concerts, DJ sets and bottle service celebrations. Guests say the music is great and the vibe carries the night from floor to floor.

places.name: Charles Hosmer Morse Museum of American Art
places.address: 445 N Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Guests call this small Park Avenue museum a jewel box of Louis Comfort Tiffany, with a big impact for its size. The galleries are peaceful and serene, all leaded-glass windows, glowing lamps and iridescent glass that shifts as you move, and the Tiffany Chapel, a whole mosaic and stained glass interior, is the breathtaking centerpiece. The Daffodil Terrace and the depth of the collection make it a feast for the eyes that rewards slowing down.

places.name: Chathams Place
places.address: Chatham's Place, 7575 Dr Phillips Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819-5149
places.description: A candlelit, old-school room in Dr. Phillips where a pianist plays and anniversaries get treated like sacred occasions. Chef Tony's kitchen leans classic: lobster salad, center-cut filet, rack of lamb, and pesto Parmesan pasta twirled tableside inside a whole wheel of cheese. Guests describe it as personal, intimate, elegant, and romantic, a quiet room built for the special night rather than the scene.

places.name: Chef Mickey's
places.address: Chef Mickey's, 4600 N World Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830-8413
places.description: The Fab Five work the tables in chef costumes at this bustling character buffet in the Contemporary, with the monorail gliding overhead. Mickey waffles, cheesy potatoes, cinnamon rolls and POG juice anchor the spread, and guests admit they came for the characters and were surprised by how good the food was. It runs loud and joyful and it is not cheap, but guests call it their best option for meeting the characters without standing in a long park line.

places.name: Coro
places.address: Coro, 3022 Corrine Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-2204
places.description: An intimate Corrine Drive room where Chef Tim Lovero changes the menu with the seasons and his mood. The potato naan with whipped chicken skin butter and the tender lamb shoulder sit beside courses like corn agnolotti and beef tartare handrolls, inventive cooking that guests call novel and familiar at the same time. The open kitchen keeps the cooks within arm's reach, and the wine list leans natural.

places.name: Cowboy Curry
places.address: 1110 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Inside Mills Market, the Japanese curry is built the slow way, a 40-hour beef curry guests call comfort food with soul. Build your bowl with chicken katsu, gyu katsu or fried oyster, and finish with the Cowboy tiramisu. The room is cozy and cute, with a cup of hojicha tea as the classic sidekick.

places.name: Cups and Pups
places.address: 2413 Edgewater Dr, Orlando, FL 32804
places.description: On Edgewater Drive in College Park, this cute, cheerful coffee stop has become a neighborhood ritual. The lavender cold brew arrives balanced without extra sweetener, joined by the Honey Nut Cheerio Latte, the Brown Sugar Pop Tart Latte, and nitro cold brew. Pastries and cinnamon rolls fill the case, pup cups keep dogs in on the fun, and the dog friendly patio makes it easy to linger with your pup beside you.

places.name: Domu
places.address: 3201 Corrine Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: The East End Market original is a compact, buzzing ramen room Orlando keeps talking about. Start with the kimchi butter wings, crisp and saucy, the kind guests say they would come back for alone. Then the Richie Rich ramen, with one of the richest broths a reviewer has ever tasted, in a buzzing room where guests say the hype is real.

places.name: Dr. Phillips Center
places.address: 445 S Magnolia Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Downtown on Magnolia Avenue, this glass performing arts center anchors Orlando's cultural life, and guests praise its sound first. Steinmetz Hall delivers acoustics guests call fantastic, the Walt Disney Theater hosts Broadway tours, and Judson's Live keeps things intimate with cabaret, while film-in-concert nights put an orchestra under the movie. The one headache is getting in and out: the center has no garage of its own and valet backs up on show nights, so plan the parking before the performance.

places.name: Edoboy
places.address: 728 N Thornton Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: A standing sushi counter on Thornton Avenue, intimate and chef-led, where every piece is handed over one at a time. Let the chef run an omakase-style flow, or call your own shots with torched nigiri and the crab and toro hand rolls guests rave about. Finish with miso soup made from the day's fish bones and the matcha s'more.

places.name: El Cilantrillo
places.address: El Cilantrillo Restaurant, 1301 Florida Mall Ave, Orlando, FL 32809-7731
places.description: South Orlando's big Puerto Rican table near the Florida Mall is lively and salsa-filled, with generous portions. Guests come for mofongo relleno, a massive chuleta kan kan, arroz con gandules and tostones rellenos, with coconut mojitos that regulars rave about. Diners born on the island call it true Puerto Rican sazón, the kind of food that takes you straight back. When the room fills, the kitchen takes its time, so order a mojito and settle in.

places.name: Enzo's On the Lake
places.address: Enzo's on the Lake, 1130 S US Highway 17 92, Longwood, FL 32750-5718
places.description: On Lake Kathryn in Longwood since 1980, this old-world Italian spot feels like eating in a villa, with a deck at the water for sunset. The kitchen cooks with confidence: bucatini alla Enzo, Dover sole, ravioli della casa, and a tiramisu or blackberry panna cotta to finish. Anniversaries land here by habit, and guests say it never disappoints. On busy nights the dining room can get loud, with tables close together.

places.name: EPCOT
places.address: 200 Epcot Center Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Open since 1982, Disney's curiosity-driven park moves from futuristic pavilions to the World Showcase lagoon and its country pavilions. Guests sum it up as eating and drinking around the world, drifting from Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind and Test Track to festival booths and a violet lemonade on a relaxing stroll around the water. The mood stays festive and immersive, though headliner rides draw serious lines when festival crowds build.

places.name: Everoak Farm
places.address: Everoak Farm, 2335 Carrington Dr, Orlando, FL 32807
places.description: A family-run regenerative farm on Carrington Drive growing Certified Naturally Grown produce with no sprays in living soil. Weekly CSA boxes, pasture raised chicken, farm eggs, and small batch honey connect the farm stand to restaurant menus and home kitchens across Orlando.

places.name: Fat One's Hot Dogs & Italian Ice
places.address: 6000 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Joey Fatone's CityWalk counter serves loaded hot dogs that go well past ballpark fare. The Fat One buries a footlong under roasted pork, pepperoni, chili beans, cheddar cheese sauce, and pop fries, the Brazilian pairs grilled linguica with Calabrian honey, and the Dirty K-Pop Dog brings kimchi slaw and gochujang mayo. Guests call the results playful, messy, and a lot, with Italian ice to cool it down.

places.name: Flatlands Bar & Grill
places.address: 124 Ruby Red Place, Winter Garden, FL 34787
places.description: Upscale casual cooking in Flamingo Crossings, in a rustic room modeled on a 1920s Central Florida citrus packing house. Mini lobster rolls, Clothesline Bacon and a butterflied Cornish hen lead the menu, with an Orange Blossom Collins at the bar and a warm cookie skillet to finish. It is a neighborhood spot with a Disney area address, cooking for locals as much as visitors.

places.name: Foreigner Restaurant
places.address: Foreigner Restaurant, 2816 Corrine Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-2226
places.description: Chef Bruno Fonseca's counter on Corrine Drive is an intimate tasting room with a menu that changes month to month. Courses pair oysters with caviar, mackerel with moqueca, and picanha with morels, each introduced by the chef himself. Guests describe personal chef vibes, warm and not stuffy, with hospitality one reviewer calls a masterclass.

places.name: Four Flamingos
places.address: Four Flamingos, 1 Grand Cypress Blvd, Orlando, FL 32836
places.description: Richard Blais's tropical kitchen at the Hyatt Regency Grand Cypress centers on an open kitchen, a raw bar, and a lobster tank. The bone-in swordfish prime rib and the Tuna Tostada with passion fruit yolk chase Florida flavors, and the Key Lime in the Coconut cocktail and dulce de leche creme brulee keep the playful streak going. Guests describe a warm, family like welcome and a magical feel to the room, though a busy night can stretch the kitchen.

places.name: Francesco's Ristorante
places.address: Francesco's Ristorante, 400 S Orlando Ave, Maitland, FL 32751
places.description: In Maitland, Sicilian-rooted Italian cooking comes out of a warm open kitchen where guests feel like family. Hand rolled pastas, wood blistered Margherita pizzas, and gnocchi Siciliana lead the menu, with the grilled octopus and chicken parmigiana drawing regular praise. Guests call it the best Italian in Orlando, portions run generous enough for leftovers, and the room books out, so regulars plan ahead.

places.name: Fluffy Fluffy Dessert Cafe
places.address: 2008 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL
places.description: Japanese souffle pancakes are made the slow way here, whipped and cooked to order until each one wobbles like a cloud. The tiramisu, creme brulee and matcha white chocolate versions draw the crowds, but guests say the croffle, crisp and golden, can steal the show. Seating is limited and the pancakes take their time, so come ready to linger in the cute, airy room on East Colonial.

places.name: Gideon's Bakehouse (Disney Springs Flagship)
places.address: 1600 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: A dark, gothic, candlelit bakehouse at Disney Springs where guests line up for massive, rich cookies. The Original Chocolate Chip, Pistachio Toffee Chocolate Chip and Coffee Cake cookies anchor the case alongside cake slices and Peanut Butter Cold Brew. Guests say the cookies stay balanced rather than overly sweet, and many call the wait worth it.

faqs.q: Do you need reservations for Gideon's Bakehouse?
faqs.a: No reservations - it's a virtual queue. Expect ~2 hours on weekdays and up to ~5 on weekends. Go during Hot Cookie Hours (2-3 PM and 7-8 PM); there's a 7-cookie limit.

faqs.q: How do I skip the Gideon's line?
faqs.a: You can't skip it, but sister savory spot Six Ravens next door at The Landing usually has a much shorter wait.

places.name: Golden Hour Wine
places.address: Golden Hour Wine, 1560 Lake Baldwin Ln, Orlando, FL 32814-6661
places.description: A small, intimate natural wine shop and bar in Baldwin Park pouring responsibly farmed, small-production wines by the taste. The shelves lean toward grower Champagne, German Riesling, and alpine and island wines, with oysters, pan con tomate, and a crispy dosa to go alongside. Guests call it a hidden treasure for natural wine in Orlando, and the dog friendly patio keeps the mood easy.

places.name: Grocery Los Hermanos
places.address: 4130 Curry Ford Rd, Orlando, FL 32806
places.description: A family-run market and taqueria on Curry Ford where guests say the food tastes homemade and very fresh. Carne asada and al pastor tacos land on handmade tortillas, the birria taco combo comes with beans and guac, and aguas frescas stay ice cold. Do your shopping among the shelves first, then sit in the bright dining corner for chilaquiles, pozole, or the flan locals keep calling out.

places.name: Harlow Grove
places.address: 186 S Main St, Winter Garden, FL 34787
places.description: Beneath a century-old oak in Winter Garden, an elegant room and open-air terrace overlook town. Downstairs stays lively around cocktails like the Eden Spritz and HG Espresso Martini, while upstairs feels quieter for plates like goat cheese croquettes, short rib dip, heirloom burrata, signature ribs, and lobster lasagna. Guests return for the decor, the attentive welcome, and a setting they describe as a whole vibe.

places.name: Hillstone Winter Park
places.address: Hillstone Restaurant, 215 S Orlando Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789-3657
places.description: On Lake Killarney in Winter Park, this elegant, serene room lets the view and the sunset do the decorating. The Hawaiian ribeye comes off the grill cooked to perfection, the French dip gets called the best a guest has ever had, and the spinach and artichoke dip and key lime pie round out the regulars' order. Expect a wait for a table, since lakeside seats are the prize.

places.name: House of Blues
places.address: 1490 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: At Disney Springs, a Southern-leaning restaurant pairs with a music hall wrapped in folk art. Guests praise generous portions, from barbecue to blackened chicken with flavor they remember, and service with a smile. Families note the kids meals feel fairly priced for the area while the room keeps a fun, memory making energy.

places.name: Hunger Street Tacos
places.address: Hunger Street Tacos, 2103 W Fairbanks Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789-4507
places.description: A colorful, mural-covered corner on Fairbanks Avenue serving Mexico City style street tacos in the open air. The suadero arrives caramelized outside and juicy inside on corn tortillas, the fried avocado taco converts skeptics, and the hibiscus agua fresca is one of the tastiest versions guests have had. All the seating is outdoors, breezy and relaxed, and the brisket tacos and queso keep groups lingering.

places.name: ICON Park & The Orlando Eye
places.address: 8375 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: An open-air stretch of I-Drive with no gate to wander in, anchored by the 400-foot Orlando Eye above the night lights. Below the wheel sit the SEA LIFE ocean tunnel, Madame Tussauds, and the SlingShot, each billed separately, so the Wheel at sunset is the anchor and the rest is pick and choose. Guests call it a mix of excitement and chill, and the views over the city are the draw.

places.name: Barbarella Orlando
places.address: 2600 Lee Rd, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: A new wave dance club on Lee Road in Winter Park where the crowd from its downtown years still packs the floor. The room runs goth-friendly and free-spirited, with light-up tables, strong drinks and DJ sets built on new wave nights and Visage reunion energy. Regulars call it still the best dance spot in town, nostalgic and welcoming in equal measure.

places.name: Jaleo
places.address: Jaleo, 1482 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830-8518
places.description: A festive Spanish tapas room at Disney Springs that guests describe as a non-stop party of flavors. Wood fired paella, croquetas de pollo, gambas al ajillo, jamon iberico and patatas bravas arrive as small plates meant for sharing, with sangria and flan to finish. Diners call the cooking the most authentic Spanish food they have had outside Spain, though the small portions mean the table orders with the price in mind.

places.name: Jiang's Kitchen
places.address: 27 E Robinson St, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: A new downtown spot on East Robinson Street where soup dumplings are folded by hand in view of the dining room. The xiao long bao come filled with pork, crab or shrimp, backed by dan dan noodles, pan-fried dumplings, Taiwan popcorn chicken and a Volcano roll, with sushi and a full bar around the dumplings.

places.name: Juju
places.address: 700 Maguire Blvd, Orlando, FL
places.description: Inside a converted Pizza Hut on Maguire Boulevard, the old roofline gives nothing away, and guests love that. Inside it is a playful, Showa-era Japanese room turning out dry-aged otoro, melt in your mouth beef tongue kushiyaki and a totally addictive mentaiko udon. The kappo bar omakase is the splurge seat, while wagyu gyoza and the Susuru chashu gohan keep the izakaya side grounded.

places.name: Kabooki Sushi
places.address: Kabooki Sushi, 7705 Turkey Lake Rd, Orlando, FL 32819-5221
places.description: On Turkey Lake Road, meticulous Japanese technique meets a globe-trotting streak in a sleek room that still feels inviting. Guests rave about the hamachi crudo, the fall-off-the-bone sticky ribs and a wagyu hot plate, with ube cheesecake to close. It is special-occasion sushi, plated like art and served with real warmth.

places.name: Kabooki Sushi Downtown
places.address: 3122 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Do not let the East Colonial strip mall outside fool you; inside is a dim, upscale room regulars call a full sensory experience. The menu runs creative, from Money Bags and sticky ribs to foie gras nigiri, wagyu on a hot rock and an ube cheesecake finish. Portions run small for the price and the room gets loud when it fills, but guests keep calling it some of the best sushi in Orlando.

places.name: Kadence
places.address: 1809 Winter Park Rd, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: A tiny, minimalist counter on Winter Park Road where a Michelin-starred omakase unfolds course by course in front of you. Guests rave about the toro, the Hokkaido uni and the sake flight, calling it some of the best sushi they have ever had, in a room whose vibe stays casual despite the high-end cooking. It feels intimate and immersive, an evening to be remembered.

places.name: Kaya
places.address: 618 N Thornton Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Filipino cooking in a cozy house on Thornton Avenue that feels like grandma's house, if grandma cooked at a very high level. The menu gives classics a modern twist: oxtail kare kare, lumpiang shanghai, kinilaw and adobo risotto, with halo-halo and kalamansi pie for dessert. The team explains every dish with care, and the whole meal reads as a love letter to Filipino culture.

places.name: Kelly Park / Rock Springs Run
places.address: 400 E Kelly Park Rd, Apopka, FL 32712
places.description: The spring run is the draw here: clear, cold water from Rock Springs into a lazy channel made for tubing. Guests call it a chill, shaded piece of old Florida, well kept and easy to love, with turtles and otters along the banks. The catch is popularity: on warm weekends the park fills to capacity early, and regulars line up well ahead of the gate.

faqs.q: What time should I arrive at Kelly Park / Rock Springs?
faqs.a: Line up by 5-6:30 AM on summer weekends - the park issues ~280 morning entry vouchers and regularly hits capacity before 9 AM. Entry is $3-5 per car; bring your own tube or rent on site.

places.name: Kia Center (formerly Amway Center)
places.address: 400 W Church St, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Orlando's big room on Church Street downtown, home of the Magic and the Solar Bears, is where the city gathers loudest. Guests call game nights electric, praise the views even from the cheapest seats, and point to the towering HD video board and the art woven through the concourses. Between basketball, hockey and major touring concerts, it runs as much on big-night energy as on whoever is playing.

places.name: King Bao
places.address: 710 N Mills Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: A loud, playful hole-in-the-wall on North Mills Avenue where steamed buns come loaded and the energy stays up. The Hogzilla piles tender pork belly into a pillowy bun, the Firecracker Shrimp brings the heat, and guests round things out with elote tots and kimchi tots. Prices stay low, portions do not, and regulars will tell you one bao is never enough.

places.name: Knife & Spoon
places.address: Knife & Spoon, 4012 Central Florida Pkwy, Orlando, FL 32837-7662
places.description: The Ritz-Carlton Grande Lakes steakhouse is built on a simple split, knife for beef and spoon for seafood, in a polished room. Chef John Tesar's kitchen dry-ages its steaks until the flavor turns deep and nutty, and guests single out the tuna crudo, the crab rice, the wagyu and a kimchi spinach that steals attention from the meat. Service gets described as going above and beyond, the kind of place birthdays get entrusted to.

places.name: Kres Chophouse
places.address: Kres Chophouse, 17 Church St W, Orlando, FL 32801-3301
places.description: Out of a 1930s Church Street landmark downtown, this steakhouse stays elegant and polished with its original architecture intact. Prime steaks are aged in house and hand-cut, the Filet Wellington is the signature, and a full vegan menu runs to oysters Rockefeller and a beef Wellington of its own, with a churro waffle for dessert. Guests call the service impeccable and the wine list deep; one regular swears the filet was the best in a decade.

places.name: Kung Fu Kitchen
places.address: Kungfu Kitchen, 8466 Palm Pkwy, Orlando, FL 32836-6431
places.description: A bustling, welcoming Chinese spot on Palm Parkway where hand-pulled and knife-cut noodles land springy and fresh. The pork xiao long bao are the order guests insist you cannot leave without, backed by Shanghai pan fried pork buns, scallion pancake with sliced beef and a watermelon slush to cool things down. A wait at the host stand is part of the ritual here, and regulars say the dumplings make it worth it.

places.name: Lake Eola Park & Linton E. Allen Memorial Fountain
places.address: Lake Eola Park, 512 E Washington St, Orlando, FL 32801-1941
places.description: Downtown's lake is the city's front porch, with swans, pedal boats, a lit fountain, and a shaded loop around the shore. Guests call it peaceful and laid-back, a place to spot birds, watch the sunset reflect off the water and breathe easy in the middle of the city. Concerts at the Walt Disney Amphitheater and a farmers market guests rave about keep it feeling like Orlando's shared living room.

faqs.q: How much are the swan boats at Lake Eola, and when are they open?
faqs.a: Swan pedal boats run about $15 for 30 minutes, Tuesday-Sunday 10 AM-7 PM (closed Mondays), no reservations - first come, first served. A rainbow boat joined the fleet in June 2026.

places.name: Level 99
places.address: 1486 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: At Disney Springs, the former NBA Experience building now holds life-sized challenge rooms for games and puzzles, tracked by wristband. The hands on format feels high energy, competitive and immersive, with Detroit style pizza and drinks available when players pause. Busy periods can mean waits that cut into play time, so groups pace their rounds.

places.name: Lukes Kitchen and Bar
places.address: Luke's Kitchen and Bar, 640 Orlando Ave S, Maitland, FL 32751-5612
places.description: From the team behind Luma on Park and Prato, this Maitland spot does playful American cooking with an open kitchen and praised patio. The Cheshire pork chop over goat cheese boursin grits and the blackened fish collar are the signatures, while the fried green tomatoes keep surprising first timers. Big parties, easy celebrations, and a crowd that keeps raving about it round out the picture.

places.name: Luminescent
places.address: Luminescent, 12286 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32826-4709
places.description: A deep-green bar on East Colonial Drive, part Indian-influenced coffee bar and part craft cocktail lounge, cozy and impeccable. Pistachio, cardamom and rose water thread through both menus, from the Keral's Kulfi with pistachio cold foam and traditional chā to affogatos with real kulfi ice cream and the espresso martini. Guests come for the aesthetics and stay because the drinks live up to them.

places.name: Magic Kingdom Park
places.address: Disney's Magic Kingdom, 1180 Seven Seas Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Guests still call the first sight of Cinderella Castle down Main Street pure Disney magic, nostalgic, storybook and joyful. Space Mountain, the Haunted Mansion, Pirates of the Caribbean and the Seven Dwarfs Mine Train anchor the lands, with the Festival of Fantasy parade and fireworks over the castle tying it all together. Expect crowds and long standby waits as part of the bargain, and give the place your full attention while you are in it.

places.name: Mango's Tropical Cafe
places.address: Mango's Tropical Cafe, 8126 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819-9323
places.description: On International Drive, this is a nightclub first, with dinner and a live Latin show folded into the front of the night. The room is festive and high-energy, dancers and live music over plates like the jerk burrito and Cuba Libre braised short rib, then the floor takes over. Guests come for the music and the great vibe, and regulars advise settling table terms in advance on VIP nights.

places.name: Mecatos
places.address: 610 W Morse Blvd, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: A bright Colombian bakery cafe on Morse Boulevard in Winter Park, built around coffee from beans sourced in Colombia. Warm pan de bono, empanadas and guava pastries fill the case, and a covered patio makes lingering easy.

places.name: Mengs Kitchen
places.address: Meng's Kitchen, 2415 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-5018
places.description: Tucked into the back of iFresh Market on East Colonial, this tiny, no-frills stall cooks Southeast Asian comfort food that tastes like home. The Hainan chicken and rice combo leads, with crispy pork belly, charsiew barbecue pork, panang oxtail and five spice roasted chicken behind it. Seating is scarce, so most regulars treat it as the takeout gem it is.

places.name: Mohawk Smokehouse
places.address: 480 S Ronald Reagan Blvd, Longwood, FL 32750
places.description: Small-batch Longwood barbecue from Tyler Evans and his wife Sarah, built on Texas-style brisket with Southern roots. The brisket carries serious bark, and the table fills out with pulled pork, mac and cheese, cornbread and shrimp and grits. It works as pop-ups, events and catering rather than a walk-in dining room, so the brisket hunt runs through its social channels.

places.name: Morimoto Asia
places.address: Morimoto Asia, 1600 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: At Disney Springs, this sleek, theatrical dining room is one guests call a diamond. The pan Asian menu centers on Morimoto Peking duck, spare ribs, tableside buri-bop yellowtail and dim sum, with orange chicken and mango sticky rice rounding out the table. Diners praise flavorful, unique cooking and cheerful service, at premium prices that set high expectations.

places.name: Mosonori
places.address: Mosonori, 7541 W Sand Lake Rd, Orlando, FL 32819-5109
places.description: Chef Henry Moso's handroll bar on Sand Lake Road is a calm, minimalist counter where temaki are handed straight to you, crisp. The Moso Omakase set moves through toro, lobster and eel hand rolls, with tastings like hamachi and sides like yamaimo rounding out the counter. It feels intimate and focused, sushi stripped down to fish, rice and timing.

places.name: Nami
places.address: Nami, 6004 Artist Ave, Orlando, FL 32827
places.description: Inside Lake Nona's Wave Hotel, this serene, low-lit Japanese room is a safe haven for its regulars. Lobster donuts, tuna pizza and Nami nuggets lead a precise small-plate menu, the Earth cocktail earns its own praise, and the lamb chops draw repeat orders. Portions lean refined rather than generous, and the separate Chef's Counter tasting is the splurge version of the night.

places.name: New General
places.address: New General, 155 E New England Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789-4330
places.description: Part cafe, part modern general store just off Park Avenue, in a bright, plant-filled room with sleek polished wood. Guests come for the blueberry lavender latte and the Blue Majik latte, plus matcha and cold brew, and stay for clean-ingredient plates like the shroom avocado toast and the breakfast burrito, much of it gluten-friendly. It reads as a hidden gem: mellow, earthy and welcoming, with shelves of small-batch goods to browse while you wait.

places.name: Nile Ethiopian
places.address: Nile Ethiopian, 7048 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819-8222
places.description: Family-run since 2006, this warm, homey room on International Drive serves meals shared on spongy injera you tear and scoop. The Chef's Special layers doro wat, kitfo and sizzling beef tibs, the vegan Taste of Nile platter covers shiro, lentils and greens, and guests say every visit feels like being welcomed into someone's home. Save room for the Ethiopian coffee ceremony, which regulars call a must.

places.name: Noir Bar
places.address: 861 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801 (inside Talay Thai)
places.description: Tucked behind a hidden door inside Talay Thai on North Orange Avenue, this speakeasy stays dark, moody and blissfully uncrowded. Cocktails like the Adam and Eve and the Divine Presence arrive layered and picture-matched to the menu, with Thai-inspired skewers keeping pace. Old school R&B hums in the background, and the whole room feels built for slow conversation.

places.name: Nomikai by Sushi Saint
places.address: 8371 International Dr Ste 60, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Chef Michael Collantes brings his celebratory style to ICON Park, energetic and refined, with sushi guests call fresh and immaculate. The omakase platter anchors the table, joined by hamachi truffle potato, salmon aguachile, miso black cod and shareable showpieces like the dry-aged tomahawk and lobster noodles. Guests say you forget you are in ICON Park once you settle in, and prices run steep, so treat it as the splurge it aims to be.

places.name: Norigami
places.address: Norigami, 426 W Plant St, Winter Garden, FL 34787-3014
places.description: Inside Plant Street Market in Winter Garden, this intimate sushi counter prepares each piece right before your eyes. The omakase leans on pristine fish and careful rice, with popcorn hamachi and toro carpaccio with truffle among the standouts, and sushi served on colorful washi paper that guests fold into cranes. Guests call it the best sushi they have had since a trip to Japan, a warm and precise experience built on trusting the chefs.

places.name: Oga's Cantina
places.address: Disney's Hollywood Studios, 351 S Studio Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Inside a buzzing Batuu watering hole at Hollywood Studios, DJ R-3X spins and guests say it feels like stepping into Star Wars. The Fuzzy Tauntaun is the famous order, its foam leaving a tingle on your lips, with the Outer Rim, Bespin Fizz and Jedi Mind Trick rounding out a playful, otherworldly menu. It is loud, festive and tight on space, with most guests standing at shared tables, so book ahead and treat it as a must-do ritual for fans.

places.name: Orlando Science Center
places.address: 777 E Princeton St, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Loch Haven Park's hands-on museum is the real kind, all digging, building and touching rather than pressing buttons. KidsTown turns young visitors loose in a miniature city, DinoDigs hides fossils to dig up, and the Crosby Observatory opens the roof to the stars. The Dome wraps its giant screen around the room for a show guests call stunning and immersive. Most exhibits skew toward younger kids and garage parking adds up, but there is easily enough to fill a full day.

places.name: The Osprey
places.address: The Osprey, 4899 New Broad St, Orlando, FL 32814-6629
places.description: On New Broad Street in Baldwin Park, an open kitchen and buzzing central bar anchor coastal cooking led by the oyster bar. Guests rave about oysters on the half shell, blue crab crush puppies, whole rainbow trout, grilled octopus, and a brownie sundae they call a must. The room feels lively, airy, and romantic at once, with staff guests describe as warm, engaging, and professional.

places.name: Osteria Ester
places.address: 629 E Central Blvd, Orlando, FL
places.description: The Good Salt group brings its touch to Italian American cooking on East Central, a warm room that reads as a neighborhood red sauce joint. Guests say the house focaccia is out of this world and the lasagna comes in generous portions built for sharing, with a tableside flambeed cheese that diners keep raving about. Cozy and unpretentious, it works for date nights and family tables alike.

places.name: Otto's High Dive
places.address: 2304 E Robinson St, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: A vintage-inspired Milk District rum bar with Bib Gourmand recognition, dim and greenery-lined and built for date night. The cocktails are the star of the show, daiquiris by the pitcher and a Cuba Libre on tap, while the kitchen answers with ropa vieja, lechon asado and a shrimp cocktail guests rave about. Raw and baked oysters, cinnamon bread pudding and orange tres leches cake round out a menu with real Havana soul.

places.name: Palm Beach Meats
places.address: Palm Beach Meats, 3421 Orange Ave S, Orlando, FL 32806-6127
places.description: A butcher shop and counter on South Orange Avenue built on one obsession: Wagyu, done every way. The menu runs decadent and creative, highbrow meets lowbrow, with a Wagyu burger, an Australian Wagyu filet katsu sando, a Wagyu Philly and Wagyu tapa over garlic rice, plus a Frito Pie for good measure. The market cases stock Wagyu cuts to take home, and the beef tallow Nutella brownie earns the melt-in-your-mouth praise guests keep repeating.

places.name: Peach Valley Cafe
places.address: Peach Valley Cafe, 2849 S Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32806-5403
places.description: On South Orange Avenue in SoDo, this cute, family-friendly cafe has porch seating and plates guests describe as generous. The Orchard Fresh Apple Fritters arrive warm and shareable, while biscuits with sausage gravy bring big chunks of sausage under giant fluffy biscuits. Shrimp and grits, chicken and waffles and the Philly Steak and Egg Croissant Benedict round out a menu rooted here since 2001.

places.name: Perla's Pizza, Vinyl Records & Cocktail Bar
places.address: 959 W Fairbanks Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Thin, crackling pizza pairs with vinyl on the turntables and a cocktail bar in this Winter Park room guests keep calling a vibe. The menu goes playful: the It's Bananas pie, a truffle shuffle pie and Mikey's Hot Double Down, plus salads guests rave about and a banana pudding one called to die for. The music runs loud enough to lean in over, which suits the party energy more than a quiet catch-up.

places.name: Permanent Vacation
places.address: Permanent Vacation, 106 Lake Ave, Maitland, FL 32751-6424
places.description: Behind an Employees Only door inside the Copper Rocket, this spot trades the sports bar for dark, theatrical tiki. Skulls and bamboo, fog, and fish floats in netting set the scene, and the Pearl Necklace leads a rum heavy menu that guests say is for real. The room is small and tables sit tight, so planning ahead is part of the ritual.

places.name: Pho Hoa
places.address: Pho Hoa, 649 N Primrose Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-5016
places.description: Nobody comes for the decor at this family-style room on Primrose Drive; everybody comes for the broth. The pho bo arrives deep and fragrant, the bun bo hue carries a slow chili warmth, and the Vietnamese iced coffee lands thick and sweet. Guests call it some of the most authentic pho in Florida, and it still holds up after all these years.

places.name: Pizza Bruno
places.address: Pizza Bruno, 3990 Curry Ford Rd, Orlando, FL 32806-2702
places.description: On Curry Ford, Bruno Zacchini's wood-fired neighborhood room does blistered, naturally leavened crust and bold flavors. The garlic knots are the cult order, one diner calling them terrific, the best anywhere in town, and the Crimson Ghost and the Blanca with lemon ricotta lead a tight specialty lineup. Service runs fast, the patio hums, and a College Park second location covers the craving west of the tracks.

places.name: Prato
places.address: Prato, 124 N Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Italian the Park Avenue way: rustic yet upscale, exposed brick and warm light, house-made pastas and wood-fired pizzas. The mustard spaghettini cacio e pepe is the dish guests single out, alongside pretzel-crusted calamari and the diavolo pizza. It is popular enough that walk-ins can wait, so the long bar earns its keep while your table opens.

places.name: Raglan Road
places.address: 1640 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: A lively Irish pub at Disney Springs where live music and Irish dancers keep the room energetic. Guests return for fish and chips, shepherd's pie, chicken pie and bread pudding, calling it always a fun time. The premium prices for pub food give some regulars pause, but the energy keeps the room full.

places.name: Ramen Takagi
places.address: Ramen Takagi, 3635 Aloma Ave, Oviedo, FL 32765-6395
places.description: A small, warm, family-run ramen shop on Aloma Avenue where everything is made from scratch, with bar seats facing the kitchen. The black garlic tonkotsu leads the menu, the pork melting in the bowl, and the pan-fried gyoza carry a ginger note that reminds guests of Japan. Regulars call it the best ramen in the Orlando area.

places.name: Ravello
places.address: 10100 Dream Tree Blvd, Orlando, FL 32836
places.description: An elegant, welcoming Italian room at the Four Seasons Resort Orlando where guests say the pasta tastes like pasta in Italy. The veal ravioli is the signature, backed by house-made pastas, slow-braised meatballs, grilled branzino and wood-fired pizza layered with prosciutto di Parma and fresh burrata. Service runs attentive and friendly, and the covered terrace offers a calmer seat when the main room turns lively.

places.name: Reyes Mezcaleria
places.address: Reyes Mezcaleria, 821 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801-1014
places.description: Michoacán-born chef Wendy Lopez cooks on North Orange Avenue in a room guests describe as beautiful and alive. Lamb birria tacos, snapper tacos and Oaxaca enchiladas with mole carry the menu, the shrimp watermelon appetizer lands with a wonderful kick, and the margaritas come out spot on. A deep bench of agave spirits and Mexican wines gives the meal its second act, though portions lean refined, so order a few plates to share.

places.name: Rion's Ocean Room
places.address: Rion's Ocean Room, 3201 Corrine Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Inside East End Market, this no-frills poke counter is built on freshness, with fish cut to order and piled over rice. Guests name the Hawaiian tobiko ahi, spicy salmon, creamy garlic shrimp and wasabi furikake tuna medley, and call the quality well worth it. It is casual counter eating, the kind of place people say quietly hooks them.

places.name: Salt & the Cellar by Akira Back
places.address: Salt & the Cellar by Akira Back, 3001 Sherberth Rd, Kissimmee, FL 34747-1787
places.description: Inside the Ette Hotel in Kissimmee, this dim, polished room feels like an occasion, elegant, warm and quietly luxurious. The menu crosses steakhouse, Mediterranean and Japanese-leaning flavors, with a tuna pizza to start and a Chilean sea bass guests praise for its crispy skin and buttery center. Service draws words like fabulous, and the afternoon tea gives the room a second life beyond date night.

places.name: Seito Sushi
places.address: Seito Sushi, 4898 New Broad St, Orlando, FL 32814
places.description: On New Broad Street in Baldwin Park by Lake Baldwin, this sushi spot is dim and elegant inside, with a lakefront patio. The menu mixes classic technique with modern rolls like tuna crispy rice with smoked trout roe, the Distinguished Gentleman Roll, bluefin chutoro, and Szechuan beef dumplings. Guests say it never disappoints, calling it a favorite sushi spot in town with food that is freshly made and service that stays top notch.

places.name: Selam Ethiopian
places.address: Selam, 5494 Central Florida Pkwy, Orlando, FL 32821-8774
places.description: A warm, calm, family-run room on Central Florida Parkway serving Ethiopian and Eritrean cooking built for sharing. Wats and tibs arrive on injera you tear and scoop, with a vegetable combination platter guests call huge and richly flavored, lentil samosas, tej honey wine and a buna coffee ceremony to close. Guests who have eaten Ethiopian food for years rank it among the best they have had, and first-timers get walked through everything with patience.

places.name: Selva Rosa
places.address: 901 S Orlando Ave, Maitland, FL 32751
places.description: Mexican and Japanese cooking mash up in Maitland, with a birria sushi roll, short rib taquiza, Wagyu picanha and a matcha mojito. Guests describe a trendy, magical room with Miami vibes, and food they call superb, balanced and fresh. It is also a loud room, conversation competing with the buzz, which fits the energy.

places.name: Shin Jung
places.address: 1638 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: A cozy, lively Korean barbecue room on East Colonial where tabletop grills hiss and K-pop plays over the spread. LA kalbi and beef bulgogi come off the fire with real char, the soon tofu stew arrives bubbling, and the banchan keeps coming. Guests say it came back better than ever after the fire, though service can run brisk when the room is packed.

places.name: Shiraz Market
places.address: 188 S US Hwy 17-92, Longwood, FL 32750
places.description: Half Persian grocery, half grill counter on 17-92 in Longwood, this spot turns a spice run into lunch. Chicken koobideh and beef kebabs come off the grill tender and full of flavor, next to hummus, ghormeh sabzi, falafel and Turkish pistachio baklava, and guests say it tastes like grandma's cooking. The kebabs are made to order and take their time, which regulars treat as a chance to wander the shelves of sweets and teas like a kid in a candy store.

places.name: Six Ravens
places.address: 1600 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: At The Landing in Disney Springs, the savory companion to Gideon's serves Coffyns, hand pies in house-baked yeast rolls with storybook names. The dark, gothic and heavily themed counter also serves Tell Tale Tatties smashed potatoes and a cookie tart, in a tiny space with little seating. Early coverage calls it pricey for counter service.

places.name: Smoke & Donuts BBQ
places.address: 601 N Primrose Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Low and slow barbecue pairs with made-to-order cake donuts in this casual, family-run Milk District room. The USDA Prime brisket comes moist and tender, the Carolina pulled pork and pork belly banh mi keep the smoke honest, and then there is the Lou, a donut under bourbon maple glaze and brisket burnt ends. Guests joke that the big donut chains could never, especially with donut holes landing on the house.

places.name: Smokemade Meats + Eats
places.address: 1400 S Crystal Lake Dr, Orlando, FL 32806
places.description: Brisket is the headline at this Central Texas counter on Curry Ford West, where the menu runs on butcher paper and meats run small batch. Pitmaster Tyler Brunache works a 16-hour brisket guests call juicy, smoky, and packed with flavor, alongside salt-and-pepper pork ribs, jalapeno cheddar sausage, smoked turkey, and house-baked bread. Pinto beans and collard greens round out the tray, and popular cuts sell out, so arriving hungry pays off.

places.name: Sodough Square
places.address: Sodough Square, 419 E Michigan St, Orlando, FL 32806-4511
places.description: Detroit-style pizza from its original Michigan Street shop, all crispy, cheesy edges over pillowy soft dough. The Detroit Rob City and the cheesy garlic bread lead a playful menu that runs to a coney dog, Gochujang wings and dough dots with Nutella, and the pepperoni comes properly cupped and oily. Detroit purists note the toppings ride on top of the cheese rather than under it, a quibble everyone else is too busy eating to make.

places.name: Sorekara
places.address: Sorekara, 4979 New Broad St, Orlando, FL 32814-6414
places.description: On New Broad Street in Baldwin Park, Chef William Shen builds a tasting menu around Japan's micro seasons, moving guests through rooms. Diners describe it as not just a meal but an experience, precise and beautifully executed, with uni courses, a carrot soda welcome drink, and house made nonalcoholic pours along the way. The storytelling is intimate and transporting, the kind of night guests call a core memory.

places.name: Soseki Modern Omakase
places.address: 955 W Fairbanks Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Chef Michael Collantes' Michelin-starred omakase counter on Fairbanks Avenue is intimate, each nigiri precise, inventive and balanced. Guests call it absolute food magic: opening bites like ninoyaki with creme fraiche and onion jam, A5 Wagyu among the courses, and a tea pairing with its own following. The splurge is the point here, a special-occasion performance at the counter.

faqs.a: Book at sosekifl.com - tickets are nonrefundable, about $259 per person. Reserve far ahead; the 10-seat counter sells out.

places.name: Sparrow Orlando
places.address: 807 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: An intimate, moody wine bar on North Orange Avenue, all low light, vinyl in the air and an unhurried pace. Chef Wendy Lopez sends out southern European small plates like mushroom pate, short rib rigatoni and Dover sole, with a tomato gimlet that guests single out. It feels cozy and a little sexy, the kind of room where a date night stretches out on purpose.

places.name: Stasio's Italian Deli
places.address: 2320 E Robinson St, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: An old-school Italian deli on Robinson Street where the warm bustle and market shelves make every visit feel like a small celebration. The signature Stasio sandwich stacks deli meats and fresh mozzarella high, the chicken parm sub has devoted regulars, and portions never leave anyone hungry. Save room for a sfogliatelle with orange-scented ricotta, a cannoli or the tiramisu on the way out.

places.name: Still Lounge by Dre and Snoop
places.address: 9101 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: A low-light lounge inside Live! at Pointe Orlando, built around Dr. Dre and Snoop Dogg's Still G.I.N. Leather couches, golden light, and throwback hip hop and R&B give it what guests call a grown and sexy elegance unusual for International Drive. The bar leans into the duo's gin with drinks like the Platinum Negroni, the bourbon based OG-OF, and a lavender honey Bee's Knees.

places.name: Sushi Saint
places.address: 400 Pittman St Ste A, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Chef Michael Collantes' playful handroll bar in Creative Village has temaki built in front of you and handed over one by one. The Trinity piles otoro, uni and caviar into a single roll, the A5 wagyu hand roll goes rich with truffle mushroom jam, and an intimate omakase counter serves the devoted. Guests call the hand rolls their absolute favorite and the fish the freshest they have had, with sake-based cocktails keeping the mood light.

places.name: Taverna Opa
places.address: 9101 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: A festive, high-energy Greek taverna at Pointe Orlando where dinner turns into a celebration, napkins flying as confetti. Saganaki flames tableside, wood-fired lamb chops and branzino anchor the menu, and loukoumades and baklava finish it, with belly dancers and the Zorba line dance pulling guests in. It gets loud as the party builds, which is exactly the point, and guests call the food some of the best Greek they have had outside Greece.

places.name: Thai House
places.address: Thai House, 2117 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-4834
places.description: A small, cozy, old-school room on East Colonial, family owned and proudly unpretentious. The pad panang is rich and comforting, the duck soup has a devoted following, and the massaman curry carries real depth. Regulars call it some of the best Thai in town, and the fried banana with ice cream is how they finish.

places.name: The Beacham & The Social
places.address: 46 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: On Orange Avenue, this century-old vaudeville theater still runs on live music, balcony sightlines and LED walls, historic and electric. The sound earns the raves here, with drums hitting like cannons and acoustics guests call incredible for rock and metalcore. Drinks run pricey, as downtown goes, but the energy in the room is the real draw.

places.name: The Boathouse & Vintage Amphicars
places.address: 1620 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: A lively, classic waterfront room at Disney Springs where guests sit by the water for steaks, a raw bar, filet sliders and lobster bisque. Diners call it the best restaurant on Disney property and praise the rolls and seasoned steaks, while noting the room can get loud and prices run high. Captain guided vintage Amphicar tours splash from the dock, tying the meal to the lake.

places.name: The Glass Knife
places.address: The Glass Knife, 276 S Orlando Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: A pretty, polished Winter Park cafe named for the antique glass cake knives on its walls, all chic light and careful detail. The creme brulee donut is the signature, built on buttermilk brioche, next to a PB&J donut, avocado and egg toast, and Onyx coffee guests are glad to find. Desserts are priced like little artworks with modest portions, so come for the splurge.

places.name: The Moderne
places.address: 1241 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Mills 50's art deco cocktail room, all gold lines and tableside smoke, swanky and a little theatrical. The smoked old fashioned arrives with ceremony, the Woman in White is the signature pour, and the plates run creative, from Korean vodka pasta to duck wontons and miso cream noodles. The room feels young and vibrant, though parking nearby can be tight.

places.name: The Monroe
places.address: The Monroe, 448 N Terry Ave, Orlando, FL 32801-1894
places.description: Good Salt's midcentury room in Creative Village turns childhood favorites serious: famous fried chicken, popper deviled eggs, pork belly s'mores. Guests call the vibes immaculate and the fried chicken some of the best they have had, and the room doubles as a coffee bar and a cocktail lounge. It reads as a neighborhood gem that visitors find by word of mouth.

places.name: The Pinery
places.address: The Pinery, 295 NE Ivanhoe Blvd, Orlando, FL 32804-6434
places.description: Warm and lakeside on Lake Ivanhoe, Florida cooking in a rustic, elegant room guests call fabulous. Start with the broiled blue crab dip and bread board with pimento cheese, then move to crab stuffed salmon, smoked duck, or shrimp and grits. Truffle Parmesan fries and a Cold Brew Martini or pina colada round out a table built for lingering over the water.

places.name: The Ravenous Pig & Brewing Co.
places.address: 565 W Fairbanks Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Winter Park's chef-driven gastropub and brewery, upscale but relaxed, classy without ever going stiff. Guests come back for mushroom and Gruyere beignets, steak frites, truffle fries and pork belly, on a creative menu that keeps regulars saying you can't go wrong. Portions run small for the price, so think of it as a splurge where the cooking carries the check.

places.name: The Social
places.address: 54 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: A small brick-walled room on North Orange Avenue where indie bands play close enough to lock eyes with. Guests praise the sound, the quick bar service, and crowds that pack in shoulder to shoulder, mosh pit included. It is the kind of stage local bands measure themselves against, intimate by design.

places.name: The Strand
places.address: 807 N Mills Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: A cozy, mid-century dining room on Mills Avenue, with mom-and-pop warmth polished up a level. The kitchen cooks classic American plates with real craft: steak frites, seared duck breast, snapper cakes and a strawberry tiramisu to finish. Guests call it a true Orlando gem, the neighborhood bistro that feels special without trying hard.

places.name: The Toothsome Chocolate Emporium & Savory Feast Kitchen
places.address: The Toothsome Chocolate Emporium & Savory Feast Kitchen, 6000 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819-7611
places.description: A steampunk chocolate factory at CityWalk, all brass, gears and towering smokestacks, built on chocolate in every course. Guests go for the sweets: warm chocolate almond bread, a s'mores sundae, and milkshakes like the Marshmallow Crisp and Chocolate X5 that get photographed before they get tasted. Expect a wait to be seated at peak times; the spectacle is the point.

places.name: The Vanguard
places.address: The Vanguard, 578 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801-1341
places.description: Inside the historic Firestone Tire Building on Orange Avenue, chest-felt sound, ceiling lasers and a dance floor that packs tight on popular nights. Guests call the energy electric, and the VIP floor up top is the escape valve when the floor turns into a sweaty free for all. EDM nights and touring bands fill the calendar.

places.name: Tori Tori
places.address: 720 N Mills Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: A dark, low-lit izakaya on North Mills where the drinks are stiff and the grill stays busy. Yakitori skewers, yuzu pepper chicken wings and the blue crab and corn croquettes move from table to table, with highballs poured strong. It is walk-in only and packs out fast, so expect a line and settle in once you are through the door.

places.name: Turci Pasta
places.address: Turci Pasta, 2120 Edgewater Dr, Orlando, FL 32804
places.description: On Edgewater Drive in College Park, a cozy, romantic hole in the wall where you can watch fresh pasta made in house. The pear ravioli stands out, alongside black truffle ravioli, purple sweet potato gnocchi, and lasagna, with tableside cannoli to finish. The room feels restful and intimate, and the limoncello dessert lands light, airy, and lemony, the kind of ending guests describe as perfection.

places.name: UniGirl
places.address: 1110 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: A quick, konbini-cute onigiri stand inside Mills Market, with a Michelin Bib Gourmand to its name. Warm rice triangles with crisp nori come filled with unagi, ikura, fried chicken, mentaiko or spicy salmon, and a sesame cream puff tempts at the counter. The popular ones sell out fast, so regulars arrive with a plan.

places.name: Universal Epic Universe
places.address: 1001 Epic Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Universal's newest park still makes guests reach for the word epic, and the scale backs them up. Portals open onto five distinct worlds: the gardens and fountains of Celestial Park, the wizarding streets of the Ministry of Magic, Super Nintendo World's playable chaos, dragon country on the Isle of Berk, and the spooky monster ground of Dark Universe. Battle at the Ministry and Monsters Unchained are the rides people plan around, with Stardust Racers streaking over the hub. Go in early for the headliners and pace the middle of the day, because lines run long and the Florida sun finds the thin shade.

faqs.q: How many days do you need for Epic Universe?
faqs.a: Plan at least 2 days. Rope-drop or buy Express Pass. Consensus best rides: Harry Potter and the Battle at the Ministry, and Monsters Unchained. Power-Up Bands for Super Nintendo World run ~$45.

places.name: Universal Helios Grand Hotel
places.address: 8505 S Kirkman Rd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Universal Helios Grand Hotel rises over Epic Universe with a celestial, Mediterranean feel and a grown-up, park-view calm. Its dedicated entrance into Epic Universe is what guests call an absolute game changer, letting them slip back for a rest and return without losing the day. Flora Taverna and the Bar Helios rooftop lounge serve the dining side, park view rooms face the nighttime show, and guests say the access is worth every penny despite premium rates.

places.name: Universal Studios Florida
places.address: 6000 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: The original Universal park, open since 1990, where the movie magic feels personal, and Diagon Alley is the reason guests give most. Slip through the brick wall for a butterbeer, then ride Escape from Gringotts under the dragon, get thrown backward through Revenge of the Mummy, and pedal the night sky with E.T. Springfield keeps families laughing between the headliners, and the day closes around the lagoon. Peak crowds push the big rides past an hour, so an early start and a short must-ride list keep the day easy.

places.name: Universal's Islands of Adventure
places.address: Universal's Islands of Adventure, 6000 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Eight themed islands ring the lagoon here, and guests keep calling the coaster lineup the strongest in Orlando. Hagrid's Motorbike Adventure and the VelociCoaster are the rides people build the day around, with snow-dusted Hogsmeade and Hogwarts on one shore and the Hulk launch on another. Between headliners the park rewards wandering, drifting from Jurassic jungle to Seuss Landing's whimsy. Headliners pass an hour by midday, so ride your big one early and let the afternoon belong to the water rides.

places.name: Victoria & Albert's
places.address: Victoria & Albert's, 4401 Floridian Way, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Inside Disney's Grand Floridian, a hushed, old-world room where a Michelin-starred tasting menu turns dinner into ceremony. Guests describe personalized menus, a live harpist and courses like Miyazaki A5 wagyu, calling it a truly unforgettable, once in a lifetime experience. Reservations are famously hard to land and the bill matches the occasion, so treat it as the splurge it is.

places.name: Voodoo Doughnut
places.address: Voodoo Doughnut, 6000 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: At Universal CityWalk, pink-box spectacle and over-the-top novelty, with a revolving display of donuts guests call ridiculous. The Voodoo Doll, Bacon Maple Bar, Memphis Mafia fritter, and Portland Cream lead the case, alongside Raspberry Romeo, Oh Captain My Captain, and a vegan lineup. Lines can stretch long at busy times, and guests still call it worth the wait.

places.name: WA Sushi
places.address: Wa Sushi, 924 Semoran Blvd, Casselberry, FL 32707
places.description: A Casselberry strip plaza hides a serious sushi counter where Chef Hong flies fish in from Japan, cozy and unpretentious. Guests call it a diamond in the rough, pointing to the Grand Nigiri Moriawase with bluefin toro, A5 Miyazaki wagyu nigiri and pieces that melt in the mouth, plus an Inferno Roll for heat. Matcha tiramisu closes the meal on a quiet, precise note.

places.name: Walter's Tavern
places.address: 2105 N Orange Blossom Trl, Orlando, FL 32804
places.description: Inside the Great Southern Box Company food hall in the Packing District, a spacious, lively game day room built for lingering. Guests talk about good drinks and zero pressure, with craft cocktails, mocktails, Vodkade drinks, and a house Orange Lager on hand. You can order food hall favorites like the birria crunchwrap straight to your table and settle in with your crew.

places.name: Wekiwa Springs State Park
places.address: 1800 Wekiwa Cir, Apopka, FL 32712
places.description: The old-Florida counterpoint to the theme parks, an emerald Apopka spring feeding the Wekiva River with clear, cold water guests call magical. Canoes and kayaks drift past turtles and the occasional manatee, and trails run through dense tropical hammock. On popular days the park reaches capacity and turns cars away, so the day-pass reservation is worth sorting out before the drive.

places.name: White Wolf Cafe
places.address: White Wolf Cafe, 1829 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32804
places.description: Quaint and vintage in Ivanhoe Village, with a kitschy, eclectic jumble of light fixtures and a whimsical feel from the first plate. The jumbo cinnamon bun arrives made for splitting, warm and not overly sweet, alongside Crab Cakes Benedict, the Baton Rouge burger, and country fried chicken. It is Southern comfort served with the kind of neighborly ease guests remember.

places.name: Will's Pub & Lil Indie's
places.address: 1042 N Mills Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: On North Mills Avenue, the divey, unpretentious heart of Orlando's independent music scene. Punk, indie and metal bills pack the floor in one room while Lil Indie's pours cocktails in the other, and pinball fills the gaps between sets. Guests say it feels like home, loud and welcoming in equal measure.

places.name: Wine Bar George
places.address: 1610 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: A calm escape from the Disney Springs crowds, cozy and welcoming, with knowledgeable guidance at the table. Wines pour by the glass, bottle, or ounce, paired with The Big Board charcuterie, mac and cheese bites, pork belly, and skirt steak. Guests call it a highlight of a visit, and the flaming cheese adds a little theatre to a relaxed tasting pace.

places.name: Winter Park Scenic Boat Tour
places.address: 312 E Morse Blvd, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Running since 1938, a pontoon ride from the end of Morse Boulevard through the chain of lakes and narrow, tree-shaded canals. The skipper narrates an easygoing ride past lakeside mansions and Rollins College seen from the water, and guests call it peaceful, scenic and completely different from the theme-park circuit. Boarding is first come and sailings can fill, so arrive with a little time to spare.

places.name: Woody's Lunch Box
places.address: Woody's Lunch Box, 351 S Studio Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Toy Story Land at toy scale, playful and nostalgic in the middle of Andy's oversized lunch gear. The Totchos are the order regulars insist on, tater tots buried under chili and cheese, alongside a grilled three-cheese sandwich with tomato basil soup, a BBQ Brisket Melt and sweet Lunch Box Tarts. Seating is outdoors and scarce, so mobile ordering and a little patience are part of the ritual.

places.name: Zaru
places.address: Zaru, 1114 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-4636
places.description: A small, minimal udon room on East Colonial built around one obsession: springy Sanuki-style noodles. Guests rave about the mentaiko udon and the shrimp tempura udon, calling it the most slurpable udon they have had, with ikura onsen tamago and hojicha panna cotta rounding out the meal. It is cozy and focused, the kind of gem people make their go-to whenever they are in Orlando.

places.name: Zeytin Turkish Cuisine
places.address: Zeytin Turkish Cuisine, 4439 Edgewater Dr, Orlando, FL 32804-1229
places.description: A cozy, family-run, lantern-lit Turkish room on Edgewater Drive in College Park. The meal starts with fluffy lavash and a tray of dips, then moves to Iskender kebab, lamb doner pide, red lentil soup, and sauteed eggplant, with knafeh and baklava to finish. The small, unpretentious dining room fills quickly, and the hospitality makes first timers feel like regulars.

places.name: Ômo by Jônt
places.address: Omo by Jont, 115 E Lyman Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789-4311
places.description: Winter Park's Michelin-starred splurge, a tasting menu staged as a journey through a series of intimate rooms. The evening moves from welcome drinks in the Salon to the chef's counter facing the open kitchen, then on to a pastry parlor for dessert. French technique meets Japanese soul in courses like snow crab chawanmushi crowned with kaluga caviar and uni, and a hazelnut kakigori that lands in Ferrero Rocher territory. Guests call it unforgettable and one of a kind, with service they describe as impeccable.

places.name: June
places.address: 700 E Washington St, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: June glows golden in Thornton Park, a rustic, romantic room cooking contemporary Mexican and Yucatecan food over wood fire. The cornbread with agave butter is the dish guests joke about wanting as a last meal, backed by chicken al pastor, esquites and a wagyu tostada built for sharing. Watermelon fresco and peppery cocktails keep pace, though plates run small at fine-dining prices, so order for the table.

places.name: Mamazzita Gastrobar
places.address: 1949 W Sand Lake Rd, Orlando, FL 32809
places.description: A Latin fusion gastrobar on Sand Lake Road where a Peruvian-leaning kitchen and sushi share the table with full nightclub energy. Ceviche Erotismo, a wagyu burger, the La Reina roll and a crispy fried whole fish anchor the food, while DJs and hookah carry the room. Guests call it a vibe and praise the atmosphere, with one honest caveat: the music runs loud enough to lean in across the table.

places.name: Kai Kai BBQ & Dumplings
places.address: Mills Market, 1110 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: A no-frills Cantonese barbecue counter inside Mills Market, Chinatown-style and fast-moving. Glistening roast duck, crackling crispy pork and honey glazed char siu hang ready to be chopped into rice boxes or tucked into a roast duck bao, with handmade dumplings steaming alongside. Portions are generous, prices stay low, and guests leave happy and satisfied.

places.name: Kappo Sushi
places.address: 11815 Glass House Lane, Orlando, FL 32836
places.description: A serene, chef-led counter in O-Town West where the omakase unfolds course by course, refined and tranquil. Guests praise absolutely beautiful food: Norigami nigiri, tuna carpaccio, pork belly and clay pot rice donabe, finished with a Taiwanese-style shaved ice dessert. The room stays intimate and focused, a calm special-occasion sushi experience guests call well priced for the quality.

places.name: Sushi Izuki
places.address: 8685 Fenton St #150, Orlando, FL 32836
places.description: A small, calm counter on Fenton Street where Chef Leo's omakase has regulars calling it their favorite in Orlando. The fish is dry-aged in house and cut to order, moving through otoro, uni, A5 wagyu and miso black cod to a matcha pudding finish, every piece better than the next in guests' telling. The room feels personal and refined, more quiet ritual than theater.

places.name: Moon Wok Kitchen & Lounge
places.address: 11701 International Dr Ste 300, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: International Drive has plenty of Chinese takeout, but this one has a moonlit lounge attached, all glow and dressed-up energy. The kitchen backs up the room: handcrafted dim sum, Cantonese roast duck, char siu with crispy pork fried rice, and wok-fired beef ho fun. Guests single out the General Tso's and the honey shrimp, and the cocktails lean into the menu's flavors. It is a Chinese dinner you can dress for, built for date night on the corridor.

places.name: Mochiry
places.address: 20 S Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: On South Orange Avenue downtown, Mochiry serves Korean-style mochi doughnuts with the springy, stretchy chew that sets them apart. Bubble-ring shapes come glazed and topped in rotating flavors, with boba teas and specialty coffees alongside. Korean corn dogs and ramen round out the counter for anyone who wants savory with their sweet.

places.name: Beef Bae
places.address: 10249 S John Young Pkwy Ste 109, Orlando, FL 32837
places.description: Formerly Charcoal Zyka, this South Orlando spot runs American barbecue through a Zabiha halal kitchen, and regulars say it works. Guests praise the beef short ribs for their tenderness, the ribs fall off the bone, and the Portuguese chicken has been the hallmark since the start. An Inferno Burger brings the heat, and a mango lassi cools it back down.

places.name: Pierogi One
places.address: 8865 Commodity Cir, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: A cozy, family-run Polish bistro on Commodity Circle where pierogi taste, as one guest put it, just like great-grandmother used to make. Varieties run from mushroom and sauerkraut to Philly cheesesteak, with vanilla cheese pierogi for dessert, plus potato pancakes, red borscht, kielbasa and a full Polish platter. The room is homey and welcoming, comfort food with genuine heritage in every folded edge.

places.name: Taffer's Tavern
places.address: Pointe Orlando, 9101 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Jon Taffer's old-world tavern warmth comes to Pointe Orlando, cozy and lively with a sports-bar hum. The menu stays tight and top shelf: a Bourbon Burger, pork belly skewers, a giant pretzel with Guinness mustard, and drinks like the Campfire and the Smoffee martini built on browned butter bourbon. Guests praise the attention to the little details, even if service can take its time once the room fills.

places.name: Great Southern Box Co. Food Hall & Bar
places.address: The Great Southern Box Company, 2105 N Orange Blossom Trl, Orlando, FL 32804
places.description: On North Orange Blossom Trail, a historic citrus crate warehouse in the Packing District turned lively, group-friendly hall of counters. Guests move between Antica wood fired pizza, birria tacos, Braza Brazilian steak plates, Kayos jerk chicken and oxtail, beef shawarma, poke bowls, and A Lo Cubano pressed sandwiches. The room runs lively and modern, with a beautiful atmosphere, a dog friendly patio, and plenty of variety for groups who cannot agree on one menu.

places.name: Austin's Coffee
places.address: 2240 W Fairbanks Ave, Winter Park, FL
places.description: Winter Park's bohemian living room, an artsy, community-driven cafe now in a bigger room on West Fairbanks Avenue. Guests fill it for open mic and jazz nights, house-roasted coffee, a Yak frozen coffee and mile high peanut butter pie. It is laid-back and welcoming, the kind of place regulars describe as keeping the same soul, just with more space to hold it.

places.name: CFS Coffee
places.address: CFS Coffee, 430 W New England Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789-4230
places.description: Short for Coffee for the Soul, a Colombian-hearted cafe on New England Avenue with a cozy room and a comfy sofa corner.
