The dulce de leche cappuccino leads, beside pan de bono, a Caribbean arepa guests treat themselves to, and smoothie bowls. People settle in to study, work and linger, calling it a cute, tranquil spot to meet up.

places.name: SEO Basilico Pizzeria
places.address: 12107 Stoneybrook W Pkwy Suite 105, Winter Garden, FL 34787
places.description: In Winter Garden's Stoneybrook area, artigianale pizza rooted in Sao Paulo Italian tradition, with founders from Mooca shaping the menu. Pies run from Italian classics like margherita with fresh basil and fior di latte to Brazilian staples like Frango e Catupiry and Calabresa, with blistered, leopard spotted crusts from patiently fermented dough.

places.name: Play Street Museum
places.address: 12107 Stoneybrook West Pkwy, STE 104, Winter Garden, FL 34787
places.description: A tiny town built for young children in Winter Garden, with a doctor's office, fire station, pet rescue and make-believe ice cream. Sessions add hands on extras like a slime lab and paint your own pottery, keeping the space fresh and age right. Local first time owners run it with obvious care, a fit for birthday parties and rainy day outings in west Orange County.

places.name: Boca Kitchen Bar Market
places.address: 358 N Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Park Avenue cooking built around what Florida farms deliver, a farm-to-table menu of handcrafted plates that shifts with the market. Guests return for sweet potato gnocchi, fried green tomatoes, the apple brie flatbread and a hibiscus martini they call the perfect start to a weekend. The room runs vibrant and warm, and the main dining room can get loud when it fills.

places.name: Bosphorous Turkish Cuisine
places.address: 108 S Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: A family-owned Turkish table on Park Avenue, warm and celebratory, where hollow lavas bread arrives puffed and blistered for the dips. Guests praise perfectly cooked lamb adana and shish kabob, lamb shank, and portions generous enough to box up for days, with kunefe to finish. Indoors it can get loud at full tilt, part of the festive noise of the room.

places.name: Pannullo's Italian Restaurant
places.address: 216 S Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: The old-school Park Avenue Italian room regulars call a longtime fave, cozy and unpretentious, with a view across Central Park. The lobster ravioli draws raves, the chicken marsala and shrimp pizziola keep the menu grounded in generous, family-style plates, and Chef Pannullo's fresh cheesecake closes the meal. Guests call it the best deal on Park Avenue, which on this street is saying something.

places.name: The Chapman
places.address: 500 S Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: On Park Avenue, the warm, artful dining room Winter Park kept asking for, built on a scratch kitchen and Florida ingredients. Start with the pull-apart rolls and whipped seasoned butter, then the lamb chops and crab cakes that diners keep naming as favorites. Guests call the flavors elevated Florida and the feel cozy-upscale, special-occasion polish with a neighborhood soul. The room can hum at peak, so ask for a quieter corner if conversation is the point.

places.name: Atlantic Beer & Oyster
places.address: 358 N Park Ave Ste B, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Tucked into the Hidden Garden just off Park Avenue, a cozy, laid-back oyster bar guests call hard to find and worth the search. Grilled oysters on the half shell lead a menu built on smoked fish dip, shrimp and fish ceviche, and a lobster roll regulars swear by. It stays small and intimate, the kind of tucked-away spot guests happily call a hidden gem.

places.name: The Alfond Inn
places.address: 300 E New England Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Staying here feels like staying inside a small contemporary art museum, elegant and art-filled yet relaxed rather than stiff. Guests linger over the pool terrace, the spa, and meals at Hamilton's Kitchen, then wander halls that feel more like a private gallery. Every stay supports scholarships at nearby Rollins College, which gives the polish a purpose guests genuinely appreciate.

places.name: Casa Feliz Historic Home Museum
places.address: 656 N Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: A storybook Spanish revival farmhouse on Park Avenue, romantic and intimate, the kind of historic home guests say they could happily live in. Docent-led tours walk you through the Andalusian architecture and the home's history with guides guests call enthusiastic and knowledgeable. The Music at the Casa concerts fill the main rooms with live music, keeping the house a gathering place.

places.name: Albin Polasek Museum & Sculpture Gardens
places.address: 633 Osceola Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: A sculptor's historic home paired with serene, lakeside sculpture gardens in Winter Park. Guests stroll tropical gardens overlooking the lake, take in the statues and paintings inside the house Polasek built, and call the history and art breathtaking. It is a peaceful, charming stop, the kind of hidden gem visitors describe as one of their favorite museums.

places.name: Mead Botanical Garden
places.address: 1300 S Denning Dr, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Winter Park's wilder, shadier green space, peaceful and a little untamed. Boardwalks and nature trails wind past ponds and water, with a butterfly garden, gopher tortoises, and a hidden amphitheater turning up along the way. Guests come to relax and unwind, spread a picnic, and say they spot something new on every visit.

places.name: Winter Park History Museum
places.address: 200 W New England Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Inside its historic railroad depot, a small, charming museum telling Winter Park's story, run with obvious care. Changing exhibits, including displays of vintage Winter Park postcards, pack local history into a quick stop guests call surprisingly meaningful. It also anchors a free self-guided walking tour of historic sites around town.

places.name: Rusteak
places.address: 101 S Eola Dr, Suite 103, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: On the Lake Eola corner in Thornton Park, a neighborhood spot cooking like it has something to prove, polished, relaxed but never stiff. The New American menu runs from honey-sage pecan chicken and a pepper-crusted NY strip to steak frites and the crab cake benedict regulars order on repeat. The patio hums, the smoked watermelon margarita has its fans, and the espresso martini gets called the best some guests have had. When the room fills it gets loud and service stretches, so the early seating is the relaxed version.

places.name: The Guesthouse
places.address: 1321 N Mills Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Mills 50's plant-filled living room, greenery trailing over white walls around a square bar. Sunlight floods the big windows early; later the room goes candlelit and cozy, full of lively conversation. The bartenders build the classics with conviction, a Tom Collins one guest called the best she had ever had, plus margaritas, a passionfruit margarita, and a proper army navy. On busy nights, Fridays especially, it packs wall to wall, so weeknights are the version the regulars fell for.

places.name: Fixtion Restaurant & Bar
places.address: 15 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: On Orange Avenue, comfort food and huge comfy booths early, club energy after dark, shape-shifting through the day. The menu leans playful, with a Wall Street turkey club, chimichurri skirt steak, truffle fries, and an espresso martini regulars swear by. Game days run on the giant screen, and later the room turns to DJs and bottle service without losing its chill. Service can crawl when it fills, so settle in and order with patience.

places.name: Wall Street Plaza
places.address: 25 Wall St, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: One downtown block holds the whole crawl: eight bars and patios that, on a big night, turn into a single street party. Wall Street Plaza is a bar-crawl sprawl with the Cantina pouring its house margarita, country spinning at Rodeo, and quieter corners like the Hen House between the stages. Guests come for the outdoor block-party energy, cold beer, and drinks priced right, and a group with mixed tastes never has to leave the block. Event nights can carry a cover, so check before you commit the crew.

places.name: Iron Cow
places.address: 2438 E Robinson St, Suite A, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Part hi-fi sushi lounge, part underground club, the Milk District's good contradiction. The kitchen sends out Dynamite and Godzilla rolls and full sushi boats while the sound system does the other half of the work. Then the decks take over: trance nights, drum and bass tour stops, house till late, with good food, good people, and live music sharing the same table. On packed show nights the bar runs thin, so order in rounds and let the music carry it.

places.name: Baires Grill
places.address: 8050 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: The parrilla decides everything at this Argentine steakhouse just off International Drive. Baires Grill serves hand cut steaks and a mixed Parrilla Criolla loaded with sausage, blood sausage, picanha and asado de tira, plus sizzling provoleta. Fried empanadas start the meal, flan with dulce de leche finishes it, and a proper Malbec belongs between those courses. The pitch is great food and good times, delivered through the grill. You taste Argentina most clearly in the mixed grill shared across the table.

places.name: Evermore Orlando Resort
places.address: 1590 Evermore Way, Orlando, FL 32836
places.description: The centerpiece is Evermore Bay, a crystal lagoon with its own beach that leaves guests saying the resort feels like it is out of the country. Around it sit houses and flats built for the whole family tree, a family water slide, paddle boarding on the bay, and Chris-Craft boats heading out at sunset. Jack Nicklaus golf and the Conrad Orlando round out the stay. On-site food and drink run at resort prices, so the houses with kitchens earn their keep.

places.name: Orlando International Premium Outlets
places.address: 4951 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: An open-air outlet village at the north end of International Drive, and a full afternoon by design. Shaded walkways run past luxury names and athletic giants, and guests warn it is the kind of place where you enter for one thing and leave with five. Weekend crowds and a peak time parking hunt come with the territory.

places.name: Black Hammock Restaurant
places.address: 2316 Black Hammock Fish Camp Rd, Oviedo, FL 32765
places.description: An Old Florida fish camp on Lake Jesup, where the menu leans into the setting: gator bites, fried gator tail, catfish nuggets, a gator burger. Airboats run off the dock, a lakeside bar pours, and guests call it a real Florida experience. Regulars say the kitchen can be uneven these days, so come for the lake, the gators and the theater of the place first.

places.name: Poke Hana
places.address: 1225A E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: A bright, laid-back Hawaiian counter on East Colonial Drive in Mills 50, where the poke bowls taste as fresh as the room feels. Guests say the tuna is the freshest outside of a top tier sushi spot, and the menu runs from the Maui Wowie bowl and crispy rice tacos to garlic fried chicken, a Kalua pork plate and plates of Hula chicken. Regulars add extra protein for a heartier bowl and save room for the butter mochi, calling it a favorite stop on a hectic day.

places.name: Rise Southern Biscuits & Righteous Chicken - Winter Park
places.address: 110 S Orlando Ave Ste 6, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: A casual counter-service spot where biscuits come out fresh and warm, crispy on the outside and soft inside. The Best Dang Chicken Box, a glazed blueberry biscuit, jumbo cheddar tots, and a hot honey butter chicken biscuit carry the Southern comfort lineup. Guests call it a must-visit, and the grits earn their own loyal following.

places.name: Lazy Moon Pizza
places.address: 11551 University Blvd, Orlando, FL 32817
places.description: UCF's divey, sticker-plastered college hangout, famous for slices bigger than your head and pies guests call ginormous. The menu runs playful: a Cuban pizza, a buffalo chicken pie, a birria calzone, Jason's Mom's Pizza and the Meaty McMeatface, with craft beer on the side. The house ritual is a dip in honey, and nobody here is pretending it is pretty.

places.name: Dutch Bros Coffee
places.address: 116 S Semoran Blvd, Winter Park, FL 32792
places.description: On Semoran Boulevard, a high-energy, genuinely friendly drive-thru where the crew remembers regulars and sings to birthday windows. The Golden Eagle, all caramel and vanilla, is the drink guests name most, with the Caramelizer and Rebel energy drinks close behind. Guests say they leave with a smile, which seems to be the house style.

places.name: Hinckley's Fancy Meats
places.address: 3201 Corrine Dr #104, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: A craft butcher stall inside East End Market, old-school in the best way, with house-cured meats in the case and a deli counter. The pastrami on rye and the banh mi put serious work between bread, and the lemon chicken salad is one guest's most delicious ever. The bacon comes crisp, thick cut and smoky, a taste of the care behind everything in the case.

places.name: Agave Azul Winter Springs
places.address: 5248 Red Bug Lake Rd, Winter Springs, FL 32708
places.description: The Winter Springs room is festive and high-energy, a family-owned Mexican kitchen where the noise is part of the fun. Guests rave about birria tacos and birria brisket, chicken fajitas, queso they call to die for, and spicy margaritas that keep pace with the kitchen. It is the kind of place where tables order widely and linger, stylized but grounded.

places.name: Fiddler's Green Irish Pub & Eatery
places.address: 544 W Fairbanks Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: A dark-wooded, cozy Irish pub on Fairbanks Avenue where live music and a properly poured pint set the tone. The kitchen leans into comfort: beer-battered fish and chips, bangers and mash, a potato soup guests call amazing, and a shepherd's pie some call the best in Orlando. Bread and butter pudding finishes things the traditional way.

places.name: The Porch Winter Park
places.address: 643 N Orange Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: A converted garage on Orange Avenue turned lively, open sports bar for game day, with big screens, games and a menu for any crew. Peel and Eat Big Reds, the Big Texas BLT, loaded tater tots, and the house porchetta sandwich anchor the comfort food, at prices guests call super fair. It is easygoing and fun, the spot regulars pick to watch football with friends.

places.name: The Wine Room on Park Avenue
places.address: 270 S Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Wine tasting without the intimidation: load a Tasting Card and pour your own tastes, from a sip to a full glass, off a wall of wines. Downstairs sits a former bank vault, upstairs cozy leather sofas and a stroll-around room built for mingling. Pear and brie flatbread, baked brie and charcuterie boards keep the tasting grounded.

places.name: The Imperial on Park
places.address: 136 S Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Park Avenue's neighborhood bar, warm and laid back, with boutique wines, craft beers and cocktails built on Winter Park Distillery spirits. The kitchen sends out a blackened grouper sandwich guests rave about, plus smoked salmon crostinis and truffle fries. Live music fills the small room, loud enough that the songs, not the conversation, carry the night.

places.name: Park Avenue Pizza
places.address: 119 E Lyman Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: A no-frills, old-school counter on Lyman Avenue, where guests go for a quick slice done right. The buffalo chicken pizza is the order regulars push hardest, alongside pizza by the slice, buffalo chicken stromboli, and a Bianca pie. Fair prices keep it a neighborhood go-to, and more than one visitor has come back the very next night.

places.name: Power House Cafe
places.address: 111 E Lyman Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: A small, bright Mediterranean spot just off Park Avenue in Winter Park where everything tastes fresh. Guests come back for the chicken shawarma wrap and falafel on pita, the Powerhouse Salad, and smoothies like the Good Karma and the mango Margo. Service moves fast and the room stays casual and friendly, so it works as easily for a quick solo stop as for a relaxed bite with friends.

places.name: Lale Mediterranean Cuisine
places.address: 521 S Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: A cozy, family-run Turkish room on Park Avenue in Winter Park, warm and intimate. The kebabs lead the menu, lamb shish and chicken sis off the grill, with pillowy lavash, haydari, lahmacun and pides from the oven. Save room for kunefe, warm with syrup and pistachio, and finish with a Turkish coffee.

places.name: Pepe's Cantina
places.address: 433 W New England Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: A festive cantina feel in Winter Park, with a beautiful bar and a dining room partly open to the air. The tableside guacamole is made in front of you and earns its praise, while birria tacos, ceviche and enchiladas keep the table busy. Guests call it one of Winter Park's best kept secrets and a great date spot, vibrant yet relaxing.

places.name: Sixty Vines
places.address: 110 S Orlando Ave Ste 12, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: A wine-country room transplanted to Winter Park, with wines on tap by the glass, carafe or bottle and a greenhouse patio that glows after dark. The menu is built for the table: creamy burrata, fig and prosciutto pizza, a double Cabernet burger and pasta dishes guests keep coming back for. At full tilt the room gets loud, which regulars treat as part of the scene.

places.name: Bulla Gastrobar
places.address: 110 S Orlando Ave #7, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: A Winter Park room for Spanish shareables, casual but still upscale, with a buzzy, celebratory energy. Tables fill with chorizo stuffed dates wrapped in bacon, patatas bravas, croquetas and garlic shrimp, and the seafood and chicken paellas anchor a bigger spread. Made-to-order sangria keeps glasses full, and churros or almond cake close things out sweetly.

places.name: Barnie's Coffee & Tea Co.
places.address: 118 S Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Tucked along a cute little lane by Park Avenue, a European-style courtyard cafe guests say feels reminiscent of a cafe overseas. The flavored coffees lead, Santa's White Christmas above all, and the kitchen turns out French toast with berries, shakshuka, a hefty croissant sandwich and the Coffee Cake Crumble. Come with a large appetite and an unhurried pace, since service can take its time once the courtyard fills.

places.name: Tibby's New Orleans Kitchen
places.address: 2203 Aloma Ave, Winter Park, FL 32792
places.description: A Mardi Gras room on Aloma Avenue in Winter Park, lively and colorful, with an atmosphere guests say feels like being back in Louisiana. The gumbo is the dish people cross town for, alongside shrimp po'boys, BBQ shrimp, boudin rolls and warm beignets, with bread pudding to finish. Order a Sazerac and settle in; the room runs festive and a little loud when the live music plays, which regulars count as part of the fun.

places.name: Alma Argentina
places.address: 3607 Aloma Ave Unit 107, Oviedo, FL 32765
places.description: A family-run Argentine steakhouse on Aloma Avenue where empanadas are fried to order; regulars call it their favorite Argentine restaurant. The parrillada mixed grill, sizzling provoleta and milanesa napolitana come out fresh and homemade, with flan or chocotorta to finish. Guests note the prices run a touch high, though most say the quality earns it.

places.name: AVA Mediterranean
places.address: 290 S Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: A glamorous Greek agora on Park Avenue, sophisticated and high-energy from the moment you sit down. Grilled octopus, whole lobster pasta, branzino and baklava anchor a kitchen guests call elite, in a room that turns dim and intimate at dinner and electric when the DJs take over late. Dress up for it, and know the dining room can run warm.

places.name: Corona Cigar Company & Diamond Crown Lounge
places.address: 127 S Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Downtown's relaxed, old-school cigar room on South Orange Avenue, where knowledgeable staff steer you to rare pre-embargo Cubans behind glass. The Diamond Crown Lounge pours deep into scotch, bourbon and prohibition-era whiskies, with mojitos for anyone not smoking. Guests call it the perfect way to spend an afternoon: unhurried, welcoming and happily lost in the humidor.

places.name: Elixir Kitchen and Bar
places.address: 9 W Washington St, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: A rustic-hip gastropub in one of downtown's original buildings, and very much the neighborhood's spot. The from-scratch kitchen punches above the bar's weight with a short rib grilled cheese, chicken and waffles and a patty melt guests name by name. Service runs unhurried, so settle onto the patio and let the room shift from hangout to dance floor as the night takes over.

places.name: Fogo de Chão, Vineland Pointe
places.address: 11543 Regency Village Dr, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: Brazilian churrasco staged tableside at Vineland Pointe, where gaucho chefs carve fire-roasted cuts one slice at a time. Picanha with its ember-kissed crust leads, with fraldinha, filet mignon and a Market Table of seasonal salads, exotic fruits and cheese with honey. Pacing runs leisurely, so treat it as the whole evening, and take the patio for the calmest seat.

places.name: QuesaLoco
places.address: 971 W Fairbanks Ave, Orlando, FL 32804
places.description: Birria country on Fairbanks Ave, in a colorful room with Dia de los Muertos murals and the joyful chaos of its food truck days. Quesabirria tacos fold tender beef and cheese into crisp tortillas built for dunking in rich consommé, and the obsession runs to birria ramen, birria pizza and loco elote. At peak the line is real, and everyone standing in it is staying for the birria.

places.name: Tom's Watch Bar
places.address: 8050 International Dr, Suite 1000, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: On International Drive, a sports bar built like a stadium, with an oversized screen and screens wrapping the room so every seat faces the action. The rooftop Sky Bar puts the skyline behind the game, and the menu goes past the usual playbook with Tom's prime rib dip, Korean BBQ wings and deep-dish nachos. Prices run arena-level, and event nights can add parking and entry fees, so check the event calendar before you go.

places.name: Disney Springs
places.address: 1486 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Disney's open-air waterfront promenade, no park ticket and no turnstile, just an evening on the water. Dining, shopping and live music stitch the neighborhoods together, from the World of Disney store to Ghirardelli ice cream in hand and boats gliding past. Crowds stack up as the night builds and prices carry the Disney premium, but guests still call it a lovely place to wander and soak up the atmosphere.

places.name: Orlando Vineland Premium Outlets
places.address: 8200 Vineland Ave, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: Minutes from Disney, a Mediterranean-inspired outdoor outlet village anchored by Prada, Bottega Veneta, Burberry, Gucci and Tory Burch. Shoppers come for stacked discounts and leave calling it a serious shopping day. The parking lots are the sport on weekends, so the shopping itself is the easy part once you are in.

places.name: O'Shucks Karaoke Bar
places.address: 7467 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Karaoke is not a theme night here, it is the whole calendar, in an unfancy Irish pub on International Drive with a proper sound setup. Guests call it the best place in Orlando for karaoke, and the crowd mixes tourists and regulars into table-wide singalongs. There is no kitchen, so outside food is welcome, while trivia, poker tournaments, and Nickel Beer nights round out the week.

places.name: Overlook Park
places.address: 1988 Spring Ave, Oviedo, FL
places.description: A small county park on the south shore of Lake Jesup, blissfully quiet under mature oaks. The boardwalk stretches over the water where osprey circle overhead and alligators drift past, with a fishing pier and shaded picnic pavilion nearby. Parking is tight and there are no restrooms, so plan accordingly.

places.name: The Grove Bar + Kitchen
places.address: 480 N Orlando Ave C-134, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Citrus-grove heritage worn warmly in a golden, textured room in Winter Park Village built for lingering. The New American kitchen sends out croquettes, Cuban spring rolls, and barbecue ribs, with honey biscuits and ahi tuna tartare in the mix, and guests say the food feels like an experience. Service can stretch when the room fills, so come unhurried and order in rounds.

places.name: Jala Indian Cuisine
places.address: 155 E Morse Blvd, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Founder Manish Nagar's Ahmedabad roots come to Morse Boulevard, in a serene, intimate room of slow-simmered, tandoor-fired cooking. Guests single out the Lamb Tikka Masala with butter naan, the laccha paratha, and a kesar pista kulfi they describe as literally melting in the mouth. It reads as fine dining, but the mood stays quiet and personal.

places.name: Simply Capri
places.address: 114 Ruby Red Place, Winter Garden, FL 34787
places.description: From Flamingo Crossings, a straight aim at the Amalfi Coast, and guests say it works: sunny, warm and transporting, like a quick trip to Italy. The Scialatielli dei Faraglioni piles shrimp, clams, mussels and calamari over house pasta, the Neapolitan pies come out wood-fired and blistered, and the Delizia al Limone closes with limoncello brightness. Prices run high for the neighborhood and tables sit close, but the welcome keeps locals calling it a hidden gem.

places.name: Salt & Ember
places.address: 322 N Alexander St, Mount Dora, FL 32757
places.description: A wood-fired steakhouse on Alexander Street in Mount Dora, relaxed and warm with a polished finish. The starters run from caviar croquettes and charred octopus with chorizo to tuna tataki and bread service with herb butter, with steak frites and the much talked about lobster carbonara behind them. Guests call it a must try in the area, and the Key lime cheesecake makes a bright finish.

places.name: Pio Pio Latin Cuisine
places.address: 2259 S Semoran Blvd, Orlando, FL 32822
places.description: On South Semoran, the Colombian staple locals lean on, a warm, family-style room where plates land generous and homestyle. The rotisserie chicken is the order regulars swear by, alongside bandeja paisa piled high, sizzling lomo saltado, and fried yucca made for dragging through the sauces. Guests talk about the service as much as the food, friendly and attentive in a way that makes the whole table feel looked after.

places.name: Caravan Uzbek & Turkish Cuisine
places.address: 8015 S Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32809
places.description: A small, cozy room on South Orange Ave where Uzbek and Turkish cooking share one table, fully halal and family run. Guests come for the mixed grill and lamb skewers, flaky samsa, fragrant To'y Osh pilaf, and fried laghman, with honey cake to finish. The welcome is the other half of the draw: people keep describing a place that made them feel like family.

places.name: Inchin's Bamboo Garden
places.address: 3900 Town Center Blvd, Orlando, FL 32837
places.description: In Hunter's Creek, Indo-Chinese fusion built for strong flavors and real heat, wok fire meeting Indian spice in nearly every plate. The burnt garlic chili fried rice is the dish guests reach for first, with hot pot momos landing steaming, Mongolian beef, and a Thai yellow curry rounding out the table. The fried rice earns its own praise for tasting clean rather than greasy, and the menu invites ordering too much on purpose.

places.name: Sideward Brewing Co.
places.address: 210 N Bumby Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: A laid-back, unpretentious taproom on Bumby Avenue where beer is brewed clean and the kitchen is, in guests' words, severely underrated. The chicken Caesar wrap draws its own fan club alongside a tempeh Reuben and pretzel with beer cheese, washed down with pours like the Space Wizard NEIPA and Moon Boots IPA. With punk on the speakers and a dog-friendly patio, regulars call it their favorite brewery in Orlando.

places.name: F&D Cantina
places.address: 617 E Central Blvd, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: On East Central, Thornton Park's festive cantina, a dog-friendly patio room where regulars dream about birria tacos and the watermelon margarita. The shrimp ceviche and bacon wrapped jalapenos join a menu that mixes light, crispy bites with bigger comfort plates. On busy nights service can run slow, the honest price of a room this popular.

places.name: Ice & Bites Cafe
places.address: 3402 Technological Ave Ste 220, Orlando, FL 32817
places.description: A whimsical, anime-tinged dessert cafe near UCF built around taiyaki, warm fish-shaped waffle cones filled with ice cream like taro and lavender. Sno shaved ice, the famous affogato cloud, espresso poured over cotton candy until it melts into the scoop below, and drinks like Pretty in Pink keep the menu playful, and one longtime guest calls the boba the best they have had in the US outside the West Coast. Board games and a cozy, super cute room make it a place to linger, not just order.

places.name: Crepe Delicious
places.address: 55 W Church St, Orlando, FL
places.description: A cosy little crêperie on Church Street downtown, where thin, golden crepes arrive stuffed with fresh, flavorful fillings. Go classic with Nutella and strawberry, try the Dubai chocolate crepe loaded with chocolate and fruit, or finish with house-made gelato and the Nutellaccino. Guests rave about the warmth of the place, calling the crepes some of the best in the area and the staff kind and attentive.

places.name: Rocco's Tacos & Tequila Bar
places.address: 7468 W Sand Lake Rd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Sand Lake Road's lakeside patio party, upbeat and colorful, where tableside guacamole steals the show before the tacos even land. Work through Hongos and fish tacos, a shrimp lava bowl, and margaritas by the pitcher while the lake does the decorating. Service can lag when the patio packs out, so order the first round and the guac together and settle into the pace.

places.name: Teak Neighborhood Grill
places.address: Teak Neighborhood Grill, 6400 Time Square Ave, Orlando, FL 32835-6453
places.description: MetroWest's tucked-away neighborhood grill, chill and laid-back, with a burger menu deep enough to keep regulars rotating through it. The Glazed Donut Burger and Kobe Burger get the headlines, but insiders point to the loaded pierogies and the soft pretzel with beer cheese, which one guest called perfection. Dogs are welcome on the patio, the staff reads like family to the regulars, and when the room fills the kitchen can take its time, so settle in.

places.name: STK Steakhouse
places.address: 1580 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: At Disney Springs, a chic steakhouse paired with club-like lounge energy, summed up by guests as vibe dining. Tomahawk steak, Wagyu Lil' BRGs, A5 wagyu, and sweet corn pudding anchor the table, with a rooftop terrace above the room. The sound runs loud and lively, part of the scene rather than a quiet backdrop.

places.name: Christini's Ristorante Italiano
places.address: 7600 Dr Phillips Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: On Restaurant Row since 1984, dinner staged as an old-world occasion: tuxedoed service, candlelight, and live accordion in the room. Guests call it one of the most romantic dinners in town and insist on the veal parm on the bone, with the veal chop and Chilean sea bass over shrimp risotto close behind. It is priced for milestones rather than weeknights, and regulars say it earns it.

places.name: El Burro Loco
places.address: 6524 Carrier Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: On Carrier Drive, bold, loud street-food energy, with guests praising its good authentic flavor. The Classic Burro Loco, quesabirria with consommé, birria street tacos, and cheese shell tacos lead the menu, and Birria Loco fries come loaded with meat and sauce. Portions satisfy in guests' accounts, with a regular saying they would just order the fries on repeat.

places.name: MOOYAH Burgers, Fries & Shakes
places.address: 3155 S Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32806
places.description: On South Orange Avenue in SoDo, a simple promise: burgers built to order, hand-cut fries and hand-spun shakes made with real ice cream. Guests rave about the fries, calling them the best they have had from a fast food spot, and praise the care with allergies at the counter. The Double Diablo brings heat alongside the MOOYAH Cheeseburger and bacon cheeseburger in a fresh, family friendly room.

places.name: Bar Louie (Plaza on University)
places.address: 4100 N Alafaya Trail, Orlando, FL 32826
places.description: At Plaza on University, a lively, relaxed gastropub on North Alafaya Trail where the crowd feels like regulars even on a first visit. The Bourbon BBQ Burger arrives big and juicy, the Voodoo Pasta has its devotees, and the Royal Red Sangria gets hailed by name. Flatbreads, truffle fries and warm cinnamon donut holes round out a menu built for sharing, with polite service keeping the patio easy.

places.name: Goodfella's Pizzeria
places.address: 11873 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32826
places.description: An old-school, no-frills slice shop on East Colonial Drive serving New York-style pies guests say taste like the kind they grew up eating. The Goodfella's Special comes loaded, the garlic knots earn their own following, and the calzones arrive huge. Longtime regulars say the room has changed some since the founding owners sold, but many still call it some of the best pizza outside New York.

places.name: Black Rooster Taqueria
places.address: 1323 N Mills Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: A small, lively Mills 50 room with a dive-bar soul and a chef's hand on the tacos. Corn tortillas are pressed in house, then loaded with smoked beef brisket, achiote pork, chicken tinga or the crispy fish taco guests keep coming back for. Regulars call them some of the best tacos in Orlando and rave about the guacamole, and a bowl of pozole verde or a slice of tres leches cake rounds out the table.

places.name: Valhalla Bakery
places.address: 5565 Old Cheney Hwy, Orlando, FL 32807
places.description: On Old Cheney Highway, a fully vegan bakery, with doughnuts, cupcakes and cakes made without dairy or egg and a case that keeps changing. Regulars talk up the sticky buns, s'mores brownies, Fruity Pebbles doughnuts, and guava and cream cheese cupcakes, plus Yolos for anyone who wants options to spare. Guests call the cakes the best tasting they have had, and the service fast and friendly.

places.name: Gelato LaCarraia
places.address: 7600 Dr Phillips Blvd Ste 38, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: A cozy, quaint Dr. Phillips scoop shop guests call a taste of Florence in Orlando. The gelato comes dense and creamy in the Italian way: benchmark pistachio, the Sinfonia Carraia and a gentle lavender, easy to finish as an affogato or beside a Nutella crepe. The welcome is unhurried, and the staff are happy to let you taste your way to the right flavor.

places.name: The Cowfish Sushi Burger Bar
places.address: 6000 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: At Universal CityWalk, the burgushi idea: sushi rolls built from cheeseburger fixings, fresh tuna rolls and a bento box sampling both worlds. Guests linger on the Blackened Tuna Nachos with crab rangoon dip and avocado salsa, plus spiked hand spun milkshakes that keep the bar playful. The vibe stays vibrant, quirky and loud, with something fantastic for everyone at a table that cannot agree.

places.name: Paddlefish
places.address: 1670 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Seafood aboard a steamboat setting at Disney Springs, with waterfront views and a rooftop deck, picturesque and relaxed. Regulars return for shrimp pasta, clam chowder, lobster corn dogs, and whole Maine lobster, plus focaccia that guests praise at the table. It gets loud when the boat is busy, and loyal guests still say it hits the spot on repeat visits.

places.name: East End Market
places.address: 3201 Corrine Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Local makers under one Audubon Park roof: Gideon's Bakehouse, Olde Hearth Bread, Lineage Coffee, Domu, La Femme du Fromage, Dochi and Hinckley's. The mix of indoor counters and the courtyard gives it what regulars call a relaxed yet lively community feel, somewhere to browse, catch up with friends and leave carrying somebody's craft in a bag. The small lot fills fast at peak times, and guests say it is worth the wait.

places.name: Wine & Corks
places.address: 420 E Church St Ste 108, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Locally owned bottle shop on East Church Street with a real sushi kitchen inside, an odd pairing that actually works. The staff loves talking bottles, from crisp whites to full bodied reds, and the self serve tasting taps turn browsing into an experience. Add a salmon tempura roll or a prosecco popsicle and it becomes an easy, unhurried evening.

places.name: Bruster's Real Ice Cream
places.address: 5584 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Cheerful, old-fashioned scoop stand on International Drive, with ice cream made in-store and fresh waffle cones. Graham Central Station and white raspberry truffle lead the regulars' loyalties, alongside a hot fudge brownie sundae, Southern banana pudding and a banana peanut butter scoop for the plant-based crowd. Guests call it good quality, not too sweet and affordable, with pup cups for the dog waiting outside.

places.name: Bonefish Grill
places.address: Bonefish Grill, 5463 Gateway Village Cir, Orlando, FL 32812
places.description: At Lee Vista off Gateway Village Circle, polished and reliable, with wood-grilled seafood that suits date night. Bang Bang Shrimp starts nearly every table, the Chilean sea bass and parmesan-crusted rainbow trout carry the mains, and a dirty martini from the bar finishes the setup. Guests reach for words like superb and never disappoints, and birthday tables land here often.

places.name: Seasons 52
places.address: 7700 W Sand Lake Rd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Oak fire and a brick oven drive the menu here, turning with the seasons and portions sized for humans. The cedar plank roasted salmon, wood-grilled filet, and flatbreads anchor the table, and guests warn that the Mini Indulgence desserts are non-negotiable, small sweets you cannot leave without. The room overlooks Sand Lake and runs lively when it fills, an easy date night without the heaviness.

places.name: Keke's Breakfast Cafe
places.address: 4192 Conroy Rd, Orlando, FL
places.description: Breakfast done by hand near Millenia: coffee ground in house, eggs cracked to order, real butter and no microwave. The Florida pancakes taste like grandma's, the stuffed French toast towers, and the Greek omelet with home fries covers the savory side. Weekend waits run long, and regulars say the plate is worth it.

places.name: Camila's Brazilian Restaurant
places.address: 5458 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: On International Drive since 1989, this festive, unpretentious buffet is where local Brazilians treat it as home. Picanha comes off the grill, feijoada and Brazilian beef stroganoff anchor the hot line, and bobo de camarao brings the creamy shrimp, with Guarana or a caipirinha in hand. Save room for flan and passion fruit mousse, and expect to head back for a second plate.

places.name: The Juicy Crab
places.address: 296 E Michigan St, Orlando, FL
places.description: Built for messy, casual seafood boils on East Michigan Street in SoDo, meant to be shared around the table. The Build Your Own Seafood Combo piles up snow crab legs, shrimp and fixings in Old Bay sauce, with a fried shrimp combo and Dungeness crab for bigger appetites. Guests praise big portions and seasoning that lands bold, though regulars note the boil can swing between visits.

places.name: Portillo's
places.address: 7715 Palm Pkwy, Orlando, FL 32836
places.description: Chicago street food lands on Palm Parkway in a loud, retro room dressed like a 50s diner, all red chrome and nostalgia. The Italian beef arrives dipped and dripping, the Chicago-style hot dog is the one guests call the best they have ever had, and the chocolate cake shake turns dessert into a drink. It reads as a taste of Chicago in Orlando, fast and generous, built for homesick Midwesterners.

places.name: Tasty Takeover
places.address: 2424 E Robinson St, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Every Tuesday night, food trucks take over the lots behind the Milk District bars for an easygoing block party. The rotating lineup keeps every visit different, from Red Panda Noodle and Mohawk Smokehouse to brisket, bao buns and street tacos. Seating is limited and parking can take patience on busy nights, but guests love the organized setup and the chance to graze across cuisines with friends.

places.name: Yellow Dog Eats
places.address: 1236 Hempel Ave, Gotha, FL 34786
places.description: Working out of a century-old general store in Gotha, funky and laid-back, with sandwich names that make you grin. The Florida Cracker stacks house pulled pork with coleslaw, gouda, bacon, pickles, and crispy onions, and the pulled pork nachos have a following of their own. Dogs are welcome on the patio, groups spread out, and guests call it less a restaurant than a destination.

places.name: Chef Art Smith's Homecomin'
places.address: 1602 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Homey Florida farmhouse cooking at Disney Springs, generous and welcoming from the first plate. Art's Famous Fried Chicken leads, with Thigh High Chicken Biscuits, Church Lady Deviled Eggs, and Momma's Mac & Cheese piled in portions guests describe as huge. Save room for Hummingbird Cake or Shine Cake, and expect a wait that regulars say is worth it.

places.name: Stadium Club
places.address: 8101 World Center Dr, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: Game day gets the full stadium treatment inside Caribe Royale, with a wraparound ribbon screen keeping every matchup in view. Guests call the atmosphere electric, and the kitchen aims past standard sports bar fare with a Slam Dunk Pretzel, smash burgers, truffle parmesan fries and chicken and waffles. It gets loud and service can wobble when the room is packed, but fans call it a whole experience rather than just a place to watch.

places.name: Duffy's Sports Grill
places.address: Duffy's Sports Grill, 951 Market Promenade Ave, Lake Mary, FL 32746
places.description: TVs everywhere in Lake Mary, so every seat feels close to the game. A busy patio and a family friendly, game day room give it the feel of a neighborhood sports bar. Order the Original Duffy's Cheeseburger, Traditional Jumbo Wings, or truffle parmesan fries, and try the Reuben that regulars single out as a standout.

places.name: Krungthep Tea Time
places.address: 1051 W Fairbanks Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Calm, minimalist black-and-white tea room on Fairbanks Avenue in Winter Park, named for Bangkok and built for long chats. The sandwiches carry the menu, Gra-prow chicken, Tomyum Goong and green curry, each sweet, spicy and savory at once, washed down with Thai iced tea or the pink Nom Yen. Brick toast desserts, like the Sleeping Beauty with Thai tea ice cream, make for a slow finish, though portions lean petite.

places.name: Metro Diner (Kissimmee)
places.address: 2714 Osceola Pkwy, Kissimmee, FL 34741
places.description: Metro Diner's Kissimmee room is a classic Florida diner, cozy and old school, doing comfort food without irony. The fried chicken and waffles headline a menu one guest calls home to some of the best fried chicken they have ever had, with cinnamon roll pancakes, Iron City meatloaf, shrimp and grits and pumpkin bread pudding rounding out the greatest hits. Portions run ample, the welcome is genuine, and fans say the wait at busy times is worth it.

places.name: Puro Dulzor by Karolene
places.address: 1354 E Vine St, Kissimmee, FL 34744
places.description: Cozy, family-run hole in the wall on East Vine Street where guests call the coffee the best in Kissimmee. Then come the Puerto Rican plates, a towering tripleta sandwich, crisp empanadillas, crema de maiz like abuela made it and a mayorca stuffed with Nutella for the sweet finish. The owner greets customers herself, and regulars say the little room simply feels like home.

places.name: Cocina Maya Mexican Grill & Mezcaleria
places.address: 3590 US-17 Ste 1026, Lake Mary, FL 32746
places.description: Cozy, festive Lake Mary room where Mexican cooking goes well past taco-shop basics, with a little tableside flair. The Queso Fundido Molcajeteado arrives bubbling, the Holy Guacamole lives up to its name, and quesabirria tacos and sizzling fajitas keep the table busy. Mezcal cocktails bring the smoke, and the margaritas are the pours guests keep coming back for.

places.name: Hooked Fish Camp
places.address: 550 Towne Center Cir, Sanford, FL 32771
places.description: Relaxed, coastal fish camp cooking comes to Towne Center Circle in Sanford. Guests describe everything as fresh and prepared perfectly, from sweet heat shrimp and Old Bay peel and eat shrimp to deviled eggs and shrimp linguine. Finish with blackened Faroe salmon, crab legs, or a slice of lemon pie in a friendly room that keeps the mood easy.

places.name: Green Papaya Thai & Sushi
places.address: 2480 W State Rd 434, Longwood, FL 32779
places.description: Thai menu and sushi bar side by side in a polished, modern Longwood room, a combo guests say exceeded expectations. The Tom Kha soup is the bowl people talk about afterward, the pad thai and drunken noodles hit their marks, and the duck with yellow curry could carry the menu on its own. The room stays calm and thoughtfully designed, an easy fit for a date or dinner with the whole crew.

places.name: Southern Steer Butcher (Orlando)
places.address: 11024 W Colonial Dr, Ocoee, FL 34761
places.description: Family-run butcher on West Colonial Drive in Ocoee, where staff guide you through the case and how to cook it. Guests come for fresh meat sold by the pound, pre marinated cuts ready for the grill, dry aged steak, house burger patties, and chicken crack sausages with flavor guests call unforgettable. One regular put it as what they had been looking for since moving to Florida, a neighborhood shop built on helpful, knowledgeable service.

places.name: The Twisted Chopstick
places.address: 412 S Woodland Blvd, DeLand, FL 32720
places.description: DeLand's cozy, Godzilla-themed sushi stop on Woodland Boulevard, family-run and relaxed as a second home. The Fire Tonkatsu ramen brings real heat, the Black Widow and Samurai rolls lead the sushi case, and starters like Dragon Balls and gyoza are built for sharing. Regulars call it the best sushi in town, and poke bowls and sushi burritos widen the order for mixed tastes.

places.name: Crooked Can Minneola
places.address: 1600 Crooked Can Loop, Minneola, FL 34715
places.description: A sprawling take on the Winter Garden brewery: production brewery and taproom fronting a food hall in Minneola. Space Cowboi IPA, Florida Sunshine and rotating beer flights pour inside, while food hall counters like This Little Piggy BBQ, Sir Benji's Donuts and The Local Butcher keep groups fed. Out back, a beer garden and live music stage give everyone room to spread out.

places.name: BTW Burgers Tacos Waffles
places.address: 115 E Main St, Tavares, FL 32778
places.description: On Main Street in Tavares, playful and unpretentious, doing exactly what its name promises with real imagination in each lane. The Winner Winner Chicken & Waffles, a Black N Blue Burger guests call unbelievable and a Taco Trio with real kick anchor the menu, while the Half Witted Monkey caramel rum waffle and deep fried Double Stuff Oreos handle dessert. Guests call it some of the best food hands down, bold and fun from first bite to last.

places.name: Harrell's Hot Dogs and Cold Cones
places.address: 54 W Plant St, Winter Garden, FL 34787
places.description: Narrow little Plant Street hideaway for grilled all-beef dogs that guests say make a simple hot dog better. Buns arrive soft, slightly sweet, and toasted with butter, loaded as a Chicago Dog, a Mac Monster, or a chili cheese dog, with hand cut fries and truffle fries on the side. Cold cones and dirty sodas finish things while the Plant Street crowd strolls past the outdoor seats.

places.name: PokeWorks (Oviedo)
places.address: 45 W Mitchell Hammock Rd, Oviedo, FL 32765
places.description: Build-your-own poke in Oviedo, with sushi-grade ahi, salmon, albacore, shrimp and scallops over rice or greens. Regulars favor the Hawaiian Ahi bowl and the poke burrito, with garlic spam musubi as the cult side order. The room is clean, fast and friendly, and guests call it their favorite healthy stop in town.

places.name: Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex
places.address: Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex, Space Commerce Way, Merritt Island, FL 32953
places.description: Stand beneath the Space Shuttle Atlantis on Merritt Island and guests say you can't help but be impressed by the real hardware. The bus tour to the Apollo/Saturn V Center, the Rocket Garden and astronaut encounters keep the history close enough to touch, and the sheer scale of the Saturn V stops people mid-sentence. Tickets, food and parking run steep, but visitors keep calling it educational at its best and worth the time and cost.

places.name: Ivanhoe Park Brewing Company
places.address: 1300 Alden Rd, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Relaxed and cozy on Alden Road, with indoor and outdoor room and a taproom guests call super dog friendly. Pours run from the crisp Park Hopp'r pilsner and Joyland IPA to Tupac ShaPorter and the Guavacation sour, with the Firestarter jalapeno hot honey ale for heat. Irregular Smash burgers and rotating food trucks keep the table covered while the beer garden stays unhurried.

places.name: La Revancha Cuban Cafe
places.address: 7339 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32807
places.description: Pressing Cubans on East Colonial Drive since 1998, with salsa on the speakers and an unpretentious, relaxed room. The Classic Cuban sandwich, ropa vieja with peppers, empanadas, and tostones anchor the savory side, while a cortadito, cafe con leche, and the Cubano iced coffee keep the coffee strong. Guests call it a favorite go to, with guava pastries and quesitos for a sweet finish and portions that satisfy.

places.name: Viet-Nomz
places.address: 11798 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32817
places.description: Cute, cozy fast-casual Vietnamese spot on East Colonial Drive with a friendly, welcoming feel. The King Pho Bowl is the headline, absolutely huge and finished at the fresh herb bar, while the NOMZ-ster Bowl XL, Wa-Pho fries and Nuoc-Nom wings keep the table busy. Guests rave about the matcha Vietnamese coffee, sweet and strong enough to order on its own.

places.name: Omelet Bar
places.address: 12250 Strategy Blvd Ste 401, Orlando, FL 32817
places.description: Bright, relaxed cafe on Strategy Blvd near UCF where the omelet is the main event, built to order from a fresh filling bar. The Bostonian stuffs lobster inside and finishes with lobster bisque, the carne frittata pairs smoked brisket with sausage gravy, and a chicken and waffle flight makes the table happy. Beignets, biscuits and gravy and stuffed French toast round things out, though the wait can stretch when the room fills up.

places.name: Market On South
places.address: 2603 E South St, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Fully plant-based food hall on East South Street, bohemian and laid-back, as much community space as place to eat. The counters cover the comfort food bases: an OrangeBird sloppy joe, BBQ jackfruit with real smoke, creamy baked mac and cheese and Kind Cleaver sandwiches. Dessert holds its own at the ice cream counter, where the cookie monster cone and Cuban cafecito scoop help prove the guest point that you do not have to be vegan to fall in love with the food here.

places.name: At The Diner
places.address: 5072 Dr Phillips Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Bright, playful Dr. Phillips spot where the pancakes do the talking, cinnamon roll, Boston cream and Fruity Pebbles versions. The Bennyffle puts eggs benedict on a waffle next to chicken and waffles, and the house potatoes earn their own fans. Portions run generous, regulars swear it is the best diner spot in Orlando, and a busy room can mean a short wait for a table.

places.name: Insomnia Cookies
places.address: 12101 University Blvd, Orlando, FL
places.description: Cozy, delivery-first cookie shop near UCF built around one simple pleasure: cookies served warm. The Chocolate Chunk and Salted Caramel Deluxe come out gooey with crispy edges, and guests say they just melt in your mouth. The Cookiewich presses ice cream between two cookies, and the Carmellionaire ice cream gives salted caramel fans a second way in.

places.name: Shake Shack I-Drive
places.address: 8359 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: The I-Drive Shake Shack sits in ICON Park under the Orlando Eye, a busy fast-casual patio stop with rustic chic polish. The ShackBurger and the bacon and cherry pepper SmokeShack anchor the menu beside the fried portobello Shroom Burger and crinkle-cut fries that stay crisp to the last one. Custard shakes steal the show, guests call them truly amazing, and the Orlandough concrete keeps it local; just expect a line when the park crowds roll in.

places.name: The Polite Pig
places.address: 1536 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Modern barbecue done fast-casual at Disney Springs, lively and chill with counter service that keeps things moving. Coffee-rubbed brisket, the Southern Pig sandwich, waffle fries, and sweet potato tots fill the tray, and guests call the mac and cheese the best they have ever eaten anywhere. Everything is built to melt in your mouth in guests' words, with bourbon and drinks on tap to round out the order.

places.name: Kai Asian Street Fare
places.address: 1555 State Rd 436 Ste 1171, Winter Park, FL 32792
places.description: Casual, unpretentious spot on State Road 436 serving craveable Asian street food under one roof. The Korean fried wings are the headline, shattering-crisp in mango habanero or spicy garlic parmesan, with tonkotsu ramen, garlic noodles and soy chili wontons rounding out the table. Guests sum it up simply: get wings, get noodles, and save room for the sweet potato mochi donut.

places.name: Main Street Pizza
places.address: 16 Broadway, Kissimmee, FL 34741
places.description: Downtown Kissimmee's old-school New York style joint, family oriented, with slices guests swear are bigger than their face. The Monster and the Colorado pile on the toppings, the Buffalo Chicken rides a white base, and one guest says it tastes just like back home in Jersey. Save room for the nitrogen ice cream, and do not be surprised if it becomes your go-to pizza spot in Kissimmee.

places.name: Paloma Parlor
places.address: 625 Main St, Windermere, FL 34786
places.description: Windermere regulars treat this as their own; now trading as Paloma Parlor, it is small, plant-filled and contemporary. The lattes come strong, smooth, and never bitter, with lavender, rose, and the Lucky Latte keeping the menu playful beside house-baked croissants and macarons. Ice cream joined the lineup after the move, and guests call it worth the short trip out of Orlando.

places.name: Dough Boyz Pizza
places.address: 201 W State Rd 434, Longwood, FL 32750
places.description: Longwood's old-school New York slice shop, family owned and confident: their line is it is not the water, it is the recipe. The Grandma pie and the Brooklyn Sicilian anchor the case, the vodka margherita takes hot honey beautifully, and the chicken parm stuffed garlic knot is a cult object all its own. Guests describe the Sicilian as biting into a cloud, and the room runs no-frills and neighborhood to the core.

places.name: Le Macaron Celebration
places.address: 671 Front St #110, Celebration, FL 34747
places.description: A small piece of Paris on Front Street in Celebration, with a bright boutique case of macarons guests call melt-in-your-mouth perfection. The shells come crisp with chewy centers in flavors like salted caramel, pistachio, rose and Colombian coffee, with eclairs, butter croissants, beignets and house-made gelato behind them. It is a quiet, pretty pause on a lakeside stroll, the kind guests say feels like flying to Paris without leaving town.

places.name: Kobe Japanese Steakhouse
places.address: 8148 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Dinner becomes theater on International Drive, with teppanyaki chefs, onion volcanoes, flying shrimp and tricks guests had not seen before. The hibachi sirloin and seafood trio come in enormous portions, and the sushi side holds its own with the Krabby Shrimp roll and soup dumplings. It is lively, generous, and built for birthdays and tables that want a show with their meal.

places.name: Twistee Treat
places.address: Twistee Treat, 4500 Curry Ford Rd, Orlando, FL 32812
places.description: A towering ice-cream cone building marks this Curry Ford Road spot, an old-school soft-serve landmark pouring since 1983. Creamy twists come in cups, cones, shakes, malts, and floats, with the Brownie Boat, waffle taco, cookiewich, and a root beer float one regular calls the best. The walk-up window can run slow, so claim a picnic bench and let the nostalgia work.

places.name: Jeremiah's Italian Ice
places.address: 877 N Alafaya Trl, Orlando, FL
places.description: Bright, Orlando-born walk-up stand in Waterford Lakes where the Gelati layers Italian ice with creamy soft serve. Scoop Froggy Frog, strawberry shortcake and Cookies and Cream lead a flavor board guests love sampling, with big portions and friendly staff at the window. The line can look long, but guests say it moves fairly quickly.

places.name: Lake Nona Deli and Market
places.address: 8510 Insular Ln, Orlando, FL 32827
places.description: Village Walk's neighborhood counter, part deli, part pizzeria, part market, built on Boar's Head meats and Olde Hearth bread. The Italian Classic sandwich and the Adore pizza draw loyal followings, with gelato and a Nutella pizza for the sweet finish. It sits inside a gated community, so expect a friendly stop at the guard shack on the way in.

places.name: High Tide Harry's
places.address: 4645 S Semoran Blvd, Orlando, FL 32822
places.description: Airport corridor's classic local seafood joint, no-frills and nautical, family owned and easygoing except about the shellfish. The Captain's Seafood Combo anchors the table, the Blue Stew has its own devoted following, and crab legs and charbroiled oysters keep the crackers busy. It is generous, fun, and proudly old-school, the kind of place locals bring out-of-towners to make a point.

places.name: Margaritaville (CityWalk)
places.address: 6000 Universal Studios Plaza Ste 704, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Full island escapism at Universal CityWalk, with kitschy tropical decor and seating sections inside and out to wander. The Volcano Nachos arrive huge and built for sharing, alongside the Cheeseburger in Paradise, coconut shrimp and a margarita flight. Buffett songs and familiar tunes fill the room while Key lime pie closes the beach day fantasy.

places.name: Five Guys (CityWalk)
places.address: 6000 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: On the upper level of Universal CityWalk, burgers stacked to order with hand-cut fries piled high in the cup. Thick milkshakes round out a familiar counter stop built around customization.

places.name: El Paraíso Del Marisco
places.address: 8421 S Orange Blossom Trl Ste 156, Orlando, FL 32809
places.description: Ecuadorian and Peruvian seafood that Orlando's Latin families describe as tasting like home. Encebollado arrives the way Manabí cooks it, the ceviche mixto snaps bright and fresh, and the chaulafán de mariscos is built to share, with bolón de verde for the plantain devotees. Plates are made to order, so the kitchen takes its time, in a warm, unfussy, family-run room.

places.name: Topgolf Orlando
places.address: 9295 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Part driving range, part restaurant, part rooftop hangout on Universal Boulevard, with climate-controlled bays and a terrace with fire pits. Guests say they go for the vibes, not the scorecard, hitting Angry Birds target games between Smokehouse Burgers and injectable donut holes. The energy stays social and welcoming to all skill levels, more hang than golf.

places.name: World Food Trucks
places.address: 5811 W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy, Kissimmee, FL 34746
places.description: A Kissimmee parking lot becomes a passport you can eat through, truck after truck serving arepas, tacos, elotes and more. Guests call the variety overwhelming in a good way, with something for everyone and music keeping the block party rolling. Quality swings from truck to truck, which is half the fun: come hungry, wander, and leave with a list for next time.

places.name: AJ's Press
places.address: 182 W State Rd 434 #1008, Longwood, FL 32750
places.description: Family-run Longwood counter built around the press, where sandwiches come off bolillo or telera soft yet crispy at the edges. The crunchy chicken sandwich is the one guests say ruined other chicken sandwiches for them, with beer braised brisket, mojo pork, and house-made lattice chips close behind. Jalapeño bacon hush puppies land while you wait in line, and the whole place feels like the neighborhood shop the chains forgot how to be.

places.name: Shake Shack Winter Park
places.address: 119 N Orlando Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: On Lake Killarney, guests call it the best view for a burger joint: the familiar Shack standard with the lake as backdrop. Order a ShackBurger or the Black Truffle Burger with cheese fries and a smooth, creamy strawberry shake, then carry it out to the patio over the water. The plaza lot can be tight and food can take a while when the place gets busy, but the lake view makes the wait feel easy.

places.name: Blaze Pizza
places.address: 4100 N Alafaya Trl, Orlando, FL 32826
places.description: Fast-fired, assembly-line pizza on North Alafaya Trail, built and made fresh right in front of you. Guests load up a Build Your Own and ask for it well done for that crispy crust, and the new Detroit-style pizza has been winning people over. Cauliflower crust, keto and vegan cheese options mean everyone at the table gets exactly the pizza they pictured.

places.name: Rome's Flavours
places.address: Rome's Flavours, 124 E Morse Blvd, Winter Park, FL 32789-3819
places.description: Cozy, family-owned trattoria on Morse Boulevard near Park Avenue, quiet and intimate, where guests say the food tastes like Italy. The carbonara steals the show, the handmade fettuccine Alfredo and the meatballs draw their own devotees, and pistachio cannoli close the meal. Couples call it their favorite restaurant in the area and come back every trip.

places.name: Cuban American Cafe
places.address: 135 W Central Blvd Ste 160, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Tucked inside a downtown credit union on Central Boulevard, a no-frills, family-run spot regulars call the real deal. The pressed Cuban comes on house-baked Cuban bread, the croquetas are homemade, and the cafe con leche tastes, as one guest put it, like home. Regulars swear the cortadito is the best Cuban coffee in town, and a guava pastelito is the right way to finish.

places.name: LaSpada's Original Cheesesteaks and Hoagies
places.address: 1010 Lee Rd, Orlando, FL 32810
places.description: On Lee Road, Delco standards come to College Park with an old-school, no-frills, family-run counter. The Original stacks steak with sweet onions and white American cheese with the cheese distributed through every bite, while the mushroom cheesesteak and the Famous Italian hoagie pile on what guests call an insane amount of meat. Soft bread, fresh veggies, and hot, crispy fries complete a sandwich guests describe as a beautiful meatrosity.

places.name: Lombardi's Seafood
places.address: 1888 W Fairbanks Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Old-school, family-run fish market on Fairbanks Avenue in Winter Park, the counter guests call the freshest fish in town. The cases run deep with stone crab claws, red snapper and Key West shrimp, and the small café cooks what the market sells: lobster bisque, clam chowder, fish tacos and a grouper sandwich. It is no-frills and bustling, and the little café fills fast, so browse the case first and eat while you decide what to take home.

places.name: Peterbrooke Chocolatier
places.address: 300 S Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Handcrafted chocolate in the European tradition on Park Avenue since 1983, and the cocoa scent reaches the sidewalk. The chocolate-covered popcorn is the signature, the house gelato gets called the best some guests have had in the US, and dipped strawberries, truffles, and malt shakes fill out the cases. Prices run Park Avenue, so buy the good stuff and buy less of it.

places.name: Cold Stone Creamery
places.address: 6000 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL
places.description: At Universal CityWalk, mix-ins fold into ice cream on a frozen granite slab, built to order at the counter. Creations press in birthday cake pieces, brownie chunks, candy and fruit, and the Brownie a la Cold Stone pairs a warm brownie with cold scoops.

places.name: Se7en Bites
places.address: 617 N Primrose Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Bustling, homey Southern bakery cafe on Primrose Drive, owner on the floor, running like a well-oiled machine. The chicken pot pie is the legend, all flaky crust and tasty filling, backed by the Minnie Pearl chicken and waffles, the Signature Chicken Biscuit and the Se7enth Heaven smash burger. The sweets lean nostalgic, from the Vanilla Bean Bourbon Bacon Moon Pie to the Ding Dong, and regulars know the popular trays sell out, so expect a line out the door.

places.name: Kelly's Homemade Ice Cream
places.address: 3114 Corrine Dr, Orlando, FL
places.description: Small-batch ice cream churned with monthly flavors like Cookie Monster, Mexican Chocolate, Key Lime Pie and Coquito, plus flights and Dog Pops. The pink and white parlor reads quirky and welcoming, and regulars describe it as more than just an ice cream shop, a little tradition they look forward to. Clear allergy labeling and rotating non-dairy options keep the case easy to navigate.

places.name: The Stubborn Mule
places.address: 100 S Eola Dr #103, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Steps from the swans of Lake Eola, Moscow mules are the calling card in a cozy, lively room regulars call simply a vibe. The Stubborn Mule Burger and the Belgian waffle burger carry the menu, and one regular calls the smash burger the best they have had in a long while, with sticky pork belly and parmesan rosemary fries earning their own loyalists. Service can be hit or miss on crowded nights, but the food and the lakefront stroll after keep people coming back.

places.name: Jesse's Rib Shack
places.address: 2202 W Pine St, Orlando, FL 32805
places.description: Jesse's Rib Shack is an old-school smokehouse on West Pine Street where you can see the smoke rolling off the back before you reach the door. Ribs and rib tips ride on the homemade Magic Sauce, the sauce guests joke about wanting to drink, with BBQ chicken, seafood rice and creamy mac and cheese rounding out the plates. The cooking reminds guests of a home barbecue: generous, laid-back and full of Southern hospitality.

places.name: The Villa
places.address: 25 Wall St Bldg B, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Now The Villa, a playful, high-energy Wall Street Plaza hangout built around arcade cabinets, board games and video game stations. Signature pours like the Banana Hammock and the Black & Blue Super Smash keep the grown-up side covered, with spinach artichoke dip and nachos supreme for the table. It is casual, group-friendly and made for crowds who cannot agree on just one kind of night out.

places.name: Croissant Gourmet
places.address: 120 E Morse Blvd, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Cozy, spotless little bakery on Morse Boulevard that guests describe as a piece of France in Winter Park. The almond croissant is the star, flaky layers around sweet almond paste, with fruit tarts, eclairs, Napoleons and macarons filling the case. The Breakfast Croissant packs an omelette into buttery layers, and seating is limited, so expect a squeeze when the case draws a crowd.

places.name: Junior Colombian Burger
places.address: 11875 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL
places.description: On East Colonial Drive, Colombian street food meets the American burger, and nothing about it is quiet. The Explosion Burger stacks plantain, mozzarella, egg, corn and potato sticks, the Triple brings crushed chips and house pineapple sauce, and the pink and garlic sauces go on everything. Guests call the burgers very juicy, some say the best they have had in ages, and the empanadas get praised as the real Colombian deal.

places.name: U & Me Revolving Hot Pot
places.address: 12384 S Apopka Vineland Rd, Orlando, FL 32836
places.description: Hot pot becomes an interactive game here, with plates circling past on a revolving conveyor for your broth. Guests favor the spicy broth, described as spicy, floral, and full of flavor, and the Tom Yum, with a sauce bar and meat and seafood bars to build from. A cat robot bringing ice cream and a finish of green tea ice cream keep it cute and family friendly.

places.name: Chewy Boba Company
places.address: 1212 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Old-school Mills 50 staple on Colonial Drive, pouring since 2002 and still keeping cups generous and prices honest. The taro milk tea is the one guests swear by, properly lavender and loaded with chewy pearls, with brown sugar milk tea, passion fruit boba tea and a floral lavender milk tea close behind. The Vietnamese iced coffee with sea salt cold foam has its own fan club, and the macarons make an easy add-on.

places.name: Hard Rock Live
places.address: 6050 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Beside the Hard Rock Cafe at Universal CityWalk, arena-scale sound and lighting with sightlines guests say stay close from almost anywhere. Memorabilia greets you at the entry and the room hosts concerts and stand up with a club like intimacy. Guests call it a world class venue for viewing a favorite band.

places.name: Inter&Co Stadium
places.address: 655 W Church St, Orlando, FL 32805
places.description: Downtown's soccer cathedral, home to Orlando City SC since 2017, and guests praise the atmosphere. The Wall supporters' section keeps the roar going while the stands turn purple, and sightlines stay good from any seat. Orlando Made concessions stock local favorites like 4 Rivers BBQ, though prices run stadium-high, and the night feels intimate and electric at once.

places.name: Orlando Farmers Market
places.address: 20 N Eola Dr, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Every Sunday, the Lake Eola lakefront becomes a shaded, dog-friendly stretch of vendors with live music and a wine and beer garden. Produce stalls, artisan goods, paella, acai bowls, and drinkable coconuts share space in what guests call a foodie's dream of a half day. Parking near the lake can be a hunt on market days, so plan for that and linger.

places.name: Marlow's Tavern
places.address: 6889 Eagle Watch Dr, Orlando, FL 32822
places.description: Neighborhood tavern in Lee Vista treating first timers like regulars, starting with pub chips loaded with blue cheese and bacon on the house. The kitchen runs scratch American: hand-cut tavern fries, crab dip, asparagus fries, shrimp and grits, and a Black and Blue burger. Guests call it a hidden gem, warm and lively without trying too hard.

places.name: Yard House
places.address: 8367 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: ICON Park's big-room guarantee: a wall of taps, a glass-enclosed keg room as centerpiece, and classic rock under everything. The menu runs wide, from poke nachos and a Korean BBQ cheesesteak to an onion ring tower built for the table, in portions that match the room. Groups land here on game days and convention nights because everybody finds something.

places.name: Bubba Gump Shrimp Co.
places.address: 6000 Universal Blvd Ste 735, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: At Universal CityWalk, full movie theme with trivia at the table and a room guests say makes you feel like you are in the film. Shrimp comes fried, coconut crusted and in a crab and shrimp boil, alongside shrimp mac and cheese and garlic bread guests keep recommending. The mood stays lively, nostalgic and family friendly, touristy in the way regulars embrace.

places.name: The Cheesecake Factory
places.address: 4200 Conroy Rd Space A-148, Orlando, FL 32839
places.description: The Mall at Millenia outpost of the famously sprawling menu, where the move is to order across it, from avocado eggrolls to Chicken Pasta Da Vinci. Portions run big enough that guests promise you will not go hungry, and the cheesecake case is the required final stop. Expect a wait to be seated, then a bustling, festive room once you are in.

places.name: The Donut King
places.address: 3716 Howell Branch Rd, Winter Park, FL 32792
places.description: Family-run, no-frills shop on Howell Branch Road where donuts come out bigger than chain versions and heavy on icing flavor. Guests reach for the maple bacon donut, the King Donut, cronuts and cinnamon rolls, and regulars call them the best donuts in the area. Apple fritters and popular flavors go fast, and freshness can be hit-or-miss, so regulars pick from what looks best in the case.

places.name: Kilwins Ice Cream - Chocolate - Fudge
places.address: 122 N Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Fresh waffle cone smell finds you first on Park Avenue, where fudge is paddled on marble and caramel apples are dipped in the open. Guests sample their way through the ice cream case, families treat it as a stop they have to make, and the chocolate dipped marshmallows win over the kids. Head out with Mackinac Island fudge or a turtle caramel apple and the Park Avenue stroll ahead of you.

places.name: Winter Park Farmers Market
places.address: 150 N New York Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Every Saturday morning, Central Park West Meadow fills with a laid-back, strollable market locals treat as a tradition. Booths run from produce, fresh pasta and local honey to Jamaican patties, kettle corn, acai bowls and armfuls of fresh flowers, with dogs in tow everywhere. Regulars swear the shroom coffee from the kombucha wagon alone is worth the trip.

places.name: The Ganachery
places.address: The Ganachery, 1486 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Jewel-box chocolate shop at Disney Springs, with an open show kitchen where you can watch ganache squares and chocolate piñatas being made. Artisan s'mores are torched to order, and hot ganache and the Minnie Ganache Pop add to the indulgence. Guests call the bites little morsels of heaven, an homage to a chocolate lover's desires in their words.

places.name: BakeChop
places.address: 110 Artisan Aly, DeLand, FL 32720
places.description: Cozy, quirky scratch kitchen on Artisan Alley in DeLand, where staff stay sweet and welcoming even when the line is out the door. The Allicin Wonderland burger arrives cooked to medium rare perfection, the Peach Jam Burger layers goat cheese and jalapeño heat, and sweet potato fries and Black Forest cake round out a menu built on fresh ingredients. Guests call it always a good choice, the kind of place where the food tastes great every single time.

places.name: Donuts To Go
places.address: 1414 W 1st St, Sanford, FL 32771
places.description: Early-morning sweet spot built around a square donut made for sharing. Donuts To Go serves a generously sized Square Glazed Donut alongside Maple Bacon, French Toast, Almond Joy, and a flaky Cronut. Chocolate cake donuts draw fans who call them heavenly, and caramel work gets its own praise. Breakfast widens the visit: burritos, biscuits and gravy, and New York-style bagels with cream cheese. Fresh, homemade, and kid-friendly, the shop earns local loyalty. Come hungry enough to take donuts and a real breakfast seriously together.

places.name: The Crooked Spoon
places.address: 200 Citrus Tower Blvd, Clermont, FL 34711
places.description: Low-key Clermont gastropub on Citrus Tower Boulevard, chef-driven but laid-back, where guests say they never leave disappointed. The 420 Burger, lobster grilled cheese and six-cheese lobster mac carry the indulgent side, while Soco wings in garlic cheese whiskey sauce get called a must-try. It stays fairly quiet, with servers glad to steer you toward dishes you rarely find anywhere else.

places.name: Over The Top Pita
places.address: Over the Top Pita, 240 Citrus Tower Blvd, Clermont, FL 34711-2704
places.description: Family-run, no-frills counter on Citrus Tower Boulevard in Clermont where every wrap is made to order. The Gyro Pita comes sliced right off the spit, stacked with crisp vegetables and bold sauces until it barely closes, and guests call the gyros among the best in Florida. Great people, great food and great prices is the regulars' refrain, with lamb, Philly cheesesteak and fajita pitas rounding out the board.

places.name: Reunion Resort & Golf Club
places.address: 7593 Gathering Dr, Kissimmee, FL 34747
places.description: Full resort scale in Kissimmee: golf by Palmer, Watson and Nicklaus, a water park with lazy river, tennis and pickleball, plus rooftop Eleven. Guests call it a perfect place to relax with a family atmosphere, a big clean property that has everything you would need. Villa condition can vary from unit to unit, so the golf and the grounds carry the stay.

places.name: Swine & Sons
places.address: 201 N Bumby Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Inside the Milkhouse on Bumby Avenue, Swine & Sons runs a casual sandwich counter with food hall energy and a pop punk playlist. The smash burger is the one guests call killer, while the Nashville Hot Chicken and Chiang Mai hot chicken sandwiches bring the heat and the pastrami holds down the classic end. Curly fries and an Oatmeal Cream Pie finish the order the way regulars do it.

places.name: Foxtail Coffee
places.address: 2401 Curry Ford Rd, Orlando, FL 32806
places.description: Orlando-born chain that still pours like a neighborhood shop, with a peaceful, low-key room in the Hourglass District.
