Cold brew runs serious, with the Vanilla Caramel Cold Brew and Foxtail Original pouring alongside cafe con leche and matcha tea lattes, plus a Chicken Bacon Ranch Crunch Wrap if you are hungry. Guests call it a perfect spot to sit and catch up, with a dog-friendly patio, pup cups, and laptops welcome at the tables.

places.name: First Watch
places.address: 11951 International Drive South Ste A, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: Bright, sunrise-lit room on South International Drive where breakfast is cooked to order and nothing sits under a heat lamp. Guests keep it simple with the Trifecta or go bigger with the Works omelette, Million Dollar Bacon, and lemon ricotta pancakes, with Floridian French toast for the sweet side. Mornings fill with families, and guests credit the smiling staff for the easy atmosphere.

places.name: Le Macaron French Pastries Winter Park
places.address: 216 N Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Tucked into a courtyard off Park Avenue, a jewel-box pastry shop guests call a wonderful little spot. The macarons are delicate and flavorful, salted caramel and pistachio up front, with a Rosa Lychee macaron cake, Napoleons, vanilla eclairs and beignets filling out the case. Add pistachio gelato or an espresso, and do not expect the box to last long: guests say it is gone too fast.

places.name: 1881 Restaurant & Bar
places.address: 1881 Restaurant, 308 Broadway, Kissimmee, FL 34741-5718
places.description: In downtown Kissimmee's historic Makinson Hardware building, old-Florida bones and lively bar energy, and guests say the walls tell the story. The menu runs broader than the building suggests: a Rodeo Burger, mango habanero wings and loaded mac and cheese with pulled pork beside Uzbek touches like fried chuchvara and a mixed grill. Settle onto the patio with a drink, catch the game, and expect a room that leans as much bar as restaurant.

places.name: Dang Boba & Musubi House
places.address: Dang Boba & Musubi House, 11772 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32817-4625
places.description: Cheerful, cozy little spot near UCF pairing boba teas with Hawaiian musubi. The lychee milk tea gets called heavenly by regulars, the Thai tea is brewed in house, and lavender milk tea, tiger tea and princess peach fruit tea fill out the board. On the savory side, spam and kimchi, classic spam and garlic soy chicken musubi make it a meal, served by staff guests describe as super sweet.

places.name: Grape & the Grain
places.address: Grape & the Grain, 1110 Virginia Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Unpretentious Mills 50 wine bar where the real draw is the covered back patio guests call the best in Orlando. Prosecco pours on tap alongside frozen sangria and the Sangria Swirl, charcuterie boards land for the table, and Florida craft beer covers the non-wine crowd. Kind bartenders, good music and a relaxed, welcoming energy make it an easy place to sip and unwind with your people.

places.name: Bento Sushi
places.address: Bento Sushi, 12715 Pegasus Dr, Orlando, FL 32816-8030
places.description: Quick, cafeteria-casual counter inside the UCF Student Union built for grabbing something fresh between classes. Guests go for the salmon poke bowl, spicy Cali bowl, California rolls and chicken gyoza, with bibimbap and chicken donburi for something heartier. Portions run modest, but students call it affordable and friendly, and a favorite stop in the union.

places.name: Juice Bar
places.address: Juice Bar, 2413 E South St, Orlando, FL 32803-6324
places.description: Cute, unpretentious counter on East South Street where everything is pressed and blended in front of you, even the fresh almond mylk. The blend names do the smiling: You're Kale-in It, Hale to the Beet Down, Gangsta Green and Captain Sunshine, alongside smoothies and acai bowls regulars call the best in town. Vegan chia muffins and a zero-pretense room keep the focus where guests want it, on juice that tastes like actual fruit.

places.name: Matt's Latin BBQ
places.address: Matt's Latin BBQ, 6607 S Semoran Blvd, Orlando, FL 32822
places.description: Puerto Rican comfort cooking on South Semoran, cafeteria-style and unpretentious, with decor guests say feels like the island. The mofongo con carne frita is the plate people rave about, next to pernil with rice and beans, juicy rotisserie chicken, morcilla, and a tripleta sandwich. Portions are shareable, the kind of spread guests describe as enough food for days.

places.name: Sly Fox
places.address: Sly Fox, 63 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801-2425
places.description: Gritty, punk-rock dive on North Orange Avenue where the regulars call themselves a built-in family. The basement stage keeps local bands loud, the beer stays cheap, and the kitchen surprises everyone: vegan hot dogs guests call a gift from god, vegan burgers and loaded tater tots. It is warm, unpolished and completely itself, a home base for Orlando's alternative crowd.

places.name: TooJay's
places.address: 2624 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: New York-style deli on Colonial Drive since 1981, with hot pastrami, a corned beef Reuben, blintzes and matzo ball soup guests call the best in town. Portions run generous and service stays fast and friendly, right down to the Rachel 2.0 and the turkey avocado on challah. Leave room for the bakery case, where the coconut cake and the famous Killer Cake rarely let a table leave empty-handed.

places.name: Fujiyama Sushi
places.address: Fujiyama Sushi, 10153 University Blvd, Orlando, FL 32817
places.description: Cozy, casual neighborhood staple on University Blvd where regulars have been coming back for years. The Heaven roll is the one guests single out, with the Volcano, Dancing Eel and Monster rolls giving the board its range, plus salmon nigiri for purists. Guests praise the warm service and reasonable prices, and call it their number one spot for sushi near UCF.

places.name: Lemongrass Thai Kitchen
places.address: Lemongrass Thai Kitchen, 1016 Lockwood Blvd, Oviedo, FL 32765-6027
places.description: Calm and contemporary inside, this Thai kitchen sits in an unassuming Lockwood Boulevard plaza. The Panang duck leads the menu and guests still talk about it months later, joined by whole snapper dinners, lobster phad thai and tamarind shrimp with housemade sauces throughout. Durian ice cream waits for the adventurous.

places.name: Stefano's Trattoria
places.address: Stefano's Trattoria, 1425 Tuskawilla Rd, Winter Springs, FL 32708-4703
places.description: Cozy, old-school Italian dining room tucked into a Tuskawilla Road shopping center, easy to miss and worth finding. Live piano drifts through the room while gnocchi della nonna in pink sauce, lobster ravioli, and veal piccata land in generous portions, with tiramisu cheesecake to finish. Longtime fans still prize it, though recent regulars say the cooking has turned uneven under new ownership.

places.name: White Rabbit Dessert Experience
places.address: White Rabbit Dessert Experience, 875 N Alafaya Trl, Orlando, FL 32828-7049
places.description: Whimsical, Alice in Wonderland themed dessert room in Waterford Lakes where guests say the theme is pure magic. Waffles lead the menu, from the Bad Bunny ube waffle to the Royal Wedding gluten-free waffle a guest called the best gluten free dessert they ever had. The Mad Chocolate, Banana Romance cheesecake and S'Mores Delight sundae keep it indulgent, and guests say it is worth the money.

places.name: Broken Strings Taproom
places.address: Broken Strings Brewery, 1012 W Church St, Orlando, FL 32805-2216
places.description: Music-first taproom on West Church Street, walls covered in murals of legends and a sister brewery sharing the roof. Reborn under new local ownership, it pours playful house beers like Penny Layne strawberry blonde, Purple Mane pale ale, and Liquid Vinyl, while guests single out the sours and the unique IPAs. It is a no-frills neighborhood room, pet friendly, where the pint comes with a stage.

places.name: Clean Eatz
places.address: Clean Eatz, 2205 Orange Ave S, Orlando, FL 32806-3038
places.description: Neat, welcoming health-focused cafe on South Orange Avenue in SoDo, where bowls and wraps keep their macros front and center. Guests single out the Southwest Bison Wrap for big flavor and the Bang Bang Shrimp Wrap for repeat orders, alongside the Clean Eatz Burger and Build A Bowl. Portions run lean by design, which regulars read as part of the trade for food that feels light and intentional.

places.name: Maple Street Biscuit Company
places.address: Maple Street Biscuit Company, 11810 Glass House Ln, Orlando, FL 32836-3794
places.description: Scratch-baked biscuits carry the Southern comfort at this Glass House Lane counter, and guests describe a warm, family vibe. The Squawking Goat stacks fried chicken with fried goat cheese, The Five and Dime and the Smashbrowns arrive under what regulars call heavenly gravy, and bonuts dusted in cinnamon sugar finish things sweetly. Wash it down with a Maple Vanilla Latte and settle into the cheerful, generous room.

places.name: Sushi Yama
places.address: Sushi Yama, 6748 Grand National Dr, Orlando, FL 32819-8526
places.description: All-you-can-eat sushi made fresh to order on Grand National Drive, which guests call the best AYCE spot in Orlando for fish to price. Dragon Rolls, Crazy Yellowtail and Dynamite Rolls anchor the waves of ordering, while hibachi and tempura cheesecake widen the table. The room feels casual and welcoming, suited to groups pacing rounds at different speeds.

places.name: Aloha Hawaiian Kitchen
places.address: Aloha Hawaiian Kitchen, 6125 S Semoran Blvd, Orlando, FL 32822-1500
places.description: Laid-back island counter near the airport serving the plate lunch guests call the best Hawaiian food on the mainland. The Aloha Special stacks crispy pork belly, ono shrimp, and mochiko chicken over rice, with huli huli chicken, loco moco, spam musubi, and a mac salad guests single out. Save room for Alohasadas, filled doughnuts in ube, haupia, and pandan.

places.name: Black Magic Pizza
places.address: Black Magic Pizza, 121 N Bumby Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Punk rock pizza window on Bumby Avenue, playful in name, serious about dough, with basically no seating and parking that fills fast. The pies sit between Neapolitan and New Haven, slightly charred and hand tossed: the Dr. Pepperoni, the Hornets Nest with hot honey and soppressata, the Cheezus and the Tuscan Leather. Vegan pies get the same care as the classics, and regulars call the results some of the best pizza they have had anywhere.

places.name: City Food Hall
places.address: City Food Hall, 1412 Alden Rd, Orlando, FL 32803-1862
places.description: Modern and bustling on Alden Road, chef-driven stalls under one roof so a group can split across smash burgers, sushi, pasta and tacos. Guests love the variety and the yard outside to relax, even as the room can run warm and prices lean high for a food hall. The central bar and the Topgolf Swing Suites upstairs turn a meal into a longer hang.

places.name: Crocante Restaurant
places.address: Crocante Restaurant, 4311 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-5217
places.description: Puerto Rican cooking on East Colonial Drive with a full cocktail bar and a festive take on homestyle flavors. The star in guest after guest's telling is the Roti Kan Kan porchetta, juicy and salty with garlicky green sauce and crunchy skin, served with Mamposteao rice or Crocante rice. Bandeja jibara, alcapurrias, mofongo, and tembleque fill out a table guests call worth the drive.

places.name: Chicken Fire
places.address: Chicken Fire, 2425 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-5018
places.description: No-frills, welcoming hot chicken joint on East Colonial Drive, Nashville style with soul. Hand breaded tenders are fried to order and tossed in heat levels running from gentle Soulful to straight fire, and regulars advise ordering one level milder than you think you want. The Hot Box piles on crinkle fries, coleslaw and Soul Sauce, and guests swear one dip in that sauce makes everything better.

places.name: Kavas Tacos & Tequila
places.address: 9101 International Dr Ste 1198, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Pointe Orlando's loud, colorful taco party, celebratory from the first chips and salsa. Quesabirria tacos arrive dripping with consomme, the three-foot taco board is built for the whole table, and the Kadillac and watermelon margaritas keep pace. Live mariachi takes requests, a fire dancer works the room, and churros close things out sweet.

places.name: Kyuramen X Tbaar- Ucf
places.address: Kyuramen X Tbaar- Ucf, 3402 Technological Ave, Orlando, FL 32817-1402
places.description: Ramen gets a playful stage set near UCF: treehouse-like seating and honeycomb booths that guests say make you feel like Japan. The bowls carry the show, with Tokyo tonkotsu shoyu, Kyushu spicy tonkotsu and a yin-yang bowl pouring two broths side by side, plus pork bao buns and takoyaki to start. Finish with a TBaar bubble tea, matcha pudding or the cherry blossom jelly in a room guests keep calling cozy and one of a kind.

places.name: Lim Ros Thai Restaurant
places.address: Lim Ros Thai Restaurant, 933 Orlando Ave S, Maitland, FL 32751
places.description: Lim Ros, meaning to taste in Thai, serves modern, northern-leaning Thai cooking in an elegant, warm Maitland dining room. The khao soi and crying tiger steak draw steady devotion, and guests describe the flavors as matching the food they grew up eating in Thailand. A full gluten free and vegan menu widens the table, with butterfly pea tea lemonade to drink.

places.name: Oza Izakaya
places.address: Oza Izakaya, 5310 Central Florida Pkwy, Orlando, FL 32821-8772
places.description: Sleek, garden-like Japanese room on Central Florida Parkway, beautiful and unhurried in a way that suits a date night. Small plates are built for sharing: yuzu hamachi, buttery uni toast, wagyu gyoza with truffle, grilled octopus with yuzu foam and miso yaki cod. Regulars praise the spot-on consistency, and more than one guest ranks the food among the best Japanese they have had in any major city.

places.name: Smokey Jay's BBQ
places.address: Smokey Jay's BBQ, 9318 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32817-4100
places.description: Mom-and-pop smokehouse on East Colonial where guests say you can taste the family-run care in every plate. The brisket comes tender and seasoned through, the ribs and pulled pork arrive in generous portions, and the Smoke House loaded fries pile the pit onto one plate. Mac and cheese, collard greens and candied yams round out the tray, with red velvet cake or pound cake waiting at the end.

places.name: Sushi Pop
places.address: Sushi Pop, 310 W Mitchell Hammock Rd, Oviedo, FL 32765-4921
places.description: Bold, loud sushi room with anime pop-culture decor, run like an artist's studio. Seasonal crudo, nikkei maki and buffalo rock shrimp show the range, and the nigiri earns melt-in-your-mouth praise from regulars. Rolls run pricey and the room packs out, so book ahead.

places.name: Ten10 Brewing
places.address: Ten10 Brewing, 1010 Virginia Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-2532
places.description: Laid-back neighborhood taproom on Virginia Drive in Mills 50, all about good beer, good tunes and good people. The self-styled DIY punk rock brew crew pours the Grandmas Purse butterscotch ale alongside IPAs like Chronically Mismanaged and East West, with a kitchen turning out Big Green Egg smoked wings and pretzels with beer cheese. Music spins without drowning out conversation, the patio welcomes dogs, and the room feels like a community hangout more than a bar.

places.name: The Escobar Kitchen
places.address: The Escobar Kitchen, 420 E Church St, Orlando, FL 32801-2775
places.description: Family-run sushi inside a wine shop on East Church Street, rolling Latin-flavored rolls regulars say they dream about. The Escobar Roll stacks shrimp tempura, churrasco, and sweet plantains, and the Paisa Roll earns the same devotion from repeat visitors. Small, chill, and full of bold flavor, it is a neighborhood staple for anyone who wants sushi with a twist.

places.name: TT Crepes
places.address: TT Crepes, 10681 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32817-4470
places.description: Inside Mei Supermarket on East Colonial, a small counter built around jianbing, the crisp, egg-laced Chinese street crepe. Scallion pancakes come off the griddle beside it, and the short menu keeps the focus on crunch, egg and scallion.

places.name: Vinia Wine & Kitchen
places.address: Vinia Wine & Kitchen, 444 W New England Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789-4224
places.description: Dinner feels like a welcome home: small, low-lit room in Hannibal Square, a boutique wine list, plates from Italy and Brazil. The braised oxtail gnocchi and the Romeu & Julieta cheese bread with guava sauce are the dishes guests name most, and the kitchen gives vegetables the same care, with vegan escargot and a beet wellington. Guests describe the result as the best meal they have had since moving to Orlando, romantic and unhurried.

places.name: AJ Chocolate House
places.address: AJ Chocolate House, 552 S Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789-4322, United States
places.description: Old-world Europe lands on Park Avenue here, with low lighting, cozy elegance, and chocolate treated as an occasion. The fondue comes piled with fresh fruit and smooth, decadent chocolate, and guests call the Belgian hot chocolate the best they have ever had. Brussels waffles, a three-tier tea tower and pistachio cheesecake round out a menu built for lingering.

places.name: Boku Sushi
places.address: Boku Sushi, 140 Independence Ln, Maitland, FL 32751-5603, United States
places.description: Calm and inviting behind warm wood and stone, this is the Maitland sushi room neighbors fold into their routine. Rolls like the Drama Queen, the Foxy Lady, and the Out of Control arrive fresh and carefully crafted, alongside grilled sea bass one guest called CRAZY good and a jalapeño hamachi people order by name. The pet-friendly patio keeps the whole meal easy, the kind of spot neighbors fold into their routine.

places.name: Schakolad Chocolate Factory
places.address: Schakolad Chocolate Factory, 9901 Hawaiian Ct, Orlando, FL 32819-8102, United States
places.description: Old-world chocolaterie on Hawaiian Court, where European-style chocolates are made fresh right on the premises. The cases hold signature truffles, hand-dipped fruits and chocolate-covered strawberries, plus molded novelties and sugar-free picks, and you can build your own box to take home. Guests call it a chocolate lover's paradise, and the hands-on Sweet Night Out events let you make and decorate your own.

places.name: Half Barrel Beer Project
places.address: Half Barrel Beer Project, 9650 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819-8766, United States
places.description: Small, family-owned brewery on Universal Boulevard with a chill, welcoming feel guests keep mentioning. Sours lead the praise, including Put the Lime in the Coconut and Starburst sours, poured alongside flights for browsing the taps. A giant pretzel with beer cheese, cheese curds, pulled chicken nachos and fall off the bone wings give the taproom its neighborhood food following.

places.name: Mario's Pizza
places.address: Mario's Pizza, 7213 Curry Ford Rd, Orlando, FL 32822-5805, United States
places.description: Family-run on Curry Ford Road, where guests say the pies taste like real pizza from New York. The Girlfriend, half pizza and half calzone, anchors the menu alongside garlic knots, pepperoni rolls, and baked ziti with meatballs, plus a ranch guests insist you try with your slice. The vegan side is a draw of its own, from the vegan Buffalo chicken pizza to vegan pepperoni the kids ask for, and the owner still comes out to talk with the tables.

places.name: Pienezza Pizza
places.address: Pienezza Pizza, 3236 N John Young Pkwy, Kissimmee, FL 34741-7549, United States
places.description: Family-run and no-frills on John Young Parkway in Kissimmee, where regulars say the Grandma pie brings it home. Guests call the slices as close to an authentic New York slice as you will find around here, crisp with a great undercarriage, and the Hey Brooklyn, Crazy Margherita and Sicilian Flag give the menu its Brooklyn accent. Garlic knots and cannoli round it out, though some regulars find the pies a touch greasy and the tangy sauce divides the table.

places.name: San Julian's Coffee
places.address: San Julian's Coffee, 110 S Orlando Ave Ste 4, Winter Park, FL 32789-3656, United States
places.description: Cozy Colombian coffee bar on Orlando Avenue, pouring rich, strong coffee and an iced pistachio latte with a devoted following. The tiramisu latte, Campesino coffee and jugo de maracuya pour alongside a true taste of Colombia: tequenos, cheese empanadas, pandebono and guava and cheese quesitos. Guests get introduced to the tequenos once and come back hooked.

places.name: Sushi Lola's
places.address: 2902 Corrine Dr, Orlando, FL 32803, United States
places.description: On Corrine Drive, owner Aaron Pak runs Japanese and Korean kitchens, so a Playboy Roll can sit beside dolsot bibimbap. Guests call it a hidden gem in the Audubon Park area, pointing to the Lava Dips, the Volcano and Spider rolls, kimchi pancakes and bulgogi, and service regulars describe as top notch. Dessert comes as a warm browned butter cookie, on the house.

places.name: Aji Ceviche Bar Casselberry
places.address: Aji Ceviche Bar Casselberry, 1436 State Road 436, Casselberry, FL 32707-6506, United States
places.description: Bright and unpretentious on State Road 436 in Casselberry, a Peruvian ceviche bar built on lime, heat, and fresh fish. Guests order the ceviche clásico and the Carretilla, drink the leche de tigre straight, and chase it with lomo saltado, crispy chicharrón de pescado, and a proper pisco sour. More than one diner says it brought back the ceviche they had in Peru, and Peruvian friends have approved it.

places.name: Hinode Sushi
places.address: Hinode Sushi, 1016 Lockwood Blvd, Oviedo, FL 32765-6027, United States
places.description: Locals call this Oviedo room their own: a warm, family-run counter on Lockwood Blvd where Chef George Tan plates sushi with artistry. The Trio Tower stacks tuna, salmon, yellowtail, mango and avocado; the Black Widow rolls out under a spiderweb of sauce; even the avocado fries arrive looking sculpted. Guests call it the most delicious sushi they have ever had, and regulars who come for the spicy salmon lunch special keep calling it their favorite in the area. Everything is made to order, so a busy room runs at its own unhurried pace.

places.name: Ollie's Public House
places.address: Ollie's Public House, 3400 Edgewater Dr, Orlando, FL 32804-3602, United States
places.description: Easy neighborhood-pub rhythm on Edgewater Drive, with a lively dog-friendly patio and rotating craft taps. The Legend sandwich and the Wall Street Reuben anchor a deep bar food menu that also hides Finnhenry's Buffalo Chicken Wrap and a chocolate espresso martini. Service can slow when the room fills, but the unpretentious buzz keeps people coming back.

places.name: Tropico Mofongo
places.address: Tropico Mofongo, 3160 Vineland Rd, Kissimmee, FL 34746-4657, United States
places.description: Bright and cheerful in Kissimmee, built around Puerto Rican mofongo of plantain, chicharron, and garlic, like a grandmother's cooking. Order it under pernil, with shrimp al ajillo, or go for the Mofongo Trio, and expect portions big enough to share or take home. The wait can stretch a little, but regulars say the mofongo makes up for it.

places.name: Bad AS's Sandwich
places.address: Bad AS's Sandwich, 207 N Primrose Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-5819, United States
places.description: Intimate, quirky counter on Primrose Drive in the Milk District, making everything in house from bread to pickles and ranch. The sandwiches arrive overfilled to the point of struggling to eat them: the Ninja with Asian glazed pork belly, the Mr. 305 Cuban, the Steakhouse and the Ya-Mon jerk chicken. House made kettle chips and guava pastries ride along, and regulars call the place a genuine hidden gem.

places.name: Dali's Lao Thai Cafe
places.address: Dali's Lao Thai Cafe, 1181 Rinehart Rd, Sanford, FL 32771-7390, United States
places.description: Family-run in Sanford, cooking Lao and Thai food on Rinehart Road with care and fresh ingredients. Portions run generous, and regulars come back for pad thai, papaya salad, and pad see ew with a clean, balanced heat. Try the Lao sausage with sticky rice and jaew bong, the red curry chicken noodle soup, or curry beef empanadas, and save room for mango sticky rice and purple lemonade.

places.name: Taqueria las Cazuelas
places.address: Taqueria las Cazuelas, 10360 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32817-4364, United States
places.description: No-frills and home-style on East Colonial, the taco outpost of the Las Cazuelas family, with portions that are famously not shy. Tacos arrive packed with meat, birria, carne asada, al pastor and carnitas, with cilantro, onion and lime set to the side so you can dress them your way. Save room for the flan, which regulars call the best on this side of Orlando.

places.name: Agave Azul Cocina Mexicana
places.address: Agave Azul Cocina Mexicana, 5475 Gateway Village Cir, Orlando, FL 32812-4002, United States
places.description: The Mexican dining room at Gateway Village near the airport is loud, festive and high-energy, immaculate with a lot going on. Birria tacos, the Oaxaca Lava molcajete, smoky churrasco, and queso fundido with chorizo carry the kitchen, and the Night in Tulum margarita carries the bar. Portions run big, the kind of plates guests end up taking home.

places.name: Delaney's Tavern
places.address: Delaney's Tavern, 1315 S Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32806, United States
places.description: Warm and stylish on the ground floor of the Delaney Hotel in SoDo, the room the neighborhood saves for special occasions. The farm-to-fork New American menu runs from blue crab beignets and she crab soup to an almond garlic crusted salmon and the Wagyu Yes Chef burger. Guests rave about the dirty martini, one calling it perhaps the best they have ever had, and the welcome feels instant.

places.name: Knife Burger
places.address: Knife Burger, 4040 Central Florida Pkwy, Orlando, FL 32837-7662, United States
places.description: Chef John Tesar's poolside stand at the JW Marriott Grande Lakes, where swimsuits pass and beef gets steakhouse respect. The sirloin patties come off the grill the way guests like them, in builds like The Ozersky, the Double Ozersky, and The Magic on an English muffin with bacon. A mahi mahi sandwich covers the non-burger order, and the whole setup stays laid-back and open-air.

places.name: Uncle Tony's Backyard BBQ Orlando
places.address: Uncle Tony's Backyard BBQ Orlando, 6807 S Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32809-6025, United States
places.description: Hole-in-the-wall on South Orange Avenue with a small-town feel that makes you forget you are in a big city. Brisket and dino beef ribs lead, with Brisket Birria Tacos and the Mac Daddy Burger showing the kitchen's playful side, and a sweet vinegar barbecue sauce guests call worth the trip alone. The sides are no afterthought here; the mac and cheese is the one guests say stays on their mind.

places.name: Beirut Grill and Deli
places.address: Beirut Grill and Deli, 3100 Alafaya Trl, Oviedo, FL 32765-9466, United States
places.description: Family-owned halal Lebanese kitchen on Alafaya Trail, where everything tastes homemade and the room feels like family. Guests rave over the beef shawarma and the creamy hummus, which one regular calls the best in Central Florida. The chicken shawarma sandwich, falafel and fried kibbeh arrive generous and fresh, and regulars tell newcomers to save room for kenefeh.

places.name: Domu Chibi Ramen
places.address: Domu Chibi Ramen, 869 N Alafaya Trl, Orlando, FL 32828-7049, United States
places.description: Ramen craft from DOMU comes to Waterford Lakes in a modern, anime-leaning room where you order at a kiosk and bowls move fast. Tonkotsu, shoyu and coconut curry ramen anchor the menu, the fried garlic on the shoyu gets singled out, and the signature boneless wing bites come crispy and sweet. Guests call it a step up from the usual fast food pace, super clean and easy to order, with portions that do not skimp.

places.name: The Goblin Market Restaurant
places.address: The Goblin Market Restaurant, 330 Dora Drawdy Way, Mt Dora, FL 32757-5593, United States
places.description: Mount Dora's storybook gastropub, a cozy book-lined hideaway on Dora Drawdy Way where guests love being surrounded by books. Regulars insist you have to have the Irish Whiskey Onion Soup, followed by the crab and lobster bisque, the Irish Cheddar Burger or a strawberry salmon salad praised as fresh and generous. The secret-garden courtyard under the camphor tree turns the room romantic, and while prices run high, nobody seems in a hurry to leave.

places.name: Henry's Depot
places.address: Henry's Depot, 212 W 1st St, Sanford, FL 32771-1204, United States
places.description: Sanford's historic Plant depot on West 1st Street is now an open-air food hall with something for everyone. Order Yugiri Ramen Project's Spicy Tonkotsu, Chin's Korean corn dogs, or a Sweet and Salty chicken sandwich, then finish with Greenery Creamery ice cream. Groups spread out, compare plates, and settle into the relaxed, family friendly space while The Basin pours craft cocktails and Mahogany serves coffee.

places.name: Hollerbach's German Market
places.address: 117 Magnolia Ave, Sanford, FL 32771
places.description: On Magnolia Avenue in Sanford, stocked with imported German pantry goods, Milka chocolate, Haribo, plus a full deli and bakery. Guests call it an underrated gem with a festive, laid back feel, and the Reubenstein with red cabbage earns repeat orders. Add a warm pretzel with spicy mustard, apple strudel or Black Forest cake, and a Speculoos Cookie Butter Coffee that guests say tastes like heaven and fall in a cup.

places.name: Indian Pavilion
places.address: Indian Pavilion, 13770 W Colonial Dr, Winter Garden, FL 34787-4202, United States
places.description: Modern Indian cooking in Winter Garden built on bold spice and careful texture, with portions that often leave leftovers. Garlic naan arrives with real quality, alongside Paneer Makhani with plenty of paneer, Old Delhi butter chicken, chicken tikka masala, and chicken biryani. Regulars point to consistency as its hallmark, the flavor and quality they want from a good Indian restaurant.

places.name: Jeni's Splendid Ice Creams
places.address: 510 N Orlando Ave #102, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Inventive, scratch-made scoops on Orlando Avenue, and guests insist you can really taste the difference. Brambleberry Crisp, Brown Butter Almond Brittle, Darkest Chocolate and Salty Caramel stack into a Buttercrisp waffle cone with pie-crust crunch, and the staff happily steer you to the right flavor. Portions run small for the price, a tradeoff fans of the flavors keep making.

places.name: Lazy Dog
places.address: 8019 W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy, Kissimmee, FL 34747
places.description: Cozy, lodge-style cabin feel on 192 in Kissimmee, relaxed and family-friendly, with a dog menu out on the patio. The comfort food runs from firecracker shrimp and crispy deviled eggs to the bison burger and campfire pot roast, with mountain berry cheesecake to finish. Service can slow down when the room fills up, but regulars call it their place to go for comfort food.

places.name: Linda's La Cantina Steakhouse
places.address: Linda's la Cantina, 4721 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-4305, United States
places.description: Serving steaks on East Colonial since 1947, a family-run old-school room with checkered tablecloths, a step back in time. The kitchen keeps the classics coming, bacon wrapped filet mignon, Porterhouse and T-bone, baked French onion soup, bourbon shrimp, and coconut custard pie to finish. Regulars praise amazing steaks at amazing prices in a room that stays packed, lively, and unmistakably an Orlando staple.

places.name: Maitland Social
places.address: Maitland Social, 360 E Horatio Ave, Maitland, FL 32751-4517, United States
places.description: Locals treat this food hall like a neighborhood living room, made for lingering with friends. Indoor and outdoor spaces gather friends around stalls like Wave Sushi with its sushi crunch wrap and enormous mozzarella sticks, plus Foxtail Coffee and garlic knots guests keep mentioning. One visit pulls you from stall to stall, and the whole corridor feels built for lingering.

places.name: Mikado
places.address: Mikado, 6417 Raleigh St, Orlando, FL 32835-5739, United States
places.description: Unassuming room on Raleigh Street in Metrowest, and the sashimi is why guests keep coming back. Cuts arrive large, tender, and ultra fresh, from toro and yellowtail to Scottish salmon and unagi, with the omakase, the Mikado Roll, and buttery uni toast as the standing orders. Cozy and old-school, it is the quiet room locals name when only real sushi will do.

places.name: Sea Thai Restaurant
places.address: Sea Thai Restaurant, 3812 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-5208, United States
places.description: Tucked into a strip mall on East Colonial, cozy and unhurried, with jazz and bossa nova and summer rolls with peanut sauce. Regulars swear by the Prik King soft shell crab with Thai fried rice, alongside basil fried rice with crispy duck, shrimp toast, and rich Panang and massaman curries. Guests describe it as a neighborhood hidden gem, the kind of place people return to for familiar flavors and friendly check ins.

places.name: Soulicious Vegan Kitchen
places.address: Soulicious Vegan Kitchen, 15 E 5th St, Apopka, FL 32703-5244, United States
places.description: Inside Apopka's Halls On 5th, vegan soul food with no compromise: fried oyster mushroom chick'n, sliders, and mac and cheese. Guests talk about mushrooms that tear apart in your mouth and an Oreo cheesecake one diner called the best they had ever had. Portions run modest for the price, but the seasoning is the point, and skeptics at the table tend to convert.

places.name: Sunshine Soulfood Cafe
places.address: Sunshine Soulfood Cafe, 2528 W Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32804-8009, United States
places.description: Soul food with a Caribbean lean on West Colonial, cooked like home: oxtails off the bone, fried chicken, mac and cheese, cornbread. Guests use words like homey and no-fuss, and more than one says the plate reminded them of home. Service can be uneven, but the portions are generous and the pineapple lemonade is worth adding.

places.name: Tactical Brewing Company
places.address: Tactical Brewing Company, 4882 New Broad St, Orlando, FL 32814-6628, United States
places.description: Veteran-founded brewery on New Broad Street in Baldwin Park, pouring with a playful streak, especially in its sours. Guests linger over the pho inspired Gose PhoSho, watermelon sour, and Night Post with its clear caramel and apple notes, in a taproom that feels laid back and living room easy. Star Wars murals, a wall of military patches and challenge coins, and staff who happily pour tastes to help you choose give it a neighborhood hangout feel.

places.name: The Jersey Spot Pizza and Pasta
places.address: The Jersey Spot Pizza and Pasta, 1137 W Columbia Ave, Kissimmee, FL 34741-3202, United States
places.description: Small, family-run Kissimmee joint on Columbia Avenue serving thin-crust, New Jersey-style pies transplants say taste like home. The Jersey Classic cheese pizza leads, with garlic knots, a pork roll sandwich and penne alla vodka rounding out the comfort menu, and guests praise the shrimp scampi pasta too. Portions are generous, prices are kind, and regulars call it their comfort food fix.

places.name: The Salty Donut
places.address: The Salty Donut, 11585 Regency Village Dr, Orlando, FL 32821, United States
places.description: At Vineland Pointe, the donut case is treated like a pastry case, cute and bright with an artisanal streak. Brown Butter & Salt, Butterbeer and cherry pie donuts share space with an Everything cragel and hot honey ricotta toast, and guests say the blueberry tastes like the best blueberry muffin. The Cinnamon Cereal Milk Latte is the pour regulars call a must, in a room made for lingering.

places.name: Tikka Shack Indian Grub
places.address: Tikka Shack Indian Grub, 1500 Alafaya Trl, Oviedo, FL 32765-4517, United States
places.description: Fast-casual Indian kitchen on Alafaya Trail that keeps flavors bold and the mood fun and casual. Regulars say Tikka Shack never misses, singling out the masala fries and the butter masala, ordered extra hot when they want heat. The tandoori chicken pizza lands on a naan crust, and the garlic naan gets described by guests as fluffy, soft and chewy.

places.name: Toll Road Brewing Company
places.address: Toll Road Brewing Company, 101 W McKey St, Ocoee, FL 34761-2616, United States
places.description: Small Ocoee taproom with a cozy, laid-back microbrewery feel, staffed by people who treat everyone like a regular. The taps pour house brews like a Pina Colada Cream Ale and a Japanese Rice Lager, food trucks rotate through, and you can bring in your own food when they do not. Live music and a totally chill vibe make it feel like a hometown hangout rather than a destination brewery.

places.name: Twenty Pho Hour
places.address: 11951 International Dr Ste B-2, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: Black-and-white ink lines wrap this International Drive room, a playful comic-book space guests compare to a music video. The pho is the real draw: rich, clean broths under short rib or crispy pork belly, with guests calling the broth heavenly and among the best they have tried in the area. Kimchi fries, Korean fire noodles and taro churro bites keep the table busy between bowls.

places.name: Vivoli Il Gelato
places.address: Vivoli Il Gelato, 1638 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830, United States
places.description: A Florentine gelateria at Disney Springs, old-world and creamy in a way guests call authentic. The affogato absolutely delivers, the signature cannoli and tiramisu hold their own, and one guest called it the best gelato her daughter has ever had. Expect a line when the complex is busy, and know some flavors run sweet, the sorbets especially.

places.name: Brooklyn Water Bagel
places.address: Brooklyn Water Bagel, 9368 Narcoossee Rd, Orlando, FL 32827-5701, United States
places.description: On Narcoossee Road in Lake Nona, bagels are boiled and baked New York style, with the water treated to mimic back home. Transplants say the result tastes just like a NY bagel: soft, fresh, and generously sized, stacked into sandwiches like the Greenpoint and a corned beef reuben. The order regulars defend is the Cubsta, iced coffee poured over coffee ice cubes so it never waters down.

places.name: The Wilson
places.address: The Wilson, 225 Celebration Pl, Kissimmee, FL 34747-4601, United States
places.description: Polished, poolside coastal bistro inside the Meliá Orlando Celebration, with a relaxed elegance guests call a cut above. The New Yorker Burger and stone-oven Margherita pizza headline a menu that also runs to a tuna poke bowl and a lobster BLT, with an espresso martini at the bar. Guests come in for a drink and stay for the hospitality, praising service that makes the whole visit.

places.name: Island Thyme
places.address: Island Thyme, 457 Avalon Park South Blvd, Orlando, FL 32828-6700, United States
places.description: Virgin Islands cooking in Avalon Park, family-run and relaxed, with plates guests call flavorful and well seasoned. The jerk chicken lands on point, the braised oxtail comes off the bone, and the stew chicken with sweet, softly crisped plantain has its own following. Rice and peas, mac and cheese, and coconut shrimp round out a menu that tastes like it came from someone's home kitchen.

places.name: Premium Matcha Cafe Maiko
places.address: Premium Matcha Cafe Maiko, 639 Mills Ave N, Orlando, FL 32803-4640, United States
places.description: Cute, cozy counter on Mills Ave devoted to real matcha, whisked to order. Guests call the matcha lattes some of the best in town, and the banana pudding matcha latte has become a signature, joined by matcha soft serve, ube soft serve and the Maiko Special parfait. Taiyaki warm from the griddle and Uji-Kintoki shaved ice keep it feeling like a calm little ritual in the middle of Mills 50.

places.name: Schweini's Delicatessen
places.address: Schweini's Delicatessen, 108 S Main St, Winter Garden, FL 34787-3556, United States
places.description: A German deli on Main Street in Winter Garden, built straight from the owner's heart. Chris Frommeyer pounds schnitzel thin, breads it, and stacks it on pretzel rolls with lingonberry compote, pickled red cabbage, and horseradish that wakes you up kindly. The Die Behrens, a pork schnitzel sandwich with real swagger, is the order. German beers pour cold, soccer plays on screens, and your dog is welcome on the patio. Choose Schweini's when you want to arrive hungry and leave grinning after a sandwich with crunch, tang, and lift.

places.name: Take A Sushi
places.address: 4725 W Sand Lake Rd #101, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Japanese cooking gets a Latin twist on Sand Lake Road, sunny, breezy, and unpretentious. The Mayorquina arrives crowned with ceviche, the Godzilla roll comes tempura-fried and hefty, and sushi burritos and the Krab Bomb keep the table playful. Guests call it fresh cuts and serious sushi, the kind of place you leave with no regrets.

places.name: Imperial Wine Bar
places.address: Imperial, 1800 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32804-6415, United States
places.description: Inside a vintage furniture store on North Orange Avenue sits Ivanhoe Village's wine bar, Imperial. Boutique wines and a craft beer list pair with small plates built for lingering: a duck sandwich, baked brie, charcuterie and shrimp tacos. The back patio is the move, a courtyard guests rank among the best in the village, with live jazz drifting through.

places.name: Sus Hi Eatstation
places.address: Sus Hi Eatstation, 9680 Narcoossee Rd, Orlando, FL 32827-7311, United States
places.description: Playful, ninja-themed counter in Lake Nona where you build your own sushi bowl, roll, or burrito exactly how you like it. The headline build is the Fry Me A River, a tempura-fried sushi burrito that lands crispy and over the top, and portions run huge enough that half a bowl often goes home with you. Everything tastes fresh, the room stays upbeat and quick, and the ube cheesecake is worth saving room for.

places.name: Volcano Hot Pot & BBQ
places.address: Volcano Hot Pot & BBQ, 3279 Daniels Rd Suite 102, Winter Garden, FL 34787, United States
places.description: On Daniels Road in Winter Garden, a bubbling hot pot and a Korean BBQ grill share the same table, so you cook each bite your way. The all you can eat spread runs large, with seafood including crab, sliced prime brisket, meats, vegetables, and udon noodles to slide into the broth. Guests call it their favorite spot for Korean BBQ, a lively, hands on room with good vibes built for groups sharing plates.

places.name: Buster's Bistro
places.address: 300 S Sanford Ave, Sanford, FL 32771
places.description: On Sanford Avenue, Belgian Trappist ales and lambics pour in proper glassware, in a cozy room regulars compare to a living room. Dogs are welcome, and the room stays comfy and lively without losing its neighborhood ease. Order the French dip, truffle frites, and poutine, or settle into shepherd's pie, croque monsieur, and short rib carbonnade.

places.name: Deeply Coffee
places.address: Deeply Coffee, 111 N Magnolia Ave, Orlando, FL 32801-2304, United States
places.description: A few steps off Magnolia downtown, a bright, minimalist room where the vibe stays chill and soothing. Espresso and pour overs share the counter with the matchas guests rave about, the blueberry matcha latte and seasonal versions with blackberry or sweet rice, all with house made syrups. Laptops and dogs settle in easily, and a wall of natural wines waits in the bottle shop.

places.name: King O Falafel
places.address: King O Falafel, 5045 W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy, Kissimmee, FL 34746-5345, United States
places.description: Family-owned Kissimmee storefront on 192 since 2009, unassuming outside and all flavor inside. The combination platter and chicken kabob lead, with falafel sandwiches, red lentil soup and a fresh Lebanese salad, plus pistachio baklava or kinafeh to finish. Guests call it the best Mediterranean and Lebanese food in town and say it has never disappointed them.

places.name: The Current Seafood Counter-Sanford
places.address: 116 E 1st St, Sanford, FL 32771
places.description: Started inside Henry's Depot, now serving a casual slice of New England on East 1st Street in Sanford. Guests praise consistently high quality food and friendly service, with blackened mahi and salmon sandwiches leading the counter. Try both lobster roll styles, New England and Connecticut, plus clam chowder, a grouper sandwich, and the fabulous hush puppies guests name again and again.

places.name: Bakery 1908
places.address: Bakery 1908, 12399 S Apopka Vineland Rd, Orlando, FL 32836, United States
places.description: Second location of the Asian bakery whose original sits on East Colonial, this one on South Apopka Vineland Road in Orlando. This location adds a noodle bar serving ramen and pho alongside the bakery offer.

places.name: Cavo's Bar & Kitchen
places.address: Cavo's Bar & Kitchen, 900 E Washington St, Orlando, FL 32801-2906, United States
places.description: On East Washington, Thornton Park's sports bar is Eagles country, where Philly fans gather and the cheesesteak earns loud praise. Regulars call the Philly one of the best they have ever had, stacked with shaved steak and molten cheese, while roast pork sandwiches, arancini, and French onion soup give the menu range beyond game day. Lively without tipping into chaos, it is a relaxed room for a long afternoon of food and drinks.

places.name: KURA SUSHI
places.address: KURA SUSHI, 11579 Regency Village Dr, Orlando, FL 32821, United States
places.description: Sushi becomes a game at Vineland Pointe, with plates gliding on a revolving belt and a robot delivering drinks. The Crispy Rice with Spicy Tuna stays crisp, the Tempura Philadelphia Roll and Spider Hand Roll draw repeat orders, and stacking finished plates feeds the Bikkura Pon prize game. Regulars call the fish so fresh and say the place never disappoints.

places.name: Rockpit Brewing
places.address: Rockpit Brewing, 10 W Illiana St, Orlando, FL 32806-4408, United States
places.description: Regulars treat this SoDo taproom on West Illiana Street as Orlando's neighborhood brewery, cozy and welcoming to newcomers. The board moves from SoDo Blondin to Mustache Ride red ale and Blackstrap con Leche milk stout, with Paul's Fault cinnamon vanilla moonshine poured for flights. Cecil's barbecue arrives at the tables, dogs settle in, and live music keeps the room feeling like a second living room.

places.name: YH Seafood Clubhouse
places.address: YH Seafood Clubhouse, 8081 Turkey Lake Rd, Orlando, FL 32819-7321, United States
places.description: Turkey Lake Road's Cantonese room, refined and warm, where round tables fill with family-style plates. Dim sum comes ordered from a check-off menu, black truffle siu mai and crystal shrimp har gow, alongside Peking duck two ways, salt and pepper calamari and golden XO fried rice. Regulars call it the best dim sum they have found in Florida and come back for the hot and sour soup, the fish and the lobster.

places.name: Barkhaven
places.address: Barkhaven, 724 Brookhaven Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-2505, United States
places.description: Playful and dog-obsessed on Brookhaven Drive, pairing a supervised off-leash park and splash zone with a full restaurant and bar. The kitchen goes beyond the expected with guava wings, the BH brisket bratwurst, and the Big Rich burger, plus pup cups and a dog menu of their own. Guests say their dogs leave happily worn out, and the cocktails, including the Raise the Woof old fashioned and BarkHaven IPA, give the humans a real reason to stay.

places.name: Beth's Burger Bar
places.address: Beth's Burger Bar, 9938 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819-8702, United States
places.description: Old-school diner feel on Universal Boulevard, built around build-your-own burgers from patty to last pickle. Guests call the burgers absolutely legit, fresh and hot with a perfect sear, whether the classic Western or the wilder Peanut Butter Burger and Mac and Cheese Burger. Garlic parm fries and onion rings seasoned just right finish the playful, neighborhood table.

places.name: Blue Amphora
places.address: Blue Amphora, 1461 N Goldenrod Rd, Orlando, FL 32807-8301, United States
places.description: Welcoming and sparkling clean on North Goldenrod Road, a Turkish bakery where the case centers on baklava. Guests rave about pistachio baklava with crisp layers, fresh pistachio, and syrup that does not overpower, alongside walnut baklava, kanafah, cheese and beef borek, and simit. Turkish coffee and tea round out a stop that regulars describe as a true Turkish taste, with staff known to share a sample while you decide.

places.name: Burger Vault
places.address: Burger Vault, 520 W State Road 436, Altamonte Springs, FL 32714-4000, United States
places.description: Small mom-and-pop counter on State Road 436 in Altamonte Springs, building halal burgers guests call juicy and wonderfully messy. The Vault Burger is the regulars' order, the Volcano Burger brings the heat, and the seasoned fries want a side of vault sauce for dipping. A pistachio shake cools things down, and the whole place runs clean, friendly, and unhurried.

places.name: Corner Chophouse
places.address: Corner Chophouse, 558 W New England Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789-4125, United States
places.description: Just off Park Avenue in Hannibal Square, a warm, prohibition-styled steakhouse that gets better as the lights go down, guests say. Dry-aged ribeye, beef cheek and beef carpaccio anchor the menu, fluffy milk bread with salted European butter opens the table, and the dessert trolley rolls through to general delight. Service draws the word impeccable again and again, with martinis keeping the celebration going.

places.name: The Current Seafood Counter
places.address: The Current Seafood Counter, 2425 Edgewater Dr, Orlando, FL 32804-5303, United States
places.description: New England fish shack spirit comes to College Park, with counter-service ease and a clean, casual room. The lobster rolls come New England and Connecticut style, the blackened mahi sandwich gets weekly repeat devotion, and Old Bay fries with malt vinegar round out the cold water comfort. Guests call it some of the best seafood in Orlando, and the short, direct menu makes it easy to see why.

places.name: 480N Wine Bar
places.address: 480 N Orlando Ave Ste 133, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Reborn from Flutes Champagne Bar in Winter Park Village, a chic, moody lounge with a Parisian streak. Wine-based cocktails, a strong champagne selection and cheeseboards carry the drink list, and the music keeps the room feeling current rather than ceremonial. Guests come for good vibes and good drinks, date nights and girls nights alike, and Latin nights with DJ Leony call for dancing shoes.

places.name: Hot Asian Buns
places.address: 204 S Sanford Ave, Sanford, FL
places.description: Started as a Sanford food truck, now a brick-and-mortar on South Sanford Avenue where every bao is handmade from scratch. The steamed buns come out pillowy and tender, filled with Korean fried chicken, beef bulgogi, or lacquered pork belly. Guests call them melt in your mouth good, and the loaded kimchi fries and double fried chicken wings round out the table.

places.name: Lake Meadow Naturals
places.address: Lake Meadow Naturals, 10000 Mark Adam Rd, Ocoee, FL 34761-3246, United States
places.description: Working farm in Ocoee whose store sells what the land makes: eggs you pick yourself, uncured bacon, turkeys raised on site. Guests call the setting tranquil, a little bit of paradise, and swear you can taste the difference in everything. Bring a cooler, because the frozen cases are where the good stuff waits.

places.name: Lineage Coffee Roasting
places.address: 3201 Corrine Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-2224, United States
places.description: Tucked in the back of East End Market, a working roastery where the cup shows the craft, from flat whites to cold brew. Guests call it the best hidden coffee shop in the market, with a welcoming, refreshingly authentic feel. Its origins go back to 2012, when the husband and wife founders started roasting in Orlando on a retrofitted grill.

places.name: Nuri's
places.address: Nuri's, 63 E Pine St, Orlando, FL 32801-2617, United States
places.description: Downtown's tavern-style pizza joint on East Pine, all cracker-crisp, paper-thin crust party-cut into squares you keep grabbing. The pepperoni and jalapeno pie with chili crisp and homemade ranch drizzle headlines, the vodka pizza converts skeptics, and some guests call it the best pizza in Orlando right now. Pinball machines and projectors keep the room lively, and pistachio soft serve closes the meal.

places.name: Qreate Coffee
places.address: 1212 Woodward St #1, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Just off Mills on Woodward Street, part coffee lab and part creative studio, with a small-town feel guests do not expect. The menu leans inventive: a Crème Brûlée Latte, the Purple Pearl ube latte, a Tiger Latte and a lavender lemonade guests call super refreshing, plus Korean cream cheese garlic bread that earns repeat orders. Staff remember regulars by name and drink, and the quiet, clean room with a plug for everyone suits laptops and lingering alike.

places.name: Sourdough Bread House
places.address: Sourdough Bread House, 5761 US-17-92, Casselberry, FL 32707-3819, United States
places.description: Cozy, family-owned Turkish bakery cafe in Casselberry built around slow-fermented sourdough guests say melts in your mouth. The Turkish breakfast is the main event: menemen with soudjouk, the Aegean omelet, huge plates, and Turkish coffee people get obsessed with. Service runs slow and the wait can stretch, but the bread is the reason to stay anyway.

places.name: The Sullivan Public House
places.address: Sullivans Public House, 116 E 1st St, Sanford, FL 32771-1325, United States
places.description: Historic Imperial building on East 1st Street in Sanford, filled with hand-carved wood, a copper ceiling, and dim, welcoming light. Guests come for what they call the best Guinness pour in all of Sanford, cold pints, and a deep Irish whiskey selection. Order shepherd's pie, fish and chips, scotch eggs, or the meatloaf sandwich on house made soda bread, with potato and garlic soup to start.

places.name: Wunderbar
places.address: Wunderbar, 4200 Conroy Rd, Orlando, FL 32839-2400, United States
places.description: Not a cocktail bar, but a family-owned superfood cafe in the Mall at Millenia food court, fresh fruit on display, made in front of you. Guests come back week after week for the acai bowls, the Tropical Breeze, and energy drinks in Berry Lime and Mango Peach. It reads as the healthy pit stop inside a shopping day, clean, bright, and quick, though counter service can wobble when the court gets busy.

places.name: Bagel King Bakery
places.address: Bagel King Bakery, 668 Kennedy Blvd W, Orlando, FL 32810-6255, United States
places.description: A working wholesale plant, not a retail shop, whose kettle-boiled bagels fill deli and cafe cases across Central Florida. Family-owned since 1977, it bakes bagels in many varieties plus danish, muffins, croissants, and King Cakes. When a bagel at an Orlando cafe has real chew and shine, there is a good chance it started here.

places.name: Cafe 34 Istanbul
places.address: Cafe 34 Istanbul, 8255 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819-9326, United States
places.description: Cafe 34 Istanbul brings a lively, linger-worthy taste of Turkey to International Drive, all grill smoke and warm welcome. Lamb adana kebabs, chicken shish and lamb chops guests call the best in Orlando come off the grill, with the Ottoman Pleasure platter built for sharing. Baklava and kunefe handle the sweet side, and Turkish tea or coffee stretches the meal while hookah fragrance drifts through the lounge.

places.name: Parva
places.address: Parva, 220 W Lake Mary Blvd, Sanford, FL 32773-5925, United States
places.description: Warm, homey Colombian bakery and cafe on West Lake Mary Boulevard in Sanford, where the pastry case leads the visit. Pan de bono, buñuelos, pan con queso, and pastel de yuca come out golden and generously sized, with a house cilantro sauce regulars rave about. Stay for bandeja paisa, calentado, churrasco, or cachapa, and finish with toasted coconut flan or tres leches.

places.name: Shaka Donuts
places.address: 2641 Curry Ford Rd, Orlando, FL 32806
places.description: Aloha spirit in a cozy Curry Ford shop where every donut is made to order and served warm, and regulars call them Orlando's best. Regulars say these are the best donuts in Orlando in their opinion, and the case backs it up: passionfruit malasadas, spicy maple bacon, butter pecan cronuts, Boston cream, and the breakfast sandwich built on a glazed donut. The room is sunny and cute inside, and locals are happy to have this one in the neighborhood.

places.name: Charlie's Bakery
places.address: Charlie's Bakery, 3213 Curry Ford Rd, Orlando, FL 32806, United States
places.description: A Curry Ford go-to for generations, baking in the same shop since 1971. The case runs from Parker House rolls to coconut cream pie, key lime pie, strawberry cheesecake, and cakes and cupcakes for every occasion, and the super premium ice cream churned in house earns its own loyal following. Regulars call it a sweet little spot, clean and cute inside, and one reviewer swears the coconut cream pie is worth calling ahead for.

places.name: Ispirazione
places.address: Ispirazione, 1711 Amazing Way, Ocoee, FL 34761-3279, United States
places.description: In Ocoee, the focus is tigelle, small round Italian breads baked fresh to order, crunchy outside and soft in the center. Fillings lean imported and creamy, from the Tigella Deliziosa and Bella Vita with burrata, prosciutto, and mortadella to a Modena basket, with pistachio tiramisu and cannoli to finish. Guests call it a cozy, hidden away find, the kind of place you return to once you know it is there.

places.name: Marketplace at Avalon Park
places.address: Marketplace at Avalon Park, 3801 Avalon Park East Blvd, Orlando, FL 32828, United States
places.description: Avalon Park's food hall and front porch, a lively casual hall of local vendors where the crew never has to agree on one menu. Guests single out the barbecue and the beignets, and the dog-friendly patio keeps the neighborhood in the room. Live music and trivia nights give it an upbeat, local pulse beyond the food.

places.name: Shakers American Cafe
places.address: Shakers American Cafe, 1308 Edgewater Dr, Orlando, FL 32804-6351, United States
places.description: Cozy College Park cottage lined with donated salt and pepper shakers, where the breakfast crowd treats it like a clubhouse. The cinnamon roll pancakes are the dish regulars say is hard to pass up, with the potato pancake and smoked salmon eggs benedict running close behind. A tight dining room means waits at peak hours, so off peak visits keep things easy.

places.name: Theo's Kitchen
places.address: Theo's Kitchen, 2952 Curry Ford Rd, Orlando, FL 32806, United States
places.description: Family-owned on Curry Ford, a staple that plays a rare double act locals keep coming back for. The Greek half runs gyro platters with homemade-feeling tzatziki, hummus, grape leaves, spinach pie, and baklava, while the other half turns out fried chicken one guest calls the best she had in Orlando. Regulars have kept coming for years and keep arguing over which half wins.

places.name: Winter Park Biscuit Company
places.address: 3201 Corrine Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-2224, United States
places.description: All-vegan counter inside East End Market built around flaky, golden oat buttermilk biscuits, stacked or smothered in gravy. Guests call the chickn the best vegan chicken they have ever had, with fried tenders that could change a skeptic's mind. Most guests settle at the courtyard picnic tables, with hibiscus lemonade to cut through the comfort.

places.name: Happy Snapper Seafood Restaurant
places.address: Happy Snapper Seafood Restaurant, 6327 Orange Ave S, Orlando, FL 32809-5109, United States
places.description: Tiny, family-run hole-in-the-wall seafood joint on South Orange Avenue that guests keep coming back to. The grouper sandwich is the order regulars defend, the deep-fried whole snapper arrives crackling, and the blue crab bisque earns its own following, all cooked, as one guest put it, perfectly, not over salted or over spiced. Seating is limited because the room is small, and that is part of the deal.

places.name: The Spice Indian Grill
places.address: The Spice Indian Grill, 4498 Alafaya Trl N, Orlando, FL 32826, United States
places.description: Alafaya Trail's laid-back neighborhood Indian spot, where guests say the kitchen always nails it and the heat stays honest. The buffet draws a crowd, the chili chicken and fish curry get named as favorites, and the chicken saag with garlic naan earns repeat orders. You pick your own spice level, the room stays chill, and a mango lassi cools things down.

places.name: TORCHY'S TACOS
places.address: TORCHY'S TACOS, 11757 Daryl Carter Pkwy, Orlando, FL 32821-4002, United States
places.description: Austin swagger lands on Daryl Carter Parkway, loud, playful, and garage-y to its bones. The green chile queso is the order guests call to die for, and the Trailer Park, Baja Shrimp and Brushfire tacos each land with their own distinct flavor. The tacos run on the compact side, so order like you mean it.

places.name: Fun-Ko's Poke Bowls and Asian Snacks
places.address: Fun-Ko's Poke Bowls and Asian Snacks, 334 N Donnelly St, Mt Dora, FL 32757-5525, United States
places.description: Tucked inside Mount Dora Marketplace on Donnelly Street, a cheerful, low-key poke counter regulars call their go-to. Build your own bowl from fresh ingredients with mix and match sauces, or go signature with the Funko Salmon, the Classic Hawaiian or the spicy Funko Fire, with onigiri and a vegan bowl in the mix. Portions are big and beautiful, prices feel right, and devotees swear it rivals the best poke outside Hawaii.

places.name: The Smoothie Room
places.address: The Smoothie Room, 25 W Crystal Lake St, Orlando, FL 32806-4403, United States
places.description: Bright, clean, and calm on West Crystal Lake Street in SoDo, built around all-natural blends with nothing hidden in the cup. Guests point to the PB Falcon acai bowl for its thin coconut shell over granola and toppings, and keep the Iron Hammer, Bahama Mama and Berry Dose in rotation. Prices sit on the premium side for smoothies, a trade regulars accept for knowing exactly what goes into each blend.

places.name: Zorba's Kitchen
places.address: Zorba's Kitchen, 7325 Lake Underhill Rd, Orlando, FL 32822-6061, United States
places.description: Small, family-run Greek kitchen on Lake Underhill Road where, as one guest put it, the chef cooks like someone's Greek grandma. Everything is made fresh from scratch: lamb gyros on soft pita, the skepasti stacked with lamb, peppers, fries and feta, moussaka, spanakopita, and feta fries on the side. The dining room is intimate and welcoming, the kind of place that makes regulars feel at home.

places.name: Bruno's Oysters
places.address: Bruno's Oysters, 426 W Plant St, Winter Garden, FL 34787, United States
places.description: Inside Plant Street Market's Barrel Room in Winter Garden, moody, rustic, and intimate around a small counter. Guests linger over oysters on the half shell, Oysters Rockefeller and roasted bone marrow, with the lobster roll and crab cake sandwich earning repeat orders. Regulars call it a little diamond, even if the counter pace can stretch when the market fills.

places.name: Cress Restaurant
places.address: Cress Restaurant, 103 W Indiana Ave, DeLand, FL 32720-4209, United States
places.description: Warm, intimate room in historic downtown DeLand, farm-to-table in spirit, with a global menu following Florida's seasons. Guests rave about the garlic escargots, the crispy duck breast and a Moroccan lamb shank that falls off the bone, finishing with white chocolate crème brûlée. Portions run small for the price, but the service is on point and the room feels made for celebrations.

places.name: Death in the Afternoon
places.address: Death in the Afternoon, 930 Mills Ave N, Orlando, FL 32803-3230, United States
places.description: Dark, intimate Mills 50 room built around absinthe, named for the Hemingway cocktail of absinthe and sparkling wine. Bartenders will build a drink around your vibe instead of a menu, and regulars swear by the Sauterelle, which drinks like mint chocolate chip ice cream with swagger, plus a Spanish-leaning kitchen turning out patatas bravas, corn ribs, a chorizo burger and short rib gnocchi. The tiny room fills quickly and feels like a quiet, understated speakeasy, made for good conversation.

places.name: Donutste Family Bakery
places.address: 605 Crescent Executive Ct Ste 120, Lake Mary, FL 32746
places.description: Fully plant-based donuts with no butter, milk, or eggs, in a bright pink Lake Mary room guests find cheerful and welcoming. The donuts are large and rich, in rotating seasonal flavors like ube cinnamon roll, red velvet, strawberry shortcake, and the tiramisu doughssant. Batches stay small and popular flavors sell out, so regulars preorder and get in line early.

places.name: El Coqui Ninja Restaurant
places.address: El Coqui Ninja Restaurant, 3097 Curry Ford Rd, Orlando, FL 32806-3301, United States
places.description: Puerto Rican soul meets Asian comfort on Curry Ford, and the mashup is the whole point. Cuerno beef eggrolls, crab rangoon, Puerto Rican Chinese rice, and roast pork mofongo with shrimp land in a room that is quirky and cozy, with flowered couches and projector boxes at the tables. Guests call it a piece of home and a real surprise fusion, and the portions make for good leftovers.

places.name: Hourglass Brewing
places.address: Hourglass Brewing, 2500 Curry Ford Rd, Orlando, FL 32806-2506, United States
places.description: Pouring inside a former church on Curry Ford, this Hourglass District taproom keeps a rotating cast of house beers flowing. Altamonte Vampire sour, Apricaustic, I-4 Eyesore, and District Kolsch sit beside beer flights, rotating food trucks, and trivia nights, with video game touches and an NES corner for good measure. Guests put its beer among the best in Central Florida, and the room stays roomy, clean, and easygoing.

places.name: J'Adore the French Bakery
places.address: J'Adore the French Bakery, 910 Sand Lake Rd, Altamonte Springs, FL 32714-7053, United States
places.description: Unassuming little French bakery in Altamonte Springs that regulars describe as a sleeper. The croissants are crisp and crunchy outside, layered and puffy inside, and nothing in the case runs too sweet: baguettes, a braided bacon twist, and canele, all subtle and impeccable. The room is small, and the pastry makes the argument by itself.

places.name: Jinya Ramen Bar
places.address: Jinya Ramen Bar, 8 N Summerlin Ave, Orlando, FL 32801-2930, United States
places.description: Lights stay dim and bowls run deep on North Summerlin, with broth simmered the slow way and a sleek room that fills fast. The Tonkotsu Black, loaded with garlic chips and garlic oil, is the purist's pick, while the spicy creamy vegan ramen converts skeptics and the JINYA Bun brings slow braised pork chashu in a steamed bun. Guests rave about the broth like it is addictive, so come hungry and plan to stay a while.

places.name: Kamayan Grill
places.address: Kamayan Grill, 7868 W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy, Kissimmee, FL 34747-1738, United States
places.description: Cozy, family-run Filipino kitchen on 192 in Kissimmee where guests say the food tastes just like home. Plates are built for sharing: the Ultimate Bilao, crispy pata, sizzling sisig, kare-kare and lumpia shanghai, with halo-halo to finish. Waits can run long when the room is busy, but regulars call the spread a real celebration on the table.

places.name: Lighthouse Seafood
places.address: Lighthouse Seafood, 101 N Country Club Rd, Lake Mary, FL 32746, United States
places.description: Half market, half cafe on Country Club Road in Lake Mary, where you can buy fish to take home or have the kitchen cook it fresh. Guests come back for crab cakes with a crisp crust and flaky center, royal red shrimp, clam chowder, and Mom Evelyn's key lime pie to finish. The room stays casual and quaint, family run and honest in the way regulars describe as real seafood cooked for us.

places.name: Moa Kai Hawaiian Diner
places.address: Moa Kai Hawaiian Diner, 2217 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-4911, United States
places.description: Retro diner comfort meets Hawaiian cooking on East Colonial Drive, all tropical color and aloha warmth. Plate lunches anchor the menu, loco moco, shoyu chicken, kalua pork and garlic shrimp, and the deep-fried Spam musubi is the plate guests push on first timers. Malasadas and ube haupia pie close things out with a glass of POG, and guests say every bite feels like the islands and a big warm hug.

places.name: Nan and Pop's Ice Cream Shop
places.address: Nan and Pop's Ice Cream Shop, 351 N Ronald Reagan Blvd, Longwood, FL 32750-4159, United States
places.description: Old-fashioned Longwood parlor where the sweet smell of waffle cones hits you at the door. Bubble waffle cones come warm and fresh, the scoops are super creamy, and red velvet is the flavor guests name most, with banana splits, freak shakes and Pop's Garbage Pail for bigger appetites. The staff are generous with samples, the room is cute and clean, and the whole place runs cozy and unhurried.

places.name: Papi Smash'd Burger
places.address: Papi Smash'd Burger, 66 E Pine St, Orlando, FL 32801-2616, United States
places.description: Small, quaint counter on East Pine where smash burgers come with a Latin soul, pressed hard until edges go lacy and crisp. The OG Double with Boujee Truffle Sauce sets the standard, the Papi Chulo brings the wink, and guests call them the best smash burgers they have ever had. Yuca fries, passion fruit lemonade and a cookies and cream shake round out the order.

places.name: Quigley Coffee
places.address: Quigley Coffee, 1730 Rinehart Rd, Sanford, FL 32771-6590, United States
places.description: Playful, bright Sanford shop on Rinehart Road that started as a cart, roasts its own beans, and shares space with a skate shop. Guests praise cups that are consistently amazing and single out the matcha, alongside named lattes like the Bear Hug, the Florida Boi candied orange latte, and the Smokey Bokey. The Jammy Sammy with habanero bacon jam is the food order regulars point to, sweet heat and all.

places.name: Red Panda Noodle
places.address: Red Panda Noodle, 274 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801, United States
places.description: Chef-driven noodle spot at downtown's A La Cart food hall, where hand-pulled biang biang noodles arrive thick with a firm bite. The spicy chicken katsu and bourbon-spiked chicken noodles hit hard, and guests warn that when the menu says spicy, it really means it. The Goomba goes the vegan route with mushrooms, mustard greens and black vinegar.

places.name: Sal's Pizza Bar
places.address: Sal's Pizza Bar, 11020 Daryl Carter Pkwy, Orlando, FL 32836, United States
places.description: Family-owned on Daryl Carter Parkway, turning out Brooklyn-style pies that transplanted New Yorkers say taste just like home. Guests call the slice the best in Orlando, pointing to the Nonna slice, vodka burrata pizza, grandpa slice and ziti slice coming hot from the oven. Garlic knots and cannoli round out an old school neighborhood counter where Sal himself is often behind it.

places.name: Wine 4 Oysters
places.address: Wine 4 Oysters, 1957 Alafaya Trl S, Orlando, FL 32828-8732, United States
places.description: In plain sight on South Alafaya Trail, an intimate little room built for date night. Oysters arrive raw from both coasts, baked Rockefeller style or in a sampler, each plated with a wine pairing in mind, alongside Thai mussels, lobster ravioli and a seafood boil in dirty butter. Guests praise the fresh, exceptionally dressed shells and the warm Eastern European hospitality that runs the room.

places.name: Ziggie's Pizza
places.address: Ziggie's Pizza, 603 Virginia Dr, Orlando, FL 32803-1844, United States
places.description: Playful little counter on Virginia Drive in Ivanhoe Village, attached to the Thirsty Topher craft beer bar, with very thin personal pies. The Killa Beez layers fig jam, prosciutto, pepperoni, goat cheese and house hot honey with real heat, while the Stardust piles on pistachio pesto and truffle oil, and guests call every pie a flavor adventure. The crust lands crisp with just the right cheese to sauce balance, light enough that you still feel good on your feet afterward.

places.name: Dezerland Park Orlando
places.address: 5250 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Guests keep landing on the same word for this International Drive indoor complex: huge. The indoor complex on International Drive stacks an auto museum holding Batmobiles, the Ecto-1 and a James Bond collection alongside Florida's longest indoor go-kart track, glow-in-the-dark mini golf, a pinball palace, boutique bowling and a trampoline park, all of it air-conditioned. Entry costs nothing and each attraction bills on its own, so the total climbs quietly; picking a few must-dos first is how regulars keep the day in hand.

places.name: Fun Spot America
places.address: 5700 Fun Spot Way, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Old-school midway the mega-parks left behind, family-owned since 1997, with White Lightning's wooden coaster and short lines, guests say. There is no admission gate to clear, just pay, ride, repeat. It reads as the coaster day Orlando families actually take, clean, unhurried and human-scale.

places.name: Orlando Watersports Complex
places.address: 8615 Florida Rock Rd, Orlando, FL 32824
places.description: Laid-back cable park where beginners and pros share the water, with an inflatable Aqua Park for bouncing between runs. Coaches teach first timers on the beginner cable while experienced riders lap the main cables, and Nautique boat pulls round out the day. Guests call the staff encouraging and genuinely invested in your success, the kind of place where kids forget their phones for hours.

places.name: Crayola Experience
places.address: 8001 S Orange Blossom Trl, Orlando, FL 32809
places.description: Hands-on color playground inside The Florida Mall, built for younger kids. Children name and wrap their own custom crayons, melt wax into shapes, try drip art, and watch their coloring come to life on screen. Guests call it creativity packed into every corner: colorful, playful, and easy to wander at your own pace indoors.

places.name: Andretti Indoor Karting and Games
places.address: 9299 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Competition drives it all: electric SuperKarts on a multi-level indoor track, laser tag, bowling, simulators, and VR bays. Guests call it a blast and praise the helpful staff, and the honest texture is demand, with waits at peak times and safety stops that can slow a race mid-run. Book ahead and it is the rainy-day or birthday answer on Universal Boulevard.

places.name: Nona Adventure Park
places.address: 14086 Centerline Drive, Orlando, FL 32827
places.description: Lake Nona lake turned playground: inflatable aqua park, cable wakeboarding for every level, and a 60-foot climbing tower. Guests call it so fun with such a nice atmosphere, and the staff earn as much praise as the attractions. The aqua park is a genuine workout, so pace yourself and refuel at Splashes Bistro between rounds.

places.name: WonderWorks Orlando
places.address: 9067 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: The upside-down house on I-Drive, a landmark since 1998, is all hands-on inside, from a hurricane shack to laser tag and a ropes course. Guests call it a cool, interactive experience, and the tax is the crowd, with peak waits and an admission price some find steep for the size. It earns its keep as the rainy-day answer for kids who need to touch everything.

places.name: Peppa Pig Theme Park Florida
places.address: 1 Legoland Way, Winter Haven, FL 33884
places.description: Next to LEGOLAND in Winter Haven, this toddler-scaled first theme park stays gentle, colorful and relaxed for little kids. Little riders loop Daddy Pig's Roller Coaster again and again, splash through the Muddy Puddles Splash Pad and float up on Peppa's Balloon Ride, with interactive play areas sized just right for small children. It is a small park by design, which families call exactly the point for first theme park memories.

places.name: Legoland Florida
places.address: 1 Legoland Way, Winter Haven, FL 33884
places.description: On the old Cypress Gardens grounds in Winter Haven, this is the hands-on park for kids who build, relaxed next to the mega parks. The Dragon coaster, LEGO NINJAGO The Ride and Miniland USA anchor the lands, and kids can even build LEGO creations while waiting in line. Waits stay short and the creativity is everywhere, though some rides and restaurants sit closed on any given day, and guests call Granny's Apple Fries a must.

places.name: Dinosaur World
places.address: 5145 Harvey Tew Rd, Plant City, FL 33565
places.description: An old-Florida roadside classic in Plant City, where crossing into thick, shaded trees feels like walking into Jurassic Park. Life-size dinosaurs stand in species groupings along the paths, and kids dig for fossils at the Fossil Dig, pan at the Dino Gem Mine and excavate a life-size Stegosaurus at the Boneyard. Extras like the train and gem mine cost on top of admission, but the pace stays unhurried, and dogs are welcome along for the wander.

places.name: Wild Florida
places.address: 3301 Lake Cypress Rd, Kenansville, FL 34739
places.description: At the Headwaters of the Everglades, airboats skim protected marsh and captains know exactly where the gators bask. Guests come back raving about alligators seen up close, babies included, and the gator feeding demonstrations back on land. A drive-thru safari, a capybara encounter and a chance to hold a baby alligator round out a hands-on day that feels like the middle of nowhere.

places.name: Knight Library
places.address: 11448 University Blvd, Orlando, FL 32817
places.description: UCF's rite-of-passage college bar on University Boulevard, loud, packed and unapologetically high energy. Students cross from campus for cheap drinks, P1 lemon drops, Ghost Bombs and Long Island pitchers, spilling onto the big patio between DJ sets. Busy nights mean a line at the door and floors that have seen things, which regulars treat as part of the college experience and the lasting memories.

places.name: Aero Rooftop Bar & Lounge
