places.address: 60 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: A small rooftop with big energy: open-air dancing above North Orange Avenue, skyline behind the DJ, lasers over the crowd. The music leans house and EDM with R&B nights mixed in, the drinks are strong, and guests talk about the sing-alongs as much as the sets. It runs pricier than the bars downstairs, which is the trade for dancing over the rooftops instead of inside them.

places.name: Ohm Nightclub
places.address: 20 E Central Blvd, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Downtown's big-room club, formerly Tier, packs two floors, with skyboxes over the floor and bottle service for groups. Touring DJs and themed takeovers drive the main room, and guests describe the full nights as a movie. Entry runs steep and the door runs strict, club mechanics in full, and the scale is the point.

places.name: Euphoria Downtown
places.address: 110 S Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: On South Orange Avenue, brunch with bottomless mimosas and lamb chops gives way to Techno Euphoria nights on a big sound system. Guests talk about pounding kicks strung through lights and visuals, and call the day parties a downtown draw. The night side is the heart of it, a room built for people who came for the music itself, with bottle sections at the splurge end.

places.name: Aura Night Club
places.address: 49 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: About the floor here: an LED-lit room in the Beacham complex on North Orange, hopping between EDM, hip-hop and reggaeton. Guests describe immaculate vibes and a room that is just energy, with no stage theatrics between you and the music. VIP tables and multiple bars ring the floor for groups that want a base.

places.name: Yaz Orlando
places.address: 114 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: On North Orange Avenue, dinner and lounge come first, then the room deepens into a club as the night goes on, low-lit and moody. One address takes a group from dinner to dancing without moving the car. The mood is the pitch here, moody rather than maximal.

places.name: The Burrow Cafe and Play
places.address: 618 N Mills Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: In Mills 50, kids get a supervised indoor playground while adults get a cafe that actually takes its drinks seriously. The iced Honey Badger latte and Blue Lychee Spritz lead a menu that runs from coffee to a S'mores latte and a mom-osa, in a room guests call warm, inviting and spotless. Parents call the combo undefeated, and birthday parties and a photo booth round out the reasons families linger.

places.name: SeaWorld Orlando
places.address: 7007 SeaWorld Dr, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: A working marine park with serious coasters, from Mako and Pipeline to Penguin Trek, plus orca presentations and a shark tunnel. Guests call it an incredible experience for families, with shows and food and drink options all over the park. The classic trade-offs apply, crowds and long waits at the headliners, so ride early and let the presentations carry the middle of the day.

places.name: Aquatica Orlando
places.address: 5800 Water Play Way, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: At SeaWorld's water park, the Dolphin Plunge clear tube passes Commerson's dolphins, and Roa's Rapids runs faster than a lazy river should. Wave pools, a wide sand beach and gentler coves fill out the day, and families describe an easy, awesome time, especially when the park runs quiet. Budget for parking, lockers and food on top of the ticket; the extras are the recurring gripe in an otherwise well-liked park.

places.name: Discovery Cove
places.address: 6000 Discovery Cove Way, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: The calm splurge on I-Drive: a reservation-only day resort where attendance is capped and the water stays clear. Guests drift the lazy river, snorkel the Grand Reef with stingrays gliding past, and take the dolphin swim, with meals and drinks included along the way. Families who return call it a getaway from the major theme parks. The one sting guests name is the dolphin-swim photo packages, priced steeply on top of admission.

places.name: Gatorland
places.address: 14501 S Orange Blossom Trl, Orlando, FL 32837
places.description: Old Florida, unpolished and proud: gators launch for chicken at the Gator Jumparoo Show while handlers work the sand nearby. A breeding marsh, rare white leucistic gators and the Screamin' Gator Zip Line overhead fill out a park running since 1949 on Orange Blossom Trail. Guests call it refreshingly non-Disney and easy on the wallet, though feedings, encounters and the zip line each cost extra on top of admission.

places.name: Medieval Times Dinner & Tournament
places.address: 4510 W Vine St, Kissimmee, FL 34746
places.description: In a castle arena on Vine Street in Kissimmee, knights joust, falconry flies, and the cheering crowd eats with its hands, no utensils. The feast centers on tomato bisque guests call to die for, roasted chicken and garlic bread, while each section roars for its knight. Drinks and souvenir photos cost extra as sellers work the aisles, but guests say the show and the meal together earn the price.

places.name: Pirates Dinner Adventure
places.address: 6400 Carrier Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: A full-size Spanish galleon sits in an indoor lagoon on Carrier Drive while acrobats swing, swords clash and cannons flash around tables. Guests cheer for their section's pirate, and the show's energy pulls kids into the story from the first scene. The chicken dinner plays second fiddle to the spectacle, so treat the meal as part of the ticket rather than the point of the night. Bring the kids, sit close, and let it be loud.

places.name: The Outta Control Magic Dinner Show
places.address: 9067 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Inside WonderWorks on I-Drive, pizza keeps coming, a volunteer gets pulled into the bit, and the room laughs before the trick lands. Guests describe magic that is funny and mind blowing, with a host who works the crowd and keeps everyone engaged, from kids to grandparents. Dinner is unlimited pizza, salad and dessert served family style at long shared tables. Seating is first come, so arrive early and expect a line when the earlier show runs long.

places.name: Boggy Creek Airboat Adventures
places.address: 2001 E Southport Rd, Kissimmee, FL 34746
places.description: From Southport Road, airboats skim East Lake Tohopekaliga into marsh grass where captains spot gators, turtles and wading birds. Guests call it a highlight of their Florida vacation, and the night tours, with spotlights sweeping for glowing eyes, are the ones people talk about for years. Back on shore there is gem mining, a butterfly garden and a Native American village to wander.

places.name: Museum of Illusions Orlando
places.address: 8375 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: At ICON Park, bring your camera: the Ames room shrinks your friends and the vortex tunnel scrambles your balance. Staff are stationed at the big set pieces to help you nail the photo each illusion is built for. Most guests are through in under an hour, so pair it with the Wheel or dinner nearby and it earns its place in the day.

places.name: SEA LIFE Orlando Aquarium
places.address: 8449 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Sharks and rays pass overhead in the 360-degree ocean tunnel while you stay dry, unhurried and air conditioned. Touch pools hold starfish and anemones, and themed zones carry you from the Atlantic to the Indian Ocean at a pace kids can manage. It is a compact aquarium, better as one stop inside an ICON Park day than as the whole day itself.

places.name: The Escape Game Orlando
places.address: 8145 International Dr Ste 511, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: For the polished, big-budget end of escape rooms, expect cinematic sets and multi-room puzzles that keep large groups busy. Guest-named favorites include The Depths, Gold Rush, Prison Break and Legend of the Yeti, and game guides nudge without spoiling when a group stalls. Guests call the rooms challenging and exciting, and plenty leave already picking the next one.

places.name: Merritt Island Bioluminescence Kayak Tours
places.address: 951 Kiwanis Island Park Rd, Merritt Island, FL 32952
places.description: On dark lagoon water around Merritt Island, dinoflagellates flare electric blue with every paddle stroke through a clear kayak. Mullet darting underneath leave comet trails, and guests say the glow is hard to get on camera but amazing in person, strongest around the new moon. Pack serious bug spray and double-check your outfitter's check-in, since several companies launch from the same park and your clothes and shoes will get wet.

places.name: Blue Spring Manatee Kayak Tours
places.address: Blue Spring State Park, 2100 W French Ave, Orange City, FL 32763
places.description: At Blue Spring State Park, guided kayaks slip into clear, 72-degree spring water where manatees roll and graze beneath the boat. Guests call drifting alongside them, noses, backs and tails breaking the surface, one of the highlights of a Florida trip, like stepping into another world. Knowledgeable guides read the animals' mood and detour into quiet side channels for eagles, turtles and glassy views.

places.name: Orlando Helicopter Tours
places.address: 8990 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: From the pad on International Drive, helicopters lift you over Disney, Universal, SeaWorld and the Orlando Eye, laid out below. Guests describe breathtaking views and knowledgeable, friendly pilots, with sunset flights and proposal flights among the signature ways up. It is a splurge priced like one, and the thrill is the point.

places.name: Revolution Adventures
places.address: 4000 FL-33, Clermont, FL 34714
places.description: In Clermont, trade park lines for mud: guided ATV rides, side-by-side buggies and the Mucky Duck, which splashes from trail into water. The pace reads more scenic drive than adrenaline chase, with a thorough safety briefing that leaves beginners feeling secure in helmets and goggles. Families fill out the day with the Archery Arrow Blitz and bass fishing on the private lake, and everyone expects to get dirty.

places.name: Polynesian Fire Luau
places.address: 4740 W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy, Kissimmee, FL 34746
places.description: On 192 in Kissimmee, drums, hula and fast Tahitian dancing build toward the fire knife performers at this festive tropical dinner show. A tropical buffet and a flaming Hawaiian rum punch come first, and audience participation pulls guests into the dances along the way. Guests call it one of the best evenings of their whole Orlando vacation, welcoming and immersive from start to finish.

places.name: St. Augustine Day Trip
places.address: 11 S Castillo Dr, St. Augustine, FL 32084
places.description: The Castillo de San Marcos anchors St. Augustine, a coquina fort that guarded Matanzas Bay through Spanish, English and American rule. Guests say you feel the history in every step, and the views from the top over the harbor and old town repay the climb. St. George Street strings colonial architecture together with ice cream shops and pubs, and parking near the fort runs scarce, so the city garage earns its fee.

places.name: Clearwater Beach Day Trip
places.address: 1 Causeway Blvd, Clearwater Beach, FL 33767
places.description: Clearwater Beach is the Gulf coast reset: sugar-white sand, soft underfoot, calm shallow water and a festive promenade along Beach Walk. Pier 60 anchors the scene with street performers, musicians and local artisans selling candles, bracelets and art. Guests call it heaven on earth, and the sunset celebration at the pier is the day's exclamation point.

places.name: Universal Stella Nova Resort
places.address: 4500 Epic Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: The value-tier basecamp for Epic Universe, space-themed, a 10-15 minute stroll away, with modern, clean, good-sized rooms. The pool deck is built for recovery days, and shuttles run to all the Universal parks. Housekeeping runs every other day rather than daily, so ask at the desk when you need extra towels or a refresh.

places.name: Universal Terra Luna Resort
places.address: 5500 Epic Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Stella Nova's sister resort on Epic Boulevard, clean and modern, with an exploration theme and a big resort pool. Guests praise the friendly staff, the range of on-site food options and shuttles that make Epic Universe and the other Universal parks easy. The walls run thin, so light sleepers may want to ask for a quieter corner room.

places.name: B&B HOTEL Orlando International Drive
places.address: 6323 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: On International Drive, the European budget formula stateside: newly renovated, spacious rooms, breakfast buffet, pool and free lobby popcorn. The vibe is clean, simple and no-frills, with free self-parking and a location guests call unbeatable for park and convention runs. Housekeeping can be inconsistent, but the value is the draw.

places.name: Villatel Orlando Resort
places.address: 5120 Del Verde Way, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: On Del Verde Way off I-Drive, villas for big groups sleep four to nine bedrooms, each with its own pool, plus Aqua Bay water park on site. Guests call the resort beautiful and very clean, with amenities everywhere and stays that land above expectations. Total the full bill before you book, since parking, resort fees and even heating your private pool land on top of the villa rate.

places.name: Nikitta
places.address: 8255 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Orlando's first serious Nikkei room pairs Peruvian ingredients with Japanese technique in a deep purple, elegant space on I-Drive. Guests talk about tiraditos, lomo saltado, spicy tuna crispy rice and nigiri that melts, with pistachio tres leches to finish. Live DJs and dancers give it a vibrant, club-like energy that has made it a date-night flagship for the corridor. Service pacing can run slow, so settle in for a leisurely evening and let the food carry the night.

places.name: Zaza Cuban Comfort Food
places.address: 1621 S Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32806
places.description: A family-run neighborhood diner in SoDo, on South Orange Avenue, built around cafecito culture and pressed sandwiches. Cafe con leche, the Cubano and medianoche anchor the counter, with ropa vieja, lechon asado, vaca frita, empanadas and guava and cheese pastries filling out the comfort menu.

places.name: Reeves Sports Bar
places.address: 50 E Central Blvd, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: A polished downtown sports bar on Central Boulevard, with screens everywhere, jerseys on the walls and a chef-driven take on game-day food. The kitchen brines and dry-rubs its wings for 24 hours, and the menu runs to buffalo hummus, tuna nachos, cheesesteak egg rolls and pressed burgers. It reads as a neighborhood room first and a sports bar second, an easy downtown stop when a game is on.

places.name: Pig Floyd's x Pigzza
places.address: 1050 N Mills Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: On North Mills, two Mills 50 names share one roof: Pigzza's sourdough pies and pastas alongside Pig Floyd's brisket. The Meat Me at Floyd's brisket pizza and The Casper white pizza lead the pies, the spicy sausage rigatoni gets called ridiculous in the best way, and the carbonara reminded one guest of meals back in Europe. A big patio and an easygoing, unpretentious room make it a group-friendly hang, though service can take its time when the place gets busy.

places.name: Mills Market
places.address: 1110 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: The food hall on East Colonial that anchors Mills 50, all shared tables, patio seating and chef-driven stalls under one roof. The lineup leans Asian, with Banh Mi Boy, Kai Kai BBQ and Dumplings, UniGirl and newer arrivals like Okonomi and Cowboy Curry, so a group can order across counters and share everything. It gets lively, and weekend seating fills fast, which is part of the communal fun.

places.name: O-Town West
places.address: 8652 Fenton St, Orlando, FL 32836
places.description: On Fenton Street in the Epic Universe corridor, a still-filling mixed-use development of new restaurants and shops. Tenants already trading include Sushi Izuki, Agave Azul, Pokemoto, Bamboo Wok and Hyderabad Cafe, giving the grid an early dining mix beyond the parks. The feel remains in progress, a corridor taking shape rather than a settled district.

places.name: Disney Starlight: Dream the Night Away
places.address: Magic Kingdom Park, 1180 Seven Seas Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Magic Kingdom's nighttime parade, dreamy and glowing, and guests call it pure nostalgia and Disney magic. The Blue Fairy leads floats carrying a Coco marigold bridge, a Moana wave and Peter Pan flying over Big Ben, closing with the Whimsy finale train. Fans call it a worthy successor to the Main Street Electrical Parade, and curb spots go early on busy nights, so claim yours ahead.

places.name: Test Track 3.0
places.address: EPCOT, 200 Epcot Center Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: EPCOT's fastest ride, wrapped in a sleek, retro-futuristic story about car design, and guests say the facelift suits it. A graphic reveal lands right before the car bursts outside into the 65 mph loop, all wind-in-your-hair speed. Lines run long and delays happen, so regulars swear by the single rider line.

places.name: GEO-82
places.address: EPCOT, 200 Epcot Center Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Inside Spaceship Earth, EPCOT's adults-only lounge stays calm, mid-century and quietly chic, right down to the coasters. The Brown Butter Old-Fashioned, the Electron and the Brûlée Banana Highball lead a classic-leaning list, and guests call it a favorite escape precisely because it skips the typical kitschy park feel. Reservations are scarce and vanish fast, so book the moment you can.

places.name: The Beak and Barrel
places.address: Magic Kingdom Park, 1180 Seven Seas Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Magic Kingdom's pirate tavern in Adventureland is theatrical, with an indoor thunderstorm and a Barker Bird working the room. The Salty Seas MARRgarita, Kraken's Catch and a souvenir skull mug carry the pirate pours, and when the anthem plays the whole bar sings along. Visits run on a tight clock, so arrive knowing your order.

places.name: Zootopia: Better Zoogether!
places.address: Disney's Animal Kingdom, 2901 Osceola Pkwy, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Inside the Tree of Life theater at Animal Kingdom, Judy Hopps and Nick Wilde host a cheerful 4D celebration. Water spritzes, seat effects and a grinning Clawhauser animatronic keep the gentle story physical, and guests treasure it as a cool, air-conditioned break. It lands softer than the bug show it replaced, which suits its family crowd just fine.

places.name: Disney Villains: Unfairly Ever After
places.address: Disney's Hollywood Studios, 351 S Studio Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: At Hollywood Studios, the villains get their own Broadway-style stage show, wicked, campy and high-energy. The Magic Mirror hosts a contest for the most misunderstood villain of all, Cruella changes wardrobe mid-song, Maleficent lands the big number, and the audience applause vote can change the ending every time. One guest summed it up as Six The Musical, but about famous Disney villains.

places.name: The Little Mermaid: A Musical Adventure
places.address: Disney's Hollywood Studios, 351 S Studio Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Ariel's story gets retold at Hollywood Studios in a colorful, nostalgic burst of puppetry and projection. Sebastian and Flounder come to life as puppets while Part of Your World, Under the Sea and Poor Unfortunate Souls carry the show, and kids light up for all of it. The story is compressed to fit, the theater fills fast, and the strong air conditioning is half the pleasure.

places.name: Soarin' Across America
places.address: EPCOT, 200 Epcot Center Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: Lifted into a hang glider seat at EPCOT, you fly over the Grand Canyon, New York Harbor and Hawaii and Alaska, wind and signature scents included. The flight opens with an Artemis rocket launch and closes with Spaceship Earth lit red, white and blue for the country's 250th anniversary. Guests call it gentle, scenic and immersive, and definitely worth doing, though the line builds fast.

places.name: Rock 'n' Roller Coaster Starring the Muppets
places.address: Disney's Hollywood Studios, 351 S Studio Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: At Hollywood Studios, you launch into the dark, all speed, inversions and loud rock, now with the Electric Mayhem playing you through it. A new pre-show puts Scooter on stage while Statler and Waldorf heckle from the balcony, and the super stretch limo dash across Hollywood runs on the band's covers. Guests call it a must-do, packed with a sense of speed, music and entertainment.

places.name: Big Thunder Mountain Railroad
places.address: Magic Kingdom Park, 1180 Seven Seas Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: The runaway mine train through Tumbleweed at Magic Kingdom, wild, rattly and scenic, with no big major drops. Reopened after a full refurbishment with fresh track and a new Rainbow Caverns scene, it still rides like the classic guests remember. Guests call it the perfect first time coaster, and regulars swear by riding it during the fireworks.

places.name: Expedition Odyssey: Fire & Ice
places.address: SeaWorld Orlando, 7007 SeaWorld Dr, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: SeaWorld's Arctic flying theater lifts riders over polar landscapes filmed in Iceland, with real animals rather than rendered ones. The flight mixes tranquil footage with fast-paced moments, gentle enough that families rate it a park highlight. The ride ends inside the Wild Arctic habitat, where belugas, walruses and seals wait on the other side of the glass.

places.name: LEGO Galaxy + Galacticoaster
places.address: LEGOLAND Florida Resort, 1 Legoland Way, Winter Haven, FL 33884
places.description: At LEGOLAND Florida, young riders head into a brick-built space adventure on Galacticoaster, an indoor launch coaster gentle enough for a first. In the queue, kids design their own spaceship before boarding, with the Biff Dipper animatronic setting the mission. The ride has already earned the nickname Cosmic Rewind for kids: silky-smooth, immersive and tuned for family thrills.

places.name: SEA LIFE Florida
places.address: LEGOLAND Florida Resort, 1 Legoland Way, Winter Haven, FL 33884
places.description: Inside LEGOLAND Florida, tanks are built like theme park sets, a theme park under the sea where habitats riff on rides and coasters. The 180-degree ocean tunnel, stingray bay, the Freshwater Swamp and Key West Harbor keep the pace gentle and kid-sized. With admission folded into the park ticket, it works as the air-conditioned reset between outdoor rides rather than a standalone trip.

places.address: 201 E Pine St #101, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: A small, family-run cafe inside the PNC building on Pine Street, scratch-made and no-frills. The menu leans homemade: pork and hash, a burrito with housemade chorizo, an avocado and tomato tartine and a limited prime rib sandwich. The lattes get the same care, sea salt caramel or white chocolate lavender.

The lobster ravioli is the dish one regular calls the reason I go there, joined by gorgonzola walnut pasta, oak-grilled salmon, and a meatball one diner called the most delicious she had ever had. Longtime regulars note the menu has shrunk over the years and the room runs loud when it fills, but for anniversaries and milestone dinners it still feels like the right table.
places.inkind_note: Two records cover the upstairs restaurant and the downstairs Market & Cafe, both at 611 S Orlando Ave; there is no separate second street address. places.name: Antonio's

places.address: 611 S Orlando Ave, Maitland, FL 32751
places.description: Downstairs, the casual half: a cafe and boutique Italian market under the same roof as the upstairs dining room. Guests eat among the wine shelves, pairing pizza, a chicken parm sandwich, or rotisserie chicken with a corkage deal at the table. Leave time to browse imported cold cuts and cheeses, because dinner here easily turns into a provisions run.
places.inkind_note: Second of two Antonio's concepts at the single 611 S Orlando Ave building (no separate second street address exists). Not confirmed on inKind: no site:inkind.com hit and no inKind page found via web search. inKind venue pages are not publicly indexed, so this may reflect poor indexing rather than absence.
places.name: Antonio's Market & Cafe

places.address: 4706 Millenia Plaza Way, Orlando, FL 32839
places.description: DJ Khaled's soul food spot across from the Mall at Millenia: loud, lively and generous. Lemon pepper turkey wings are the order guests rave about, alongside fried chicken with red velvet waffles, collard greens guests call seasoned to perfection, and a round of the Famous Mystery Drink for the table. Portions run huge and plates arrive in shareable spreads, though service can stretch thin when the room is in full party mode.

Not confirmed on inKind: no site:inkind.com hit and no inKind page found via web search. inKind venue pages are not publicly indexed, so this may reflect poor indexing rather than absence.
places.name: The Licking

places.address: 8600 El Prado Ave, Orlando, FL 32825
places.description: A clubby tavern inside the revived Rio Pinar golf course, fairways beyond the patio and a relaxing, neighborhood feel. Guests come for the prime rib and the coffee-rubbed NY strip, plus the Pine & Oak burger and bartenders who remember your drink. Live music fills the room on some nights; when events pack it in, it gets loud and service stretches, so a quiet patio table is the sleeper pick.

places.name: Pine & Oak Tavern

places.address: 8001 S Orange Blossom Trl Kiosk TT124, Orlando, FL 32809
places.description: A bright Colombian kiosk inside The Florida Mall, turning out obleas with arequipe, acai bowls with Nutella and fruit, and a proper cortadito. Guests praise the friendly counter staff and call the arepas exquisite, with cholados and Dubai chocolate for the sweet finish. It is a quick, tropical pause between stores that beats the standard food court routine.

places.name: Amazonica

places.address: 5640 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Sfiha's bakes palm-sized Brazilian meat pies on International Drive, golden rounds filled with beef, chicken and catupiry cheese, or four cheeses. Sweet versions run to Nutella, dulce de leche and a Romeo & Juliet pairing, with coxinha and guaraná rounding out the order. The room is casual, friendly and lively, and combo boxes make feeding a crew easy, though busy nights can mean a wait.
places.inkind_note: No inKind listing found via public web search; inKind participation unverified.
places.name: Sfiha's International Drive

places.address: 5078 Dr Phillips Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: The Dr Phillips neighborhood clubhouse: a warm, rustic room with comfy booths, a big patio behind roll-up doors, and friendly, efficient staff. The prime rib sliders are the must-order, backed by a smash burger, the western omelette, a breakfast pizza, and house-infused vodkas poured into the Tavern Mule. Portions are generous and prices sit middle of the road, which is exactly the point.
places.inkind_note: Confirmed: multiple Yelp reviewers report paying with the inKind app and using inKind promotional deals at this location.
places.name: Burntwood Tavern

places.address: 478 E Altamonte Dr #102, Altamonte Springs, FL 32701
places.description: An old-school Cantonese dining room in Altamonte Springs that transplanted New Englanders call the real thing. The Eight Treasures clay pot is the star guests point newcomers to, with salt and pepper calamari, house fried rice with real shrimp, Hong Kong roast duck and dim sum around it. Portions run huge, dishes land hot and fresh, and the room stays no-frills and family style.
places.inkind_note: No inKind listing found via public web search; inKind participation unverified. Also note this location is in Altamonte Springs, not Orlando proper.
places.name: Yummy House

places.address: 6424 Carrier Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: A polished Brazilian rodizio on Carrier Drive, minutes from the Convention Center, where gauchos carve picanha, ribeye and lamb at the table. Between rounds, the buffet carries its own weight: a sushi spread, made-to-order pasta, salads and warm pao de queijo. Guests praise the quality of the meat and the warm, welcoming room; come hungry and pace yourself, since the cuts arrive in waves and the premium ones tend to come later.
places.inkind_note: No inKind listing found via public web search; inKind participation unverified.
places.name: Divina Carne

places.address: 3573 Aloma Ave, Oviedo, FL 32765
places.description: A pretty, family-owned Vietnamese room in Oviedo, with colorful walls, lit cubbies of bric-a-brac and paintings of old Saigon. The pho is the anchor, with rich broth and generous beef that one guest calls the best pho here, and the Curry Chicken Noodle Soup gets called one of the best things a visitor has ever tasted. The golden pancake arrives crisp and bright, and Charlie's Special lemon chicken is the house signature.
