SeaWorld Howl-O-Scream
places.address: 7007 SeaWorld Dr, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: Howl-O-Scream takes over SeaWorld after dark as a separate-ticket Halloween event, all fog, scare zones, haunted houses and coasters in the dark. Guests rave about the jump scares and the Monster Stomp show, with a poison apple cocktail in hand between houses. Lines for the houses can run long, and the scares are the whole point, so go in ready for them.

places.name: CoCo Key Water Park
places.address: 7400 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: A low-key hotel water park on International Drive that sells day passes, so no resort stay is needed. Slides, a foam party and the Key Quest arcade keep younger kids busy, Parrot's Perch and Minnows Lagoon suit the small ones, and lifeguards are on duty throughout. Guests like that it skips the huge crowds and expensive tickets of the big parks; read the resort and parking fee fine print before you book.

places.name: All-Inclusive Pass with Kennedy Space Center
places.address: Multiple attractions across Orlando + Kennedy Space Center
places.description: One all-inclusive pass bundles Kennedy Space Center with LEGOLAND Florida, the Orlando Eye, SEA LIFE, Madame Tussauds and WonderWorks. Guests call the app easy to use and like not reaching for their wallet at every gate. The catch is planning: the pass rewards travelers who map out their days, with Kennedy as the full-day anchor.

places.name: Drawn to Life: Cirque du Soleil
places.address: 1478 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: At Disney Springs, Disney animation blends with Cirque du Soleil acrobatics in a nostalgic production. A larger-than-life animation desk anchors the staging, with aerial and acrobatic acts set to Disney music and familiar characters woven into the storyline. Guests call it the best of both Disney and Cirque du Soleil, and say there really isn't a bad seat in the house.

places.name: Speakeasy Murder Mystery Dinner Show
places.address: 6400 Carrier Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Behind the doorbell at Teatro Martini on Carrier Drive, a 1920s speakeasy murder mystery folds the audience into the case over dinner. Guests call it immersive and interactive without being embarrassing, with actors funny enough to keep the room laughing between courses. The herb roasted chicken earns genuine praise, and a Death by Chocolate brownie closes the night.

places.name: Downtown Food Tour
places.address: A La Cart - City, 274 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: A walking food tour through the real Orlando, the downtown locals eat in, with history and art folded into the route by your guide. Stops hit vendors you would not normally try, for tastings like Sticky Pork Bites, a Quesito, Colombian street food and a Deviled Egg Smash Sandwich, plus a secret dish. Groups stay small and personal, and guests warn that you will get full.

places.name: Milk District Eats Food Tour
places.address: 201 N Bumby Ave, Orlando, FL 32803 (meets in front of the Milkhouse)
places.description: A small-group walking food tour through the dairy-named district east of downtown, personal, easygoing and rich with local history. The guides know the neighborhood cold and lead guests through independent rooms for bites like Bad As's sandwiches, Milkhouse wings and kale salad, and Kelly's ice cream with Foxtail cookies. Guests call it an interesting and delicious way to learn the area, and promise you will not leave hungry.

places.name: Ivanhoe Village Food Tour
places.address: 1211 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32804
places.description: A knowledgeable local guide leads this well-organized walk through a lakefront vintage district of shops and cafes, stop by tasting stop. Guests come hungry for plates that range from pizza to fried alligator bites, with history and hidden gems woven between bites. It suits a couple or small group looking for an easy, delicious way to learn the neighborhood by taste.

places.name: Brews and Bites Walking Tour
places.address: Ten10 Brewing Company, 1010 Virginia Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Through Ivanhoe Village breweries and bars, guides guests call knowledgeable and upbeat share plenty of local history along the way. Small groups sample craft beer alongside soft pretzel with beer cheese and locally made pizza, with behind the scenes stories at each stop. It feels like a guided introduction for people who want to map the Virginia Drive beer scene with company.

places.name: Fettuccine Pasta-Making Class
places.address: Goblin Studios, 805 W Central Blvd, Orlando, FL 32805
places.description: In a hands-on downtown class, Chef Mark walks you through fresh fettuccine from scratch: mixing, rolling thin, slicing ribbons and cooking them off. His classic marinara goes over the top, and you sit down to eat the pasta you made. Guests call it beginner-friendly and social, a skill they will use again long after the plates are cleared.

places.name: Hard Rock Cafe Orlando
places.address: 6050 Universal Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Guests call it the world's largest Hard Rock Cafe, at Universal CityWalk, walls covered in guitars, tour jackets and memorabilia in every corner. Order the Original Legendary Burger or the Legendary Nachos, add flatbreads or fajitas for the table, and expect flavorful American food served by attentive staff.

places.name: Café Tu Tu Tango
places.address: 8625 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: An I-Drive original since the 1990s that treats dinner like an art opening, with resident artists painting at easels, walls doubling as the gallery. The menu is small plates built for passing: brick oven flatbreads, tuna crudo, Cuban sliders and sangria pitchers. Guests call the atmosphere vibrant and buzzing, and it earns the word; expect a loud, high-energy room, not a quiet conversation.

places.name: Ole Red Orlando
places.address: 8417 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Blake Shelton's honky-tonk in the middle of ICON Park, with live country on stage and scratch-made Southern cooking from the kitchen. Guests rave about the Honey Bee Hot Chicken and Waffles, the Redneck Nachos and fried pickles one reviewer called the best they have ever had, all of it in a room they describe as electric. Dinner and a show in one stop; just know the bar tab runs steep, so pace the rounds.

places.name: Helena Modern Riviera
places.address: 8441 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: The polished room inside ICON Park, a Mediterranean supper club for Italian and Greek plates like crudos, whole fish and a Moroccan lamb shank. Guests say every corner feels like a photo and the theme decorations are always on point. It is the park's grown-up dinner, calmer than the midway outside; service can take its time, so settle in rather than watch the clock.

places.name: Gordon Ramsay Fish & Chips
places.address: 8391 International Dr Ste C-1, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Gordon Ramsay's British chippy at ICON Park, done up like a Union Jack beach shack, with counter service and a short menu. The Fish Combo comes hot and fresh in crispy batter, the Dirty Chips are loaded, and the sticky toffee and Biscoff shakes finish it. Guests call it a great spot for fish and chips; seating inside is scarce, so at busy times you may end up on the patio or taking it to go.

places.name: The Capital Grille
places.address: 9101 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: The default client steakhouse at Pointe Orlando, a short walk from the Rosen hotels, running the full expense-account ritual. Dry-aged steaks, a Kona-crusted strip, lobster bisque and a bread basket guests single out, backed by a serious wine list. Service is polished without hovering and the room stays quiet enough for actual conversation, which is why groups book it when the dinner has to go right.

places.name: Maggiano's Little Italy
places.address: 9101 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Family-style Italian at Pointe Orlando, built for the table that cannot agree on one dish. The classics come in generous sharing portions: chopped salad, chicken piccata, baked ziti, rigatoni alla vodka and a bruschetta guests call the best they have had, in a warm, red-checkered room. Portions assume a crowd and usually go home for a second meal; service can take its time, so order the favorites early and settle in.

places.name: The Hampton Social
places.address: 9101 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: A coastal escape inside Pointe Orlando, whitewashed wood and rose on the tables, with seafood towers, a lobster roll and blackened sea bass. Guests say it gives off a fun, coastal Hampton vibe, the slot between casual and formal where a dinner feels like a pause from the show floor. It is nice but not stiff; at peak times the room gets loud, so bring the group that likes it lively.

places.name: Cuba Libre
places.address: 9101 International Dr #1004, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: A two-story Old Havana courtyard rebuilt inside Pointe Orlando, all palm shadows, live Latin music, and rum. Guests come for ropa vieja, empanadas, and pineapple guacamole, stay for the mojitos and the Cuban bread, and let dinner slide into dancing without changing rooms. On busy nights the bar and kitchen take their time, so settle in and order early.

places.name: JoJo's Shake Bar
places.address: 9101 International Dr Ste 1208, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: A retro diner at Pointe Orlando where the shakes arrive wearing their own desserts. Guests pile in for over-the-top specialty shakes, boozy shakes for the grown-ups, smash burgers, and a giant cinnamon roll, in a room full of arcade-era color built for photos. Treat one ridiculous shake as the event itself and share it around the table.

places.name: Main Event
places.address: 9101 International Dr Ste 1032, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Bowling, laser tag, billiards, a ropes course and a big arcade fill one roof at Pointe Orlando, food lane-side and a full bar for groups. Guests call it loud in the best way, a neon-lit fun factory where families and convention crews can actually do something together. If you are booking a birthday party, confirm the details in writing and check back before the day.

places.name: Madame Tussauds Orlando
places.address: 8387 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Inside ICON Park, the wax museum lets guests pose with pop stars, superheroes, sports legends and a Justice League lineup for group photos. The figures reward a close look, staff pass along fun facts as you wander, and the whole thing stays playful and hands-on. It is a brisk, air-conditioned walkthrough, so pair it with the wheel or the aquarium next door.

places.name: Hyatt Regency Orlando
places.address: 9801 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: The headquarters hotel on International Drive, tied to both convention concourses by bridges, so the show floor is a walk, not a shuttle ride. Guests praise large, comfortable rooms, warm service, and the Grotto Pool waiting behind the meeting rooms. Budget for parking and a daily resort fee, and light sleepers should ask for a room away from connecting doors.

places.name: Rosen Centre
places.address: 9840 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Rosen's flagship tower on International Drive, joined to the convention center's West Building by its own skywalk. Inside, the Everglades steakhouse and Harry's poolside bar handle hosted dinners without a car, and guests note big rooms, plenty of elevators, and staff who stay attentive through heavy show weeks. Some corners show their age and parking adds up, but the location carries it.

places.name: Rosen Plaza
places.address: 9700 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: The West Building's other skywalk hotel, crossing to Hall F by the Gary Sain Memorial Bridge, calmer and more relaxed than the flagship. A recent renovation leaves the rooms clean, simple, and modern, and guests keep using the word immaculate for everything from the lobby to the pool. Jack's Place covers steakhouse dinners on site, and Pointe Orlando's restaurants sit steps away.

places.name: Hilton Orlando
places.address: 6001 Destination Pkwy, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: A convention hotel with a resort hiding inside it, linked to the South Concourse by its own pedestrian bridge. Once the badge comes off, guests drift to the lazy river, the waterslide, and Spencer's steakhouse, and describe the whole place as immaculate, updated, and calming. It works as well for families as for attendee groups, which is why the convention crowd keeps coming back to it.

places.name: bartaco
places.address: 7600 Dr Phillips Blvd Ste 28, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: A beachy patio spot in the Marketplace at Dr Phillips, where street-style tacos land on trays and the table grazes at its own pace. Guests rave about the pork belly taco, the Baja fish, and margaritas with real heat. The tacos are street-sized by design, so order a spread and expect the small plates to add up.

places.name: Le Café de Paris
places.address: 5170 Dr Phillips Blvd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: A family-run French cafe holding down the quiet end of Dr Phillips, cozy and unhurried. Guests face a near-impossible choice at the pastry case: made-to-order crepes, huge madeleines, Croque Madame, and Quiche Lorraine around locally roasted coffee. It is the neighborhood's slow breakfast and long conversation, the kind of place regulars would rather keep to themselves.

places.name: Norman's Orlando
places.address: 7924 Via Dellagio Way, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Norman Van Aken's flagship at Dellagio, where New World cooking fuses Florida, the Caribbean, and Latin America. Guests single out the yuca-stuffed crispy shrimp, the blue crab beignets, and a key lime pie they warn you not to skip. The pacing runs leisurely, so treat dinner as the whole evening and let it unfold.

places.name: Dragonfly Robata Grill & Sushi
places.address: 7972 Via Dellagio Way, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Skewers cook over binchotan charcoal at this Dellagio robata grill, and the sushi bar keeps up with rolls like the Big Boss. Guests call it a cool, polished room with a quieter date-night rhythm than the steakhouse row around it. Order a spread of small plates and let the table share its way through the fire and the raw bar.

places.name: Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar
places.address: 8030 Via Dellagio Way, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: By the Dellagio fountains, Fleming's does the classic steakhouse thing right: prime cuts, a deep wine list, and sharp service. The tomahawk is the order guests name for a celebration, with a dry-aged ribeye and filet mignon behind it and a chocolate lava cake to close. Polished without being pretentious, it is the low-risk reservation on Sand Lake, the room where a business dinner or an anniversary lands exactly as planned.

places.name: Peperoncino
places.address: 7988 Via Dellagio Way Ste 108, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Tiny and homey by the Dellagio fountain, this Italian spot has guests saying it feels like Italy. House pastas, a Margherita pizza, Nonna Concetta's meatballs and chicken parmigiana carry a menu regulars call their favorite date night. The room holds very few tables, so seating runs tight and a reservation is the smart move.

places.name: Vines by H
places.address: 7533 W Sand Lake Rd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Restaurant Row's long-running wine and jazz room is back under a new name at the same Sand Lake address. Live jazz and smooth vocals set an unhurried tempo over blue crab fingers, oysters Rockefeller, lamb chops and house-made linguine bolognese, with a deep cellar behind it. Service can take its time on a busy night, so order, settle in, and let the music carry the pacing.

places.name: The Whiskey
places.address: 7563 W Sand Lake Rd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Rock and roll energy on Sand Lake, with chef-driven burgers and a bar that runs deep on whiskey. Guests rave about the Whiskey Burger, the Shroom N' Swiss and parmesan truffle fries, cooked exactly as ordered and, in one regular's words, melt in your mouth. Live music keeps the room loud in the good way, so bring the crew that wants to exhale, not the client who needs a quiet corner.

places.name: Eddie V's Prime Seafood
places.address: 7488 W Sand Lake Rd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Prime seafood and steak up front, then live trios in the V Lounge keep the night going after dinner. Guests single out the tuna tartare, Chilean sea bass, shellfish tower and bananas foster butter cake, all carried by polished, celebration-minded service. On busy nights the music can swallow the table talk, so ask for a quieter corner if the conversation matters.

places.name: Ocean Prime
places.address: 7339 W Sand Lake Rd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: White-tablecloth polish at the I-4 end of Restaurant Row, with seafood, prime steaks, a raw bar, and a dressy bar scene. The warm butter cake is the finish guests insist on, after Chilean sea bass, twin lobster tails and lobster bisque. Prices run high and a few extras, bread service among them, are charged apart, so ask what is included and the evening stays as smooth as the service.

places.name: Ruth's Chris Steak House
places.address: 7501 W Sand Lake Rd, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: The familiar name on Restaurant Row, recently remodeled and still doing the sizzling-platter ritual exactly to spec. Filets and ribeyes arrive sizzling hot, with lobster mac and cheese and lobster bisque in support and service guests call impeccable. It is the no-surprises client dinner; just order your steak a degree under your usual, since the kitchen occasionally sends one past the mark.

places.name: Disney Character Warehouse
places.address: 4969 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Disney's own closeout store inside the International Premium Outlets, where cleared park merchandise lands at outlet prices. Loungefly backpacks, spirit jerseys, pins and ear headbands turn over constantly, and shoppers describe it as thrifting with better odds: you will strike gold, but not always. On busy days a virtual queue meters the door and the room packs in, so treat it as a destination, not a quick stop.

places.name: Ford's Garage
places.address: 4971 International Dr Ste 3D.09, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: A burger bar dressed as a 1920s service station at the outlets, with vintage Fords overhead and shop rags for napkins. The burgers are huge, from the Signature and Estate to a brisket burnt ends melt and Firestone shrimp, and guests praise the hospitality as much as the food. It is the sit-down refuel the outlet day actually deserves, a room kids read as an attraction on its own.

places.name: Ford's Garage
places.address: 8201 Vineland Ave Ste 1801, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: Inside Vineland Premium Outlets, this vintage garage room has classic cars, shop-rag napkins in hose-clamp rings, and tire sinks. The menu runs broad, anchored by Black Angus burgers, a tower of jumbo onion rings, fried pickles and a colossal chocolate cake, with a strong beer selection at the bar. Guests praise the fun atmosphere, but service can crawl when the room fills and an automatic service fee lands on every check, with a tip still expected on top.

places.name: Orlando Outlet Marketplace
places.address: 5269 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: The quieter outlet run on north I-Drive is a smaller open-air center anchored by Nike Clearance, with Levi's and Adidas behind it. Guests come for last-chance clearance and easy parking, in a center that stays uncrowded next to the mega-outlets down the road. It will not fill a whole day, and that is the appeal: a targeted bargain mission, done well.

places.name: Hash House A Go Go
places.address: 5350 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: Twisted farm food in huge portions, just a short hop from the north I-Drive outlets. Sage fried chicken Benedicts, a chicken and waffles tower, churro waffles and hubcap pancakes arrive massive and creative, and one guest's verdict sums it up: come hungry and leave with your next meal. The room stays busy and waits can stretch at peak, so order to share and let breakfast become the main event.

places.name: Lake Buena Vista Factory Stores
places.address: 15657 S Apopka Vineland Rd, Orlando, FL 32821
places.description: Near Disney on SR 535, this compact open-air outlet center keeps things low-stress with Nike, Gap, and Tommy Hilfiger. Guests call it smaller than the other outlets with better deals to be had, and the surface parking is plentiful instead of a garage battle. It is the outlet run sized for families who want the bargains without the production.

places.name: Hollerbach's Willow Tree Cafe
places.address: 205 E 1st St, Sanford, FL 32771
places.description: On East 1st Street in Sanford since 2001, this festive German room is communal, lively, and has a roof terrace. The kitchen leans on schnitzel, wurst, and potato pancakes, with pretzel and beer cheese, eisbein pork shank, apple strudel, and Black Forest cake rounding out the table. Guests call it worth the drive, and the extensive gluten free menu gets specific praise from diners who need it.

places.name: Columbia Restaurant
places.address: 649 Front St, Celebration, FL 34747
places.description: On Front Street in Celebration, this lakeside sister to the 1905 Ybor City original brings old Florida with hand-painted tiles. The Original 1905 Salad is prepared tableside and guests call it to die for, the sangria is mixed at the table too, and the Paella a la Valenciana anchors the menu alongside empanadas and roast pork. Finish with the white chocolate bread pudding in a room that stays festive and lively.

places.name: Celebration Town Tavern
places.address: 721 Front St, Celebration, FL 34747
places.description: Across from the lake on Front Street sits a cozy little slice of New England in the middle of Celebration. Guests swear by the clam chowder, calling it some of the best they have ever had, alongside a Maine lobster roll, fried clams, steamers and fish and chips. Finish with Boston cream pie that regulars call wicked good, and the whole room feels like a little trip to Boston.

places.name: Canvas Restaurant & Market
places.address: 13615 Sachs Ave, Orlando, FL 32827
places.description: Laureate Park's lakeside table in Lake Nona is relaxed and upscale, with water views and a breezy patio. Guests call it their go-to restaurant in Lake Nona, ordering across a menu that runs from lobster eggs benedict and a toasted Cubano to whole roasted local snapper, with Nutella doughnuts and key lime cheesecake to finish. The room can run loud when it fills, but the range keeps the neighborhood loyal.

places.name: Park Pizza & Brewing Company
places.address: 6941 Lake Nona Blvd, Orlando, FL 32827
places.description: In Lake Nona Town Center, the oak-fired pies and the beer in your glass were both made just a few steps away. The Truffle Shuffle and Big Island lead the menu, the giant soft pretzel with beer cheese disappears fast, and a warm skillet cookie closes things out. The dining room runs lively and loud when it fills, so families drift to the patio facing the green.

places.name: Chroma Modern Bar + Kitchen
places.address: 6967 Lake Nona Blvd, Orlando, FL 32827
places.description: Saturated color and a lively buzz fill this Lake Nona Town Center small-plates room, built for passing dishes around. The signature move is the Parm to Table fettuccine, truffle pasta tossed in a Parmesan wheel until every strand shines, backed by whipped ricotta crostini, charred octopus, and caramelized Brussels sprouts. Guests say Chroma never disappoints, though service can stretch when the room fills, so settle in and let the plates arrive.

places.name: Bosphorous Turkish Cuisine
places.address: 6900 Tavistock Lakes Blvd, Suite 100, Orlando, FL 32827
places.description: Warm and laid-back in Lake Nona Town Center, with lavas bread landing puffed from the oven to tear and share. Kebabs come off the grill smoky at the edges, the lamb shank goes tender, and the mixed grill is built for the table, with sigara boregi, pistachio baklava, and Turkish tea to stretch the meal out. A guest who grew up in Turkey vouches for the authenticity, and regulars say the plates are made to be shared.

places.name: Nona Blue Modern Tavern
places.address: 9685 Lake Nona Village Pl, Orlando, FL 32827
places.description: Lake Nona's dressed-up tavern feels upscale but comfortable, with a big center bar and a kitchen cooking from scratch. The prime rib and pork chop carry the menu, firecracker shrimp snaps with heat, and the carrot cake is the one guests call the best in Orlando. Regulars have been coming for years and call it the neighborhood's best table, espresso martinis very much included.

places.name: Garni Café
places.address: 6100 Wave Hotel Dr, Orlando, FL 32827
places.description: Up on the Wave Hotel's second floor, a casual French bistro in a botanical room full of greenery and rattan. Croque madame and steak frites are the signatures, with executive chef Guillaume Robin running the kitchen. It replaced the hotel's earlier HAVEN Kitchen in June 2025 and kept the room's garden calm intact.

places.name: The Living Room Bar
places.address: 6100 Wave Hotel Dr, Orlando, FL 32827
places.description: The Wave Hotel's Lake Nona lounge is eclectic and art-filled, arranged around a pink dogwood tree with low chairs. The espresso martini is the drink guests rave about, one calling it the best in Orlando, and the bar pours from a deep tequila list. Small plates like charred pulpo and street corn ribs circulate while you lounge.

places.name: Don Julio Mexican Kitchen & Tequila Bar
places.address: 9776 Eagle Creek Center Blvd, Orlando, FL 32827
places.description: Festive and airy in Eagle Creek, this Mexican kitchen and tequila bar leads with the birria tacos. Guests call the guacamole the best they have had, the chicken fajitas arrive in famously generous portions, and passion fruit margaritas and ceviche keep the table bright. The room gets lively as it fills, which is part of the draw.

places.name: Maki Hibachi
places.address: 11954 Narcoossee Rd, Suite 1, Orlando, FL 32827
places.description: Tiny and intimate at Lake Nona Landing, this spot treats sushi like a craft, with fish guests call the freshest around. The tuna tataki draws the strongest language at the table, backed by the Nona roll, the sexy lobster roll, and hibachi plates with fried rice and the white sauce regulars swear by. Portions run large enough for leftovers, and a passion fruit sakitini keeps the small room lively.

places.name: Hot Taco Street Taqueria
places.address: 9680 Narcoossee Rd, Suite 103, Orlando, FL 32827
places.description: Street-style energy in Lake Nona Village: neon pink, agave murals, and patterned tile in a room guests call festive and spotless. The crunchy birria and quesabirria land crisped and cheesy, backed by elote and churros fried to order with dipping sauces. Frozen margaritas and aguas frescas keep the table cool, and regulars say it is the kind of place you genuinely want to keep coming back to.

places.name: Tomasino's Pizza
places.address: 14009 Narcoossee Rd, Suite 130, Orlando, FL 32832
places.description: Lake Nona's neighborhood slice shop is old school and family packed, with New York style pies guests call the real thing. Start with the garlicky cheese knots regulars rave about, then the Mama's Moo-za-relll or the Don Tomasino, with meatball sliders and mac and cheese fries for the table. The pies run rich and unapologetically cheesy, and a slice of Junior's cheesecake closes the meal.

places.name: Pho Haven
places.address: 14019 Narcoossee Rd, Suite 105, Orlando, FL 32832
places.description: Cozy and spotless on Narcoossee Road, where the broth comes clean and comforting, fragrant with star anise. The house special stacks rare steak, brisket, flank and meatballs, the short rib and oxtail bowls run richer, and bun bo hue brings real heat, with crackly banh mi, herbal summer rolls and sweet, strong Vietnamese iced coffee alongside. Portions can vary between visits, but regulars keep coming back and call it their haven.

places.name: Pisco Express
places.address: 9717 Eagle Creek Center Blvd, Suite 100, Orlando, FL 32832
places.description: Peruvian cooking at counter speed inside Eagle Creek Center, and guests keep adding it to the rotation. Ceviche clasico lands bright with lime, lomo saltado sizzles with the fries folded in, and arroz chaufa, anticuchos and causa round out a menu that punches above its fast casual format. The pisco sour and chicha morada finish it, and more than one guest swears the steak melts in your mouth.

places.name: BaBbi BaBbi Korean Kitchen
places.address: 10799 Moss Park Rd, Suite 102, Orlando, FL 32832
places.description: Bright and fast casual at the Shoppes at East Park Village, where K-pop energy meets sizzling stone pots. Bibimbap arrives ready to mix, its rice crisping under bulgogi, vegetables and egg, while bulgogi kimbap, Korean corn dogs with a real cheese pull and chewy tteokbokki in spicy sauce fill out the table. Soondubu and bomb fries keep the comfort coming.

places.name: Green Meadows Petting Farm
places.address: 1881 Jack Calhoun Dr, Kissimmee, FL 34741
places.description: Under the live oaks at Lancaster Ranch Park in Kissimmee, this petting farm is all open air and hands-on. Kids feed goats, alpacas, donkeys and pigs, climb into the corn pit, and ride out on a tractor-drawn wagon through Old Florida pasture. Guests call it the most screen free and special time, the kind of peaceful place where little ones just run and burn off energy.

places.name: The Lucky Lure
places.address: The Lucky Lure, 1427 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32804
places.description: On the Lake Ivanhoe shore, an open-air dive guests call their best local watering hole. The full bar pours a wide run of beers and seltzers, with pool and foosball keeping the casual, dog friendly room loose. It is unpretentious and easy, the kind of place people settle into by the water.

places.name: Leiah
places.address: Leiah, 409 N Magnolia Ave, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: Small and candlelit on Magnolia Avenue, where guests say the service makes them feel like the only diners there. The tasting menu moves through lobster bisque guests call the best they have had, handmade truffle tortellini, wagyu potato foam and beet salad, with wine pairings matched course by course. It feels intimate and unhurried, a special occasion spot that finishes with mango brulee.

places.name: The Tavern Bar & Tacos
places.address: The Tavern Bar & Tacos, 75 E Colonial Dr, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: It calls itself a vibe bar and guests back it up, starting with birria tacos one regular said should be criminal. Dart boards, TVs and chess boards fill the room, portions run generous, and the prices stay easy. It is a laid-back neighborhood hangout on Colonial Drive with divey edges and tacos guests call absolutely fire.

places.name: Gravity Taproom
places.address: Gravity Taproom, 777 N Orange Ave, Suite D, Orlando, FL 32801
places.description: A welcoming North Quarter hangout where rotating craft taps pour beside brick-fired Neapolitan pies. The Not So Classic Margherita, the Pro Figure pizza, Trial Wings and a giant Bavarian pretzel with beer cheese give the food real weight, and a cheesecake flight finishes the table. The pours run premium, but guests say the ever-changing selection keeps regulars coming back, dog in tow on the patio.

places.name: The Caboose Bar
places.address: The Caboose Bar, 1827 N Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32804
places.description: A dive on N Orange Ave in Ivanhoe Village where guests say the bartenders make you feel like a regular. The kitchen turns out Caboose Wings guests have called the best wings in Orlando, plus fully loaded tots, mozzarella sticks and boiled peanuts. The vibe stays chill and welcoming, with regulars who treat newcomers like family.

places.name: Sixty South Restaurant and Lounge
places.address: Sixty South Restaurant and Lounge, 60 S Ivanhoe Blvd, Orlando, FL 32804
places.description: Inside the DoubleTree on Ivanhoe Boulevard, a spacious, polished lounge with lots of room to meet and talk. Guests single out the wings, cooked to perfection, plus grilled mahi mahi, Siesta Key fish tacos and fried mushroom ravioli. A DoubleTree Cookie Martini closes things out in a relaxed room that suits hotel guests and downtown locals alike.

places.name: Santiago's Bodega
places.address: Santiago's Bodega, 802 Virginia Dr, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Lively and eclectic on Virginia Drive, a tapas room built for sharing plates out on the patio. Guests linger over miso crusted short ribs, beef carpaccio, saganaki, patatas bravas and yellowfin tuna ceviche, with red sangria poured in huge glasses. Regulars call it one of the best spots in Orlando for food and service that feels impeccable.

places.name: Colorado Fondue Company
places.address: Colorado Fondue Company, 1016 Semoran Blvd, Casselberry, FL 32707
places.description: Dressed like a Colorado ski lodge, this Casselberry room has timber, stone, and cozy booths built for lingering over a pot. Cheese fondues like the Muenster Mash start the night, mains grill on a hot rock at the table, and a Blizzard Turtle or Bailey's salted chocolate fondue finishes it. Guests call it romantic and festive, and better value than the big fondue chains; on busy nights the room gets loud and the courses take their time.

places.name: Paddy's Pub Longwood
places.address: Paddy's Pub Longwood, 995 W State Rd 434, Longwood, FL 32750
places.description: Longwood's no-frills neighborhood sports pub, with Diamond pool tables, dart boards, and TVs on the games. Regulars come for the wings, Flanagan's cheese fries and the Flanagan's Special burger, and for pool and dart tournaments that keep the room competitive. The staff is friendly, the service quick, and guests say they always meet the best people here.

places.name: Ain't Miss Behavin' Sports and Tiki Bar
places.address: Ain't Miss Behavin' Sports and Tiki Bar, 1550 FL-436, Winter Park, FL 32792
places.description: Cozy and hole-in-the-wall on FL-436, this sports and tiki bar keeps a local crowd where everybody is welcome. The sliders get singled out as on point, backed by wings, buffalo chicken egg rolls, margarita flights and beer buckets built for groups. Karaoke, pool tournaments and the back tiki bar keep the room busy.

places.name: Debbies Bar
places.address: Debbies Bar, 1490 FL-436, Casselberry, FL 32707
places.description: Debbies is a classic Casselberry dive on Semoran Boulevard, a small, old-school full liquor bar where the atmosphere stays fun and relaxing. Pool tables, poker games and Jell-O shots fill the room, the bartenders are awesome, and the prices feel like another era. Guests love the small bar feel, the fun crowd, and a night that is never boring.

places.name: Lucky China
places.address: Lucky China, 6756 Aloma Ave, Winter Park, FL 32792
places.description: A no-frills takeout staple in Aloma Square that regulars prize for one thing above all: consistency. House Special Lo Mein, Mongolian Beef, sweet and sour chicken and crackly crab rangoon arrive hot in generous portions, and guests say they have never had a bad plate. It is bang-for-your-buck neighborhood Chinese, the kind of order you stop deliberating over and simply repeat.

places.name: Thai Place
places.address: Thai Place, 501 N Orlando Ave Ste 319, Winter Park, FL 32789
places.description: Family-run since 1999, this calm, cozy Winter Park Village room is where longtime regulars bring everyone they love. The cooking aims for the balance guests call the perfect blend of spice, sweet and savory: drunken noodles, Panang and green curries that melt into the jasmine rice, Tom Kha Gai and crisp fried potstickers. A lychee martini or mango sticky rice finishes things in the same unhurried register.

places.name: Boardwalk Pizza
places.address: Boardwalk Pizza, 5419 Lake Howell Rd, Winter Park, FL 32792
places.description: Jersey shore, old-school pizzeria feel comes to Lake Howell Road, with an open kitchen and a small-town welcome. The thin crust pies come whole or by the slice, and regulars point to the Great White, the garlic knots and a Philly cheesesteak they argue is the best in Orlando. Gluten-free pizza and a cannoli at the counter keep the whole family in the game.

places.name: Asia Kitchen
places.address: Asia Kitchen, 5405 Lake Howell Rd, Winter Park, FL 32792
places.description: Bright and spotless on Lake Howell Road, a neighborhood staple where you might get fresh wontons while you wait. The boba tea gets the loudest love, backed by orange chicken, chicken lo mein, crab rangoon and pillowy bao. Prices land gentle, the welcome is warm, and it has a way of becoming a regular go-to.

places.name: Toasted
places.address: Toasted, 1945 Aloma Ave, Winter Park, FL 32792
places.description: Everything here starts with grilled cheese, artisan bread pressed crisp around fillings like the Fig and Goat. The Death by Truffle and the Mac Attack go full comfort, with truffle fries and tomato soup made for dunking on the side. It stays super chill and easy on the wallet, with gluten-free and vegan options that hold their own.

places.name: Maya Cafe Lounge & Gallery
places.address: Maya Cafe Lounge & Gallery, 1980 Howell Branch Rd, Winter Park, FL 32792
places.description: You spot it early: a hot pink building on Howell Branch Road, walls covered in art from the family who run it. The kitchen leans warm and eclectic, with a Cuban sandwich, steak tacos, the Maya Burger and an eggplant dip guests keep talking about. Add a Maya Latte or fresh juice, and the cozy, colorful room makes newcomers feel like regulars.

places.name: Oodle Ramen & More
places.address: Oodle Ramen & More, 5812 Conroy Rd, Orlando, FL 32835
places.description: Playful and anime-touched on Conroy Road, with a warm, sleek room inside. The Spicy Tonkotsu is the bowl regulars swear by, with silky broth and what one guest called the most perfect ontama egg, and the Tan Tan wins first-timers over. Beyond the noodles, the omurice is a whole experience and the Wagyu Beef Don is a must, with takoyaki to start.

places.name: Bar One Orlando
places.address: Bar One Orlando, 1516 McCoy Rd, Orlando, FL 32809
places.description: Tiny from the street, but inside a cozy, very clean neighborhood bar on McCoy Road with pool and darts. The patio is the charmer, with picnic tables, cornhole, giant Jenga and a warm fire pit under the string lights. Order the wings (guests swear you will order another round), the Venezuelan empanadas and tequenos, and expect bartenders who remember you and your drink.

places.name: Murphy's Pub Orlando
places.address: Murphy's Pub Orlando, 6582 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: I-Drive's friendly British-style soccer pub, where any shirt is welcome and expats treat it as home. The Guinness pour comes properly, the screens carry Premier League football, and the kitchen turns out fish and chips, steak and ale pie, shepherd's pie and the Boomin' Reuben. Guests call the atmosphere amazing and the welcome genuine, with pool, darts and a dog-friendly patio rounding out the local feel.

places.name: Rum Jungle
places.address: Rum Jungle, 5533 International Dr, Orlando, FL 32819
places.description: I-Drive's Caribbean concert hall is loud and dance-floor driven, powered by soca, dancehall, reggae, and hip hop. Behind the bar stands a wall of rum, and the Orlando Sunset is the signature pour. Covers and parking add to the night's cost, but guests who come for reggae call it the place to be.

places.name: Todd English's bluezoo
places.address: Todd English's bluezoo, 1500 Epcot Resorts Blvd, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
places.description: At the Dolphin, seafood arrives in an underwater glow of blue glass and soft light, polished and romantic. The raw bar opens the night, then the signature dancing fish arrives grilled whole, alongside Cantonese-style lobster, branzino with crisp skin and crab nachos. Guests call the service and food top notch and the whole experience spot on, with the Burnt Orange and Zooberry pouring in the lounge for those who linger; just know the check runs high, even by resort standards.

places.name: Vanbarry's Public House
places.address: Vanbarry's Public House, 4120 S Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32806
places.description: On South Orange Avenue in SoDo, it starts with house pickles on the table and a covered patio facing Lake Jennie Jewel. Guests settle into relaxed, chill vibes with the Bare Naked Burger, Boomin' Shrimp Tacos, Fig and the Pig flatbread and bacon caramel fries, plus table side s'mores around the fire pit. Board games, dogs on the patio and kids at the table keep it feeling like a local hangout, even when service stretches at peak crowd.

places.name: The Porch South Orange
places.address: The Porch South Orange, 4757 S Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32806
places.description: Front porch energy on South Orange Avenue, in a welcoming neighborhood room guests choose over touristy spots. The Southern Mama Jama burger stacks pimento cheese, house bacon jam and crispy onions, while blackened grouper tacos, shrimp and grits and Porch Tenders keep the menu Southern and hearty. A wedge salad with regular fans and a patio built for game day crowds round out the draw.

places.name: Formaggio and Friends
places.address: Formaggio and Friends, 4745 S Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32806
places.description: Cozy in SoDo, an Italian grocery and wine bar where cheese cases, pantry shelves, and a communal table share one room. Guests urge each other to run for the mortadella sandwich and call the crab cakes the best in town, alongside the TomaRashi board and hand pulled bocconcini and burrata. Hosts pour tastings with knowledgeable guidance, keeping the feel closer to a neighborhood hangout than a shop.

places.name: Cecil's Texas Style Bar-B-Q
places.address: Cecil's Texas Style Bar-B-Q, 2800 S Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32806
places.description: Cafeteria style since 1992 on South Orange Avenue, an old-school roadhouse where trays move down a fast, friendly line. Brisket is hand sliced to order alongside ribs, pulled pork and hot links smoked over hickory, with jalapeno mashed potatoes, collard greens and sweet potato souffle piled on as sides. Guests talk up huge portions and value for the price, and the free self serve soft serve closes the tray on a sweet note.

places.name: 4 Rivers Smokehouse
places.address: 4 Rivers Smokehouse, 3200 S Orange Ave, Orlando, FL 32806
places.description: On South Orange Avenue, Signature Angus brisket guests call A+, alongside burnt ends, the Messy Pig, and the Texas Destroyer. Portions run generous, with jalapeño cornbread, homestyle sides, and Crispy Cream Bread Pudding from the bakery case. The line moves fast past the trays, and the outdoor pavilion gives families room to spread out for a full feast.

places.name: 4 Rivers Smokehouse
places.address: 4 Rivers Smokehouse, 11764 University Blvd, Orlando, FL 32817
places.description: The UCF outpost on University Boulevard feeds Knights fans and east Orlando families the full smokehouse lineup. Burnt ends come out of this world, the Signature Angus brisket and pulled chicken get cooked to perfection, and trays fill out with mac and cheese and collard greens. The line moves fast, the room gets game-day loud, and the bread pudding made with Krispy Kreme donuts handles dessert.

places.name: Audubon Park Community Market
places.address: 1842 E Winter Park Rd, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: Every Monday evening since 2009, the Stardust parking lot fills with Florida growers, ranchers, fishermen, and makers. Everything on the tables was grown, raised, caught or made in Florida: just picked produce, fresh seafood, prepared meals, baked goods and handmade crafts. Neighbors graze from stall to stall while local musicians play, and the gathering feels like the neighborhood's weekly front porch.

places.name: Bachata Breeze Restaurant
places.address: 5773 Curry Ford Rd, Orlando, FL 32822
places.description: On Curry Ford Road, a Dominican buffet and full menu by day, then live Latin music and dancing after dark. The Picadera Bachata loads the table with fried chicken, carne frita, tostones, mofongo balls, queso frito, longaniza and salami, and plates like mofongo con camarones, churrasco and sancocho carry the meal from there. Guests talk about the music and the drinks as much as the food, and the full bar keeps the night moving.

places.name: El Colmadon
places.address: 743 N Magnolia Ave, Orlando, FL 32803
places.description: A Dominican counter on North Magnolia named for the colmadón, the corner store back home that feeds the whole block. The chopped cheese gets chopped on the grill and finished with the house Colmadon sauce, the pastelón version layers in maduros and mozzarella, and the fritura piles pica pollo, fried salami, tostones and queso frito onto one plate. Regulars call it their favorite Dominican food in the city, and the chimi de res is the order that wins over first-timers.

places.name: El Bloque 407
places.address: 730 W Sand Lake Rd, Unit 30, Orlando, FL 32809
places.description: A corner of Sherman Avenue transplanted to Sand Lake Road, with the same griddle, recipes, and people from Upper Manhattan. The chopped cheese is the headline, chopped on the flattop and pressed into a roll, and Dominican bodega food fills the rest of the counter, from yaroa to the tres golpes pizza. It runs late every night, the way a bodega should.

places.name: Nuno's Cafe
places.address: 12001 Avalon Lake Drive Suite G, Orlando, FL 32828
places.description: A family-run breakfast and lunch room with a Jersey diner accent and Portuguese and Italian roots. The corned beef hash and berry-stuffed French toast are the orders regulars defend, and a complimentary round of sweet dough croquettes lands like a house handshake. It is the sit-down breakfast Avalon Park was missing.

places.name: Café Coquí
places.address: 3819 Avalon Park East Blvd, Orlando, FL 32828
places.description: A Puerto Rican bakery built for the morning line, with quesitos, flan de queso, tres leches, and coffee flights. Saturdays draw a crowd that treats the case like a checklist. The pineapple coconut French toast is the sleeper order.

places.name: The Bakery Colombian Cafe
places.address: 13001 Founders Square Dr, Orlando, FL 32828
places.description: A Colombian family bakery where warm pandebono and fresh buñuelos set the tone right away. Arepas come with eggs pericos, beef empanadas stay crisp, and the case runs from almond croissants to tres leches. A proper neighborhood anchor for Founders Square.

places.name: Bowigens Beer Company
places.address: 3801 Avalon Park East Blvd #120, Orlando, FL 32828
places.description: The Avalon Park outpost of the Casselberry-born brewery runs a 6,000 square foot indoor-outdoor taproom inside the Marketplace hall. Twenty-plus house beers pour at once, anchored by the 407 Pils and an Avalon Park Amber, with rotating sours and stouts for the regulars. The dog-friendly patio makes it the hall's easiest hang.

places.name: Cheese To Share
places.address: 3801 Avalon Park East Blvd Ste. 150, Orlando, FL 32828
places.description: Inside the Marketplace hall, a modern European cheese room with fondue, loaded boards, and brie toast. It is the hall's built-in date night, wine in hand and nowhere to rush off to.

places.name: The Humble Crumb
places.address: 3801 Avalon Park East Blvd Ste. 140, Orlando, FL 32828
places.description: A small bakery counter inside the Marketplace hall turning out pastries and cakes for the neighborhood. It works best as the sweet stop on an Avalon Park wander: something from the case, coffee in hand, back out to the square.

places.name: Vespr Coffeebar
places.address: 626 N Alafaya Trl, Orlando, FL 32826
places.description: A specialty coffee room on the Alafaya corridor with a quiet, laptop-friendly hum UCF students found fast. The honey pot iced latte and fresh chai lead, with seasonal matcha and homemade pastries behind them. Avocado toast covers the light-lunch angle.

places.name: Jacob's Cafe & Restaurant
places.address: 12789 Waterford Lakes Pkwy, Orlando, FL 32828
places.description: A Turkish cafe doing the full spread: a proper Turkish breakfast plate, house gelato, and ribeye steak bowls. Strawberry matcha and sweet cream cold brew keep the drinks interesting. It reads family-run because it is.

places.name: Super Recipes Cafe
places.address: 815 N Alafaya Trl, Orlando, FL 32828
places.description: A Korean home-style counter tucked inside the LA Fitness on Alafaya, open to anyone who walks in. Kimbap, buldak ramen and marinated beef plates come cooked to order, with smoothies on the side. The gym setting is the only hurdle, and regulars clear it without thinking.

places.name: Dixie Cream Cafe
places.address: 434 Main St, Windermere, FL 34786
places.description: An independently owned Main Street room with 1950s diner warmth and a from-scratch Southern kitchen. Smoked brisket hash, Bananas Foster French toast and biscuits under sausage gravy run the morning. The dog-friendly patio keeps it a neighborhood ritual.

places.name: Windermere Brewing Company
places.address: 111 W 5th Ave, Windermere, FL 34786
places.description: Windermere's hometown brewery, a block off Main Street with a dog-friendly backyard and rotating food trucks. The Watermann helles and Orange Grove Outlaw IPA pour beside a peach wheat called Party Boat. Trivia and bingo nights give the week a rhythm.

places.name: Fresco Pizzeria
places.address: 527 Main St, Windermere, FL 34786
places.description: A wood-fired pizzeria from the Scialoia family, whose Dr. Phillips Italian kitchens go back to 2006. Pies come off 48-hour dough with blistered edges, and the handmade pastas hold their own against them. Main Street's family dinner anchor.

places.name: Windermere Farmers Market
places.address: 520 Main St, Windermere, FL 34786
places.description: Every Friday, Town Square Park fills with a small hometown market: fresh produce, seafood, breads, local honey, and plants. Live music drifts over the brick street and leashed dogs are part of the crowd; pairing it with coffee at Paloma down the block is the local routine.

places.name: Tim's Wine Market
places.address: 428 Main St, Windermere, FL 34786
places.description: The Windermere storefront of Orlando's long-running independent wine shop, with siblings on Orange Avenue and in Sanford. Small-producer bottles are the point, and the staff teach as they pour. On Fridays the Wine Down pours free tastes for whoever wanders in.

places.name: Bella Tuscany
places.address: 13424 Summerport Village Pkwy, Windermere, FL 34786
places.description: A family-owned Tuscan room in Summerport with a wine list past 700 bottles and Wine Spectator recognition. Beef carpaccio and a lobster and pumpkin risotto served in the pumpkin itself lead the menu, with chicken parm for the traditionalists. The patio keeps date night outside when the weather behaves.

places.name: Kelly's Homemade Ice Cream
places.address: 14387 Bridgewater Crossings Blvd, Windermere, FL 34786
places.description: The Windermere scoop shop of the Orlando-born ice cream maker that started in Audubon Park. Small-batch flavors rotate through salted caramel Oreo, PB&J potato chip and guava cheese, and flights exist for the undecided. A Summerport evening ritual in the making.

places.name: Zackleys
places.address: 3260 University Blvd, Winter Park, FL 32792
places.description: Family owned since 2000 and tucked inside the Full Sail campus, with wood oven pizzas, paninis, and Jamaican beef empanadas. It is the rare campus food spot that has outlasted the buildings around it, and the Nutella pizza has a quiet following with students between sessions.

places.name: Aloma Bowl
places.address: 2530 Aloma Ave, Winter Park, FL 32792
places.description: A 32-lane bowling house on Aloma Ave run by a local family group that has operated Central Florida lanes for decades. Between games there is an arcade, billiards, and the Brooklyn South bar and grill inside, which makes it an easy group night that never needs a plan B.

places.name: Alexandria Market
places.address: 6148 Hanging Moss Rd, Orlando, FL 32814
places.description: A Middle Eastern grocery on Hanging Moss Rd stocking halal meats, fresh fateer and pita, baklava, and za'atar. For international students cooking food from home, this is the deepest bench of ingredients anywhere near Full Sail.

places.name: Pereira Latin Products
places.address: 2914 Forsyth Rd, Winter Park, FL 32792
places.description: A Latin grocery on Forsyth Rd carrying the pantry staples, snacks, and drinks the big supermarkets skim past. It is small, practical, and close to campus: the stop for students who want ingredients that taste like home without a cross-town drive.

places.name: Vivahealthy Pink House
places.address: 7612 University Blvd Unit 21, Winter Park, FL 32792
places.description: A bright healthy cafe on University Blvd built around smoothies, juices, salads, and weekly meal prep for students. The pink house branding is not subtle, and neither is the point: food that leaves you able to study afterward.

places.name: Aladdin Cafe
places.address: Aladdin Cafe, 1015 FL-436, Casselberry, FL 32707
places.description: A family owned Lebanese kitchen on Semoran Blvd, 100 percent halal, dough hand-stretched daily and eggplants charred over flame. Shawarma, falafel, baked kibbi, and lamb shank with biryani rice carry the menu, and a pistachio tres leches cake closes it.

places.name: An Vi Vietnamese Kitchen & Sandwich
places.address: An Vi Vietnamese Kitchen & Sandwich, 1052 FL-436, Casselberry, FL 32707
places.description: House-made bone broth pho, fresh rolls, banh mi, vermicelli bowls, and Cajun fried rice with catfish at this bright Semoran Blvd kitchen.

places.name: Bagel King Casselberry
places.address: Bagel King Casselberry, 1455 Semoran Blvd, Suite 113, Casselberry, FL 32707
places.description: The Bagel King family's retail cafe, serving New York style kettle-baked bagels made fresh daily for breakfast and lunch. Challah French toast, biscuits and gravy, and an everything bagel bacon egg and cheese lead the favorites.

places.name: Boba Garden
places.address: Boba Garden, 1184 E State Rd 434, Winter Springs, FL 32708
places.description: A family owned bubble tea cafe in Town Center, pouring made-to-order milk and fruit teas, with board games in a nature-inspired room. The blue cheese foam is the signature, over Thai tea, taro, and Kagoshima matcha lattes.

places.name: Bowigens Beer Company
places.address: Bowigens Beer Company, 1014 FL-436, Casselberry, FL 32707
places.description: The original Bowigens taproom, pouring since 2015 on Semoran Blvd, with 25-plus taps, a pilot brewhouse, and a full kitchen. The 7 Layer Stout has won national awards, and the room still runs like a neighborhood hangout started by two musician friends.

places.name: Brightlight Books
places.address: Brightlight Books, 161 E SR 436, Fern Park, FL 32730
places.description: A family run used bookstore in Fern Park, buying, selling, and trading since 1995, with about 200,000 books across 7,000 square feet. One of the largest theology collections in the Southeast gives it a depth most used shops never reach.

places.name: Casselberry Art House
places.address: Casselberry Art House, 127 Quail Pond Circle, Casselberry, FL 32707
places.description: The city's art house since 2002, a former lake house on Lake Concord turned gallery and classroom with rotating exhibitions. The Sculpture House next door covers 3D and installation work, and festival nights open every gallery in the park at once.

places.name: Central Winds Park
places.address: Central Winds Park, 1000 Central Winds Dr, Winter Springs, FL 32708
places.description: The city's sports and festival hub on about 100 acres, with ball fields, fishing, a three-story playground, and a dog park. The Cross Seminole Trail runs through it, and each January it hosts the Central Florida Scottish Highland Games, the largest community event in Seminole County.

places.name: The Cuban Sandwich Cafe
places.address: The Cuban Sandwich Cafe, 140 W State Rd 434, Winter Springs, FL 32708
places.description: A small breakfast and lunch cafe on west 434, opened in 2025 by a veteran local Cuban restaurateur and scaled down on purpose. Cubanos, ham croquettes, bistec empanizado, and carne con papas, with pastries, smoothies, and coffee.

places.name: Cubans On The Run
places.address: Cubans On The Run, 2956 S US 17-92, Casselberry, FL 32707
places.description: A small mom-and-pop Cuban counter on 17-92 where the owner greets regulars by name. The Cuban sandwich, ropa vieja, chimichurri steak, and papa rellena anchor a menu that runs deep for its size, from caldo gallego to tres leches, all at low prices.

places.name: Greek Eatery
places.address: Greek Eatery, 1188 E State Rd 434, Winter Springs, FL 32708
places.description: A family owned Greek kitchen in the Town Center for more than 15 years, turning out gyros, souvlaki, pastitsio, and moussaka. Reviewers call the gyros the best they have had, and the room runs on dine in, takeout, and delivery.

places.name: Khaos Sports Bar and Grill
places.address: Khaos Sports Bar and Grill, 178 W State Rd 434, Winter Springs, FL 32708
places.description: A lively dive sports hub on west 434 that expanded in 2026 with a new kitchen, more pool tables, and a smoke-free interior. Wings are the draw, with darts, karaoke, and domestic beer buckets on game day.

places.name: Kiko Japanese Cuisine
places.address: Kiko Japanese Cuisine, 5661 Red Bug Lake Rd, Winter Springs, FL 32708
places.description: On Red Bug Lake Rd since 2023, this neighborhood sushi spot won fans fast with fresh sashimi, inventive rolls, and vegan options. The sushi and sashimi boat and surf and turf ramen show the range.

places.name: Lake Concord Park
places.address: Lake Concord Park, 95 Triplet Lake Drive, Casselberry, FL 32707
places.description: Casselberry's event front yard since 2010: a lakefront park with old oaks, an amphitheater, a sculpture garden, and a playground. Second Friday food truck nights and art festivals keep it busy, and most events are free.

places.name: Napoli's Pizza & Italian Restaurant
places.address: Napoli's Pizza & Italian Restaurant, 122 W State Rd 434, Winter Springs, FL 32708
places.description: A simple family pizzeria on west 434, with garlic knots, baked mussels, and eggplant Campania beside the pies. Chicken parmesan, piccata, and marsala round out a menu that punches past its price.

places.name: Original Anthony's NY Pizza
places.address: Original Anthony's NY Pizza, 1455 FL-436, Suite 105, Casselberry, FL 32707
places.description: The self-declared original Anthony's, slinging New York style pies since 1987 for Casselberry, Winter Park, and Maitland. The 18 inch Extravaganza loads up sausage, meatballs, and pepperoni, and the menu runs to wings, subs, and chicken parm.

places.name: Poblano's Cocina Mexicana
places.address: Poblano's Cocina Mexicana, 908 FL-436, Casselberry, FL 32707
places.description: A family owned Mexican kitchen on 436 built around the poblano pepper, with chile rellenos and a full vegetarian section. Top shelf margaritas, red sangria, and a coconut mojito anchor the bar, and a private room takes group dinners.

places.name: Ristorante Positano Authentic Italian
places.address: Ristorante Positano Authentic Italian, 1168 Tree Swallow Dr, Winter Springs, FL 32708
places.description: In the Town Center, owner Salvatore greets guests personally in a cozy, family-like Italian room. Campania pizza, fettuccine alla panna, chicken piccata, and carbonara anchor the menu, with tiramisu to finish.

places.name: Secret Lake Park
places.address: Secret Lake Park, 200 N Triplet Lake Drive, Casselberry, FL 32707
places.description: A quiet park of about 40 acres around three connected lakes, with a boardwalk loop, kayak access, and pavilions. It is the calm counterpart to Lake Concord's event energy, good for a shaded walk and a wood stork sighting.

places.name: Semoran Skateway
places.address: Semoran Skateway, 2670 Cassel Creek Blvd, Casselberry, FL 32707
places.description: Family owned since 1978, the roller rink generations of Casselberry kids grew up in, now with lessons and adult rhythm nights. Parents skating the same maple floor they skated as kids is the whole story here.

places.name: Senor Tequila Mexican Grill
places.address: Senor Tequila Mexican Grill, 855 E State Rd 434, Winter Springs, FL 32708
places.description: A spacious, family friendly Mexican grill in the Villaggio plaza on 434, with a big local following in Winter Springs. Carne asada, molcajete, fajitas, and the Sangrita, a sangria and frozen margarita mashup, lead a menu with a big seafood bench.

places.name: Spill Wine Bar
places.address: Spill Wine Bar, 1196 Tree Swallow Dr, Suite 1314, Winter Springs, FL 32708
places.description: A locals-first wine bar in the Town Center, started by a local for the locals, pouring 100-plus wines and a deep craft beer list. Live music, trivia and bingo nights, flatbreads, and a patio make it Winter Springs' living room after dark.

places.name: Sushi Delight & Bowl
places.address: Sushi Delight & Bowl, 1172 Tree Swallow Dr, Winter Springs, FL 32708
places.description: A pan-Asian counter on the Tree Swallow Dr restaurant row, rolling sushi and building rice bowls to order. Spicy beef bowls, the Hama roll, and crispy pork belly make it the row's quick lunch move.

places.name: Taiwan Cafe
places.address: Taiwan Cafe, 158 W State Rd 434, Winter Springs, FL 32708
places.description: A family Chinese kitchen on west 434 doing classic stir fries, noodles, and rice plates with fresh ingredients. General Tso's, honey glazed chicken, and salt and pepper chicken lead a menu that mixes English and Chinese dish names.

places.name: Taqueria Las Cazuelas Winter Springs
places.address: Taqueria Las Cazuelas Winter Springs, 162 W State Rd 434, Winter Springs, FL 32708
places.description: Tacos, milanesa de res and pollo, chips and guacamole, and queso dip at counter prices, a second room for the East Colonial taqueria.

places.name: Velvet Brew Cafe
places.address: Velvet Brew Cafe, 3950 S US 17-92, Suite 1024, Casselberry, FL 32707
places.description: A Latin-leaning bakery cafe on 17-92 pairing smooth coffee with pan de bono, alfajores, and a pistachio croissant regulars chase. A cozy, modern room made for slow mornings and pastry runs.

places.name: Victorio's II Italian Restaurant & Pizzeria
places.address: Victorio's II Italian Restaurant & Pizzeria, 200 E State Rd 434, Winter Springs, FL 32708
places.description: Serving Winter Springs since 1989, this spot is known for Detroit style deep dish baked in Detroit pans, sauce ladled on after. Hand tossed pies, the sealed Nero Sub, and a lasagna over a pound and a half make it a family standby on 434.

places.name: Vinzo's Italian Grill & Pizzeria
places.address: Vinzo's Italian Grill & Pizzeria, 1006 FL-436, Casselberry, FL 32707
places.description: A family Italian grill running 22 years on Semoran Blvd, working from family recipes that came down from New York and New Jersey. Kickin Shrimp, chicken penne alla vodka, stromboli, and cannoli give it more range than the pizzeria name suggests.

places.name: Zocalo 436 Mexican Grill
places.address: Zocalo 436 Mexican Grill, 505 FL-436, Casselberry, FL 32707
places.description: A Mexicolombian grill and bar on 436, where birria tacos share the menu with a Burrito Paisa and a parrillada for the table. Cozy booths, a small outdoor lounge, and mango margaritas make it an easy neighborhood night.
